BURHAN:v4p392/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p392/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p392/r3.claim: Divine لعل retains its ordinary hopeful force: when a generous speaker uses it for a desired good, it implicitly promises that good, as in the call to worship for taqwa.
BURHAN:v4p392/r3.anchor: من الكريم للمخاطبين في ذلك المحبوب تعريض بالوعد

BURHAN:v4p392/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p392/r4.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة
BURHAN:v4p392/r4.claim: Malik and Abu Hanifa say that the divine law is binding, cited while explaining the inducement to reach the high rank of taqwa through faith.
BURHAN:v4p392/r4.anchor: ومن ثم قال مالك وأبو حنيفة الشرع ملزم

BURHAN:v4p392/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p392/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p392/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God's inducement is certain like a promise; al-Zarkashi sees rational Mu'tazili obligation in this and says hope-inducing wording prevents complacency.
BURHAN:v4p392/r5.anchor: وقد قال الزمخشرى وقد جاءت على سبيل الاطماع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r3.claim: Alternatively, the surah's central purpose is to establish the Book's true meaning and form: it exposes hypocrisy, calls people to worship, proves its inimitability, then teaches law and debates the People of the Book.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r3.anchor: مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.claim: The call to worship is followed by creation as proof that God deserves worship; the warning against partners follows because the creation evidence establishes that He has no partner in worship or creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p291#2/r1.anchor: إلى آخره بوصف هو دليل استحقاقه للعبادة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p563/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p563/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p563/r1.claim: Al-Harali says al-Baqara first classifies humanity, then explains God's creation of the world for them and His honor to Adam before addressing Arabs and their disputes with Israelites.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p563/r1.anchor: واستمر إلى أن بان الأمر غاية البيان فأخذ يذكر مننه سبحانه على الناس المأمورين بالعبادة

STUDYQURAN:2:20/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r2.claim: Laʿalla, rendered “that haply,” is frequent in the Quran and can also mean “that perchance” or “that someone might.”
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r2.anchor: occurs frequently in the Quran and is sometimes

STUDYQURAN:2:20/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r3.claim: Because laʿalla suggests hope or anxiety, it raises a theological problem when used of God, since those qualities are usually associated with creatures.
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r3.anchor: It can be seen to present a theological problem, as it implies anxiety or hope, qualities usually associated only with creatures.

STUDYQURAN:2:20/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r4.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r4.claim: One solution treats God's hope as tantamount to a promise, since nothing could prevent its fulfillment.
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r4.anchor: tantamount to a promise, as nothing could stand in its way (Z)

STUDYQURAN:2:20/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r5.claim: Another solution attaches the hope expressed by laʿalla to the subject of the statement rather than to God.
STUDYQURAN:2:20/r5.anchor: or that the hope is connected to the subject of the statement, not to God.

TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r1.claim: God addresses the unbelievers, hypocrites, and other accountable people, commanding humble obedience and exclusive worship of the Lord who created them, their ancestors, and even their idols; the Creator can benefit or harm, unlike idols.
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r1.anchor: وعن الآخر أنه يخادع الله والذين آمنوا بما يبدي بلسانه من قلبه: آمنا بالله واليوم الآخر

TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses worship your Lord as “unify your Lord”; al-Ṭabarī explains this as directing worship and obedience exclusively to Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r2.anchor: وكان ابن عباس فيما روي لنا عنه يقول في ذلك نظير ما قلنا فيه، غير أنه ذكر عنه أنه كان يقول في معنى: {اعبدوا ربكم} [البقرة: 21] وحدوا ربكم

TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s report says the command addresses both unbelievers and hypocrites: unify the Lord who created them and those before them.
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " قال الله: {يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم} [البقرة: 21] للفريقين جميعا من الكفار والمنافقين

TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r4.speaker: السدي، أبو مالك، أبو صالح، ابن عباس، مرة، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r4.claim: The report transmitted from al-Suddī and these authorities explains that God created the present people and those who came before them.
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره، عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي

TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r5.claim: The command is evidence against those who say God may not impose an act beyond a person’s capacity unless He first grants assistance, since He commands people He has said will not believe to worship and repent.
TAB-FULL:v1p384#2/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية من أدل دليل على فساد قول من زعم أن تكليف ما لا يطاق إلا بمعونة الله غير جائز إلا بعد إعطاء الله المكلف المعونة

TAB-FULL:v1p387/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r1.claim: Worship, obey, and devote worship to God so that you avoid His anger and become among those He is pleased with.
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r1.anchor: لتتقوه بطاعته وتوحيده وإفراده بالربوبية والعبادة

TAB-FULL:v1p387/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses لعلّكم تتقون as “that you may obey.”
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {لعلكم تتقون} [البقرة: 21] قال: لعلكم تطيعون "

TAB-FULL:v1p387/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes Mujāhid to mean that obedience and abandoning error enable people to fear their Lord.
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r3.anchor: والذي أظن أن مجاهدا أراد بقوله هذا: لعلكم أن تتقوا ربكم بطاعتكم إياه وإقلاعكم عن ضلالتكم

TAB-FULL:v1p387/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r4.claim: لعل does not express uncertainty in God; here it means “so that,” as in the poet’s example where people promise to stop fighting so the other side will stop.
TAB-FULL:v1p387/r4.anchor: ذلك على غير المعنى الذي توهمت، وإنما معنى ذلك: {اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم} [البقرة: 21] ، لتتقوه بطاعته

TAB-FULL:v3p123/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p123/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v3p123/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd explains taqwa here as avoiding killing out of fear of retaliatory qisas.
TAB-FULL:v3p123/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله " {لعلكم تتقون} [البقرة: 179] قال: لعلك تتقي أن تقتله فتقتل به "

TAB-FULL:v3p156/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p156/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p156/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the phrase as abstaining during the fast from food, drink, and sexual intercourse, which would invalidate it.
TAB-FULL:v3p156/r1.anchor: فتتقون من الطعام، والشرب، والنساء مثل ما اتقوا

TAB-FULL:v3p156/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p156/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p156/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says this means abstaining from food, drink, and women, as Christians before them abstained.
TAB-FULL:v3p156/r2.anchor: عن السدي، أما قوله: {لعلكم تتقون} [البقرة: 179] يقول «فتتقون من الطعام، والشرب، والنساء مثل ما اتقوا

TABATABAI:2:21-25/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r1.claim: After describing the guided, disbelieving, and hypocritical groups, God calls all people to worship and join the pious through the following verses.
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r1.anchor: فرع تعالى على ذلك أن دعى الناس إلى عبادته وأن يلتحقوا بالمتقين دون الكافرين والمنافقين بهذه الآيات الخمس

TABATABAI:2:21-25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r2.claim: The context makes “so that you may become pious” modify the command to worship rather than the statement that God created people, though both constructions make sense.
TABATABAI:2:21-25/r2.anchor: وهذا السياق يعطي كون قوله { لعلكم تتقون } متعلقا بقوله { اعبدوا } ، دون قوله { خلقكم } وإن كان المعنى صحيحا على كلا التقديرين

TABRISI:2:21/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r1.claim: خلق can mean an act done according to measure; creating the heavens means bringing them about according to wisdom without excess or deficiency.
TABRISI:2:21/r1.anchor: الخلق الفعل على تقدير وخلق السموات فعلها على تقدير ما تدعو إليه الحكمة

TABRISI:2:21/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r2.claim: خلق can also mean nature or temperament, while خلاق means a share.
TABRISI:2:21/r2.anchor: والخلق الطبع والخليقة الطبيعة والخلاق النصيب

TABRISI:2:21/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r3.claim: يا is the vocative particle; أي is broad and indefinite until a genus noun such as الناس specifies its addressee.
TABRISI:2:21/r3.anchor: يا حرف النداء وأي اسم مبهم يقع على أجناس كثيرة إنما يتم بأن يوصف وصفته تكون باسم الجنس

TABRISI:2:21/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r4.claim: أي is a singular definite vocative, built because it occupies the place of the address pronoun; its ending is moved to distinguish its contingent building.
TABRISI:2:21/r4.anchor: فأي منادي مفرد معرفة مبني لأنه وقع موقع حرف الخطاب وهو الكاف وإنما بني على الحركة

TABRISI:2:21/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r5.claim: الناس is nominative as the descriptor of أي; here it cannot be accusative because it is the true addressee, with أي as its linker.
TABRISI:2:21/r5.anchor: والناس مرفوع لأنه صفة لأي فتبعه على حركة لفظه ولا يجوز هنا النصب

TABRISI:2:21/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r6.claim: The required, nondeletable ها signals a renewed vocative; al-Māzinī’s allowance of an accusative descriptor is rejected because Arabic usage attests only nominative.
TABRISI:2:21/r6.anchor: وأجاز المازني في يا أيها الرجل النصب وذلك فاسد لما ذكرناه

TABRISI:2:21/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r7.claim: الذين is accusative by coordination with the pronoun in خلقكم; من قبلكم is its relative clause.
TABRISI:2:21/r7.anchor: والذين من قبلكم في موضع نصب لأنه عطف على الكاف والميم

TABRISI:2:21/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r8.claim: لعل is an accusative-taking particle like إنّ and resembles a verb; كم is its accusative noun and تتقون its nominative predicate clause.
TABRISI:2:21/r8.anchor: ولعل حرف ناصب من أخوات إن وقد ذكرنا القول في مشابهته الفعل

TABRISI:2:21/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r9.claim: The address includes all accountable people, believers and unbelievers, but excludes children and the insane.
TABRISI:2:21/r9.anchor: هذا الخطاب متوجه إلى جميع الناس مؤمنهم وكافرهم إلا من ليس بمكلف

TABRISI:2:21/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
TABRISI:2:21/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan say Qurʾānic addresses “O people” were revealed at Mecca, while “O believers” were revealed at Medina.
TABRISI:2:21/r10.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس والحسن أن ما في القرآن من:

TABRISI:2:21/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r11.claim: اعبدوا ربكم means draw near to God through worship.

TABRISI:2:21/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:21/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command to worship your Lord as a command to affirm His oneness.
TABRISI:2:21/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه قال معناه وحدوه

TABRISI:2:21/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r13.claim: God brought you into existence after nonexistence and created those before you; their blessings benefit you because yours are incomplete without those given your ancestors.
TABRISI:2:21/r13.anchor: أوجدكم بعد أن لم تكونوا موجودين وأوجد من تقدم زمانكم

TABRISI:2:21/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21/r14.claim: One reading makes taqwā the purpose of creation: worship God so that you may fear Him, as in the statement that jinn and humans were created to worship.

TABRISI:2:21#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21#2/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:21#2/r1.claim: Another gloss is “worship Him so that you may guard yourselves”; alternatively, respect divine limits and avoid what God forbade.
TABRISI:2:21#2/r1.anchor: وقيل معناه اعبدوه لتتقوا وقيل معناه لعلكم تتقون الحرمات بينكم

TABRISI:2:21#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21#2/r2.claim: لعل expresses no divine uncertainty here; as in exhortation to accept advice, it softens admonition and brings it closer to the listener.
TABRISI:2:21#2/r2.anchor: فليس أنه من ذلك على شك وإنما يريد اقبله ترشد وإنما أدخل الكلام لعل ترقيقا للموعظة

TABRISI:2:21#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21#2/r3.claim: A poem uses لعل in a pledged appeal to stop fighting, meaning “so that we stop,” not expressing doubt.
TABRISI:2:21#2/r3.anchor: وقلتم لنا كفوا الحرب لعلنا نكف ووثقتم لنا كل موثق

TABRISI:2:21#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:21#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh says لعل expresses hope addressed to hearers, as in the command to Moses and Aaron to speak gently so Pharaoh may remember or fear; God knows the outcome.
TABRISI:2:21#2/r4.anchor: وقال سيبويه: إنما وردت لفظه لعل على أنه ترج للمخاطبين

TABRISI:2:21#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21#2/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:21#2/r5.claim: One proposed wisdom is to keep servants from feeling secure or self-satisfied about their deeds, making them increasingly diligent and wary of neglect.
TABRISI:2:21#2/r5.anchor: وقيل فائدة إيراد لفظه لعل هي أن لا يحل العبد أبدا محل الآمن المدل بعمله

TABRISI:2:21#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21#2/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:21#2/r6.claim: Hope or doubt about the hereafter is expressed from the worldly perspective, whereas the hereafter stated alone is certain.
TABRISI:2:21#2/r6.anchor: وأكثر ما جاءت لفظة لعل وغيرها من معاني الشك فيما يتعلق بالآخرة في دار الدنيا

TABRISI:2:21#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21#2/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:21#2/r7.claim: A further gloss is “so that, in your hope, you may guard yourselves from the Fire”; لعل is phrased in terms of servants’ perspective.
TABRISI:2:21#2/r7.anchor: وقيل معناه لعلكم توقون النار في ظنكم ورجائكم وأجرى لعل على عباده دون نفسه

TABRISI:2:21#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:21#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:21#2/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī says this final explanation is close to Sībawayh’s account of لعل as hope directed to hearers.

THALABI:v1p166#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p166#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the address to people is for Meccans, while the address to believers is for Medinans; here the address is general.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يا أيها الناس خطاب أهل مكة، ويا أيها الذين آمنوا خطاب أهل المدينة، وهو هاهنا عام

THALABI:v1p166#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r2.claim: Worship means affirming God's oneness and obeying Him.

THALABI:v1p166#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r3.claim: God brought the addressees and those before them into existence after they had been nothing.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r3.anchor: أوجدكم وأنشأكم بعد أن لم تكونوا شيئا

THALABI:v1p166#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p166#2/r4.claim: The purpose is that people may escape illicit gain and punishment.

THALABI:v1p166#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p166#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
THALABI:v1p166#2/r5.claim: Sibawayh classifies laʿalla and ʿasā as particles of expectation; the source's continuation of his point is lacunose.
THALABI:v1p166#2/r5.anchor: قال سيبويه: لعل وعسى حرفا ترج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r1.claim: Yā is the vocative particle; Arabic rarely combines another particle with a noun to make a complete utterance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r1.anchor: (يا) حرف ينادي به (¬3)، ولا تكاد تجد في كلام العرب حرفا تألف مع اسم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r2.claim: Ayy is an ambiguous singular vocative noun built on ḍamma; الناس is its required adjective, and هاء is obligatory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r2.anchor: و (أي) (¬4) اسم مبهم مبني على الضم، لأنه منادى مفرد، و {الناس} صفة لأي لازمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r3.claim: One cannot say يا الرجل because yā itself supplies definiteness, which would duplicate the article on الرجل.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز (¬5): يا الرجل، لأن (يا) تنبيه بمنزلة التعريف في الرجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r4.claim: The mandatory هاء compensates for the missing iḍāfa, since أي is normally annexed in interrogative and declarative use.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r4.anchor: و (ها) لازمة لأي (¬7)، وهي عوض من الإضافة في (أي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r5.speaker: المازني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r5.claim: Al-Mazini uniquely allows accusative الرجل after يا أيها الرجل.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r5.anchor: والمازني يجيز (¬2) في (يا أيها الرجل) النصب في (الرجل)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq says the accusative is defensible by the vocative's syntactic position, as in other vocatives with an adjective.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وقوله قياس؛ لأن موضوع المنادى المفرد نصب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r7.speaker: النحويون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r7.claim: Other grammarians require the adjective to be nominative: الرجل is the true addressee, and أي is only an intermediary because the article blocks direct yā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r7.anchor: والنحويون غيره (¬7) لا يقولون في هذا إلا الرفع، والعرب لغتها في هذا الرفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r8.claim: The address يا أيها الناس includes every morally responsible person, believer or unbeliever.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r8.anchor: و {يا أيها الناس} عموم في كل مكلف من مؤمن وكافر (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r9.speaker: الحسن وعلقمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r9.claim: Al-Hasan and ʿAlqama are reported to restrict people-addresses to Meccans and believers-addresses to Medinans.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p215/r9.anchor: ويروى عن الحسن وعلقمة (¬4). أن {يا أيها الناس} خطاب أهل مكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r1.claim: Worship your Lord means submitting to Him through obedience, which is proper only toward the owner of all entities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {اعبدوا ربكم} أي اخضعوا له بالطاعة، ولا يجوز ذلك إلا لمالك الأعيان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r2.claim: True creation is originating something without any prior example; everything God creates is originated in that way.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r2.anchor: (الخلق): ابتداع شيء لم يسبق إليه (¬2). وكل شيء خلقه الله فهو مبتدئه على غير مثال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r3.claim: Arabic also uses khalaqa for measuring leather to make a waterskin, water bag, or shoe; Zuhayr's verse witnesses that usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r3.anchor: قال زهير: ولأنت تفري (¬6) ما خلقت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r4.claim: Calling a measurer a creator is metaphorical: human making is estimation, imitation, or forgery within limited ability, whereas God's creation originates without precedent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r4.anchor: وقيل للمقدر: خالق على الاستعارة لا على استحقاق اسم الخلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r5.claim: The verse argues from the Arabs' admission that God created them: they should worship the Creator rather than created idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p218/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أن الله تعالى احتج على العرب بأنه خالقهم وخالق من قبلهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r1.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says laʿalla can express hope, purpose (kay), or expectation/conjecture.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (لعل) يكون (¬5): ترجيا، ويكون بمعنى: (كي)، ويكون: ظنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r2.speaker: يونس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r2.claim: Yunus, with Qutrub agreeing, says laʿalla can mean kay, citing Qur'anic examples and everyday requests made so that an action may follow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r2.anchor: وقال يونس (¬7): (لعل) يأتي في كلام العرب بمعنى: (كي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r3.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r3.claim: Sibawayh says laʿalla is a word of hope and encouragement: worshippers may hope to avoid God's punishment, while God knows Pharaoh's eventual outcome.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p219/r3.anchor: وقال سيبويه: (لعل) كلمة ترجية وتطميع للمخاطبين (¬9). أي كونوا على رجاء وطمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r12.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r12.claim: Abu Ishaq treats the prohibition as an argument from their admission that God created them: the rivals cannot create, whereas God is the Creator.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p227/r12.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: هذا احتجاج عليهم لإقرارهم بأن الله خالقهم

QASHANI:2:21-22/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22/r1.claim: After describing the happy and wretched, Qashani says the address calls people to divine unity.
QASHANI:2:21-22/r1.anchor: لما فرغ من ذكر السعداء والأشقياء، دعاهم إلى التوحيد

QASHANI:2:21-22/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22/r2.claim: The first level of unity is unity of acts; tying worship to lordship lets people see blessings and love God, as the saying describes God creating creatures and making Himself beloved through blessings.
QASHANI:2:21-22/r2.anchor: توحيد الأفعال، فلهذا علق العبودية بالربوبية

QASHANI:2:21-22/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22/r3.claim: Worship is gratitude for a bestowed blessing, and God specifies His lordship over people so they will specify their worship for Him.
QASHANI:2:21-22/r3.anchor: إذ العبادة شكر فلا تكون إلا في مقابلة النعمة، وخصص ربوبيته بهم ليخصوا عبادتهم به

QASHANI:2:21-22/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22/r4.claim: Creation, its prerequisites, the earth, sky, rain, and plants are attributed to God so people recognize all acts as His and lift the first veil, the veil of acts.
QASHANI:2:21-22/r4.anchor: نسب إنشاءهم وإنشاء ما توقف عليه وجودهم من المبادئ والأسباب والشرائط كمن قبلهم من الآباء والأمهات

QASHANI:2:21-22/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22/r6.claim: Worshippers worship the maker, whose manifestation appears in created form; each knows God only to the extent of the divinity found within, and these people found only the voluntary agent.
QASHANI:2:21-22/r6.anchor: وربهم هو المتجلي في صورة الصنع، إذ كل عابد لا يعبد إلا ما يعرفه

QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r1.claim: Islam requires both testimonies: unity alone hides differentiation and becomes determinism leading to heresy and antinomianism, while attributing acts only to the Messenger hides unity and becomes dualism; Islam joins both and regards the Messenger as the manifestation of divine acts.
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r1.anchor: بين قولنا: لا إله إلا الله، وبين قولنا: محمد رسول الله، واعتقاد مظهريته

QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r2.claim: Created acts relate to divine acts as body to spirit: spirit is their source but acts through the body, just as God originates acts that appear through creatures.
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r2.anchor: فكما أن مصدر الفعل هو الروح ولا يتم إلا بالجسد، فكذلك مبدئ الفعل هو الحق

QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r3.claim: A messenger is necessary because veiled, distant creatures cannot receive divine knowledge directly; a mediator combines a spirit witnessing the divine presence with a human nature among people, receives divine words, and conveys them to people who accept him through shared nature.
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r3.anchor: فيجب وجود واسطة يجانس بروحه الشاهدة للحق الحضرة الإلهية، وبنفسه المخالطة للخلق الرتبة البشرية

QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r4.claim: The Messenger receives the divine words in his heart and conveys them through his purified self to humankind.
QASHANI:2:21-22#2/r4.anchor: ليتلقى قلبه من روحه الكلمات الربانية، ويلقي إلى نفسه القدسية، ويقبل منه الخلق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r5.claim: The people addressed are the inhabitants of Mecca.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r5.anchor: { يا أيها الناس } يعني: أهل مكة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r6.claim: Worship your Lord means submit to Him through obedience.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r7.claim: God created you by bringing you into being when you were nothing.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r7.anchor: { الذي خلقكم }: ابتدأكم ولم تكونوا شيئا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r8.claim: Those before you are your forefathers; the passage also says God created those earlier generations.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r8.anchor: { والذين من قبلكم } [آباءكم] [وخلق الذين من قبلكم].

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r9.claim: The Creator is more deserving of worship than a created being such as an idol; worship Him to avoid His punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:20-21/r9.anchor: أي: إن عبادة الخالق أولى من عبادة المخلوق وهو الصنم { لعلكم تتقون } لكي تتقوا بعبادته عقوبته أن تحل بكم.

ELMALILI:2:21/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r1.claim: The verse connects Fātiḥa's Lord of the worlds, the covenant of You alone we worship, guidance for the muttaqīn at the sūra's opening, and the combined purpose of the three stories and rainstorm parable.
ELMALILI:2:21/r1.anchor: Bu âyetin, Fâtiha’daki لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ vasfının isbâtına, اِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ mîsâkına

ELMALILI:2:21/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r2.claim: In Qur'anic order this is God's first explicit command and begins Islam's foundation with the oneness of worship and lordship.
ELMALILI:2:21/r2.anchor: Tertîb-i Kur’ân’a nazaran bu âyet Allah teâlâ’nın sarih olarak ilk emrini hâvî oluyor ki bu emir

ELMALILI:2:21/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r3.claim: The command shows that divinity depends on lordship, lordship on creatorship, and thereby establishes God as Creator.
ELMALILI:2:21/r3.anchor: ulûhiyetin rubûbiyete, rubûbiyetin hâlıkıyete tevakkufunu gösteriyor ve hâlıkı isbat ediyor.

ELMALILI:2:21/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r4.claim: The argument then establishes prophethood and defends Muhammad's truthfulness.
ELMALILI:2:21/r4.anchor: Ve akabinde nübüvveti ve sıdk-ı Muhammedîyi isbat ve müdafaa ediyor.

ELMALILI:2:21/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r5.claim: The address includes all people who have reached human maturity through reason and puberty: believers, unbelievers, hypocrites, every nation, rich and poor, learned and ignorant.
ELMALILI:2:21/r5.anchor: hepiniz mü’min, kâfir, münafık, hangi sınıfa

ELMALILI:2:21/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r6.claim: Everyone is always obliged to worship and obey the Lord who created them and all their forebears, bowing to Him with complete love, reverent fear, respect, and good manners.
ELMALILI:2:21/r6.anchor: Sizi ve sizden evvelkileri, babalarınızı, analarınızı, bütün atalarınızı, ecdâdınızı vesâirlerini baştan nihâyete halk eden Rabbinize

ELMALILI:2:21/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r7.claim: Those who pledged You alone we worship should fulfill that pledge; those who did not should make it and worship and obey God.

ELMALILI:2:21/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r8.claim: The aim is that people may actually be protected and become true muttaqīn; fear of worldly events or death, or refusing to hear, cannot protect them.
ELMALILI:2:21/r8.anchor: bilfiil korunabilesiniz, hakīkī müttakīlerden olmanızı ümit edebilesiniz

ELMALILI:2:21/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r9.claim: La'allakum expresses hope rather than a guarantee: protection is a strong hope, not something worshippers can be certain of.
ELMALILI:2:21/r9.anchor: Dikkat ediniz, لَعَلَّكُمْ buyuruluyor. Bu ise ümit ifade eder.

ELMALILI:2:21/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r10.claim: God's will cannot be constrained by worship; servitude works by the ordinary order, while actual protection comes from divine grace and mercy.
ELMALILI:2:21/r10.anchor: Çünkü irâde-i ilâhiyeyi hiçbir şey takyid edemez. Siz ibadetinizle O’nu korumaya mecbur edemezsiniz.

ELMALILI:2:21/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r11.claim: Worship is gratitude for creation and nurture, not a power that obligates God or puts Him in anyone's debt; no one can fully render the worship and thanks God deserves.
ELMALILI:2:21/r11.anchor: İbadet evvelemirde hilkatinizin, terbiyenizin bir şükrânıdır; bunun Allah’ı mecbur edecek, minnet altında bırakacak bir kudret-i mûcibesi yoktur

ELMALILI:2:21/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:21/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:21/r12.claim: Worshippers should remain hopeful rather than assume every outcome is guaranteed, place their hope only in God, and recognize their Creator by reflecting on their creation and upbringing.
ELMALILI:2:21/r12.anchor: ancak ümidvâr olunuz ve ümidinizi Allah’tan başkasına bağlamayınız ve Allah’ı tanımak için hilkatinize ve terbiyenize bakınız

QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r1.claim: Worship means abstaining from prohibitions, persevering in obedience, meeting duties humbly, and avoiding idleness and disdain.

QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r2.claim: The particle “perhaps” gently eases the command and places people between fear and hope.

QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p28/r3.claim: Godfearingness is guarding oneself and faithfully obeying so as to avoid the threatened punishments.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r1.claim: After the preceding verses distinguished believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites, this verse calls all people to serve God regardless of their belief status.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r1.anchor: Bundan önceki âyetlerde iman bakımından insanlar “mümin, kâfir, münafık” olarak çeşitlendirilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r2.claim: Islam's divine call is addressed to all humanity without distinction of religion, language, race, region, or class.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r2.anchor: din, dil, ırk, bölge, sınıf... farkı gözetmeksizin bütün insanlığa yöneltilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r3.claim: There is no prerequisite for accepting the call: anyone who sincerely professes God's oneness and Muhammad's messengership becomes Muslim, begins serving God, and has past sins erased, however serious.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r3.anchor: Daha önce neler yapmış, ne kadar büyük suç ve günah işlemiş olursa olsun bir kimse gönülden benimseyerek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r4.claim: Worship is due only to the uncreated, necessary, eternal creator who gives things their properties; only Allah possesses these qualities.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r4.anchor: Bu vasıfları taşıyan tek varlık kâinatın yaratıcısı ve rabbi olan Allah Teâlâ’dır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r5.claim: On the main translation, serving God through Islamic faith, worship, ethics, and deeds produces taqwa; the Muslim restrains desires by thoughtful recourse to values and limits, and neither complete taqwa nor human perfection exists without worship and restraint.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r5.anchor: Allah’a kulluk olmadan sakınma (takvâ) gerçekleşemez, sakınma olmadan da kâmil insan olunamaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r6.claim: An alternative translation makes taqwa the purpose for which God created people; worship and taqwa then complete one another and together constitute the purpose of creation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r6.anchor: Âyeti, “Sizi ve sizden öncekileri sakınsınlar diye yaratan Allah’a kulluk edin” şeklinde çevirmek de mümkündür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:21/r7.claim: The commentary also points to its discussion of taqwa at 2:197.

BURHAN:v1p189/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p189/r1.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
BURHAN:v1p189/r1.claim: Urwa says legal penalties and prescribed duties were revealed in Medina, while accounts of earlier peoples and punishments were revealed in Mecca.
BURHAN:v1p189/r1.anchor: قال ما كان من حد أو فريضة فإنه أنزل بالمدينة وما كان من ذكر الأمم والعذاب فإنه أنزل بمكة

BURHAN:v1p189/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p189/r2.speaker: الجعبرى
BURHAN:v1p189/r2.claim: Al-Jaʿbari distinguishes transmitted from analogical identification and offers markers: يا أيها الناس, kalla, disjoint letters with exceptions, Adam and Iblis, and past peoples indicate Meccan; laws indicate Medinan.
BURHAN:v1p189/r2.anchor: وقال الجعبرى لمعرفة المكى والمدنى طريقان سماعى وقياسى فالسماعى ما وصل إلينا نزوله بأحدهما

BURHAN:v1p189/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p189/r3.speaker: علقمة
BURHAN:v1p189/r3.claim: Alqama’s report says verses addressing people with يا أيها الناس are Meccan and those addressing believers with يا أيها الذين آمنوا are Medinan.
BURHAN:v1p189/r3.anchor: قال كل شىء نزل فيه ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ فهو بمكة وكل شىء نزل فيه ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا ﴾ فهو بالمدينة

BURHAN:v1p189/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p189/r4.speaker: البزار
BURHAN:v1p189/r4.claim: Al-Bazzar says the report is usually transmitted from Alqama without a chain to the Prophet’s Companion; only Qays is known to connect it.
BURHAN:v1p189/r4.anchor: وهذا يرويه غير قيس عن علقمة مرسلا ولا نعلم أحدا أسنده إلا قيس

BURHAN:v1p189/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p189/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p189/r5.claim: The people-address rule is not universal: al-Baqara and al-Nisa are Medinan yet contain it, while Meccan al-Hajj addresses believers; it works as a general tendency, as Makki qualifies.
BURHAN:v1p189/r5.anchor: فإن أراد المفسرون أن الغالب ذلك فهو صحيح ولذا قال مكى هذا إنما هو فى الأكثر وليس بعام

BURHAN:v2p322/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p322/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p322/r1.claim: A call summons the addressee’s attention and most often accompanies a command or prohibition; here يا أيها الناس introduces a command.
BURHAN:v2p322/r1.anchor: ومنها النداء وهو طلب إقبال المدعو على الداعي بحرف مخصوص وإنما يصحب في الأكثر الأمر والنهي

BURHAN:v2p322/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p322/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p322/r3.claim: The command can precede the call, as in وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيها المؤمنون.
BURHAN:v2p322/r3.anchor: وربما تقدمت جملة الأمر جملة النداء كقوله تعالى ﴿ وتوبوا إلى الله جميعا أيها المؤمنون ﴾ 7

BURHAN:v2p322/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p322/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p322/r4.claim: When a declarative statement follows a call, a command may follow that statement, as in يا أيها الناس ضرب مثل فاستمعوا له.
BURHAN:v2p322/r4.anchor: وإذا جاءت جملة الخبر بعد النداء ( 1 ) تتبعها جملة الأمر كما في قوله تعالى ﴿ يا أيها الناس ضرب مثل فاستمعوا له ﴾ 2

BURHAN:v3p268#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p268#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p268#2/r1.claim: The verse progresses from nearer to farther: it addresses the present people before their predecessors and mentions earth before heaven.
BURHAN:v3p268#2/r1.anchor: قدم ذكر المخاطبين على من قبلهم وقدم الأرض على السماء

BURHAN:v3p303/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p303/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p303/r1.claim: The second-person form تجهلون can prevail over the third-person قوم because the address remains active; Ibn al-Shajari offers a circumstantial reading, while Ibn al-Anbari says قوم means أنتم.
BURHAN:v3p303/r1.anchor: وقال أبو البركات بن الأنباري ولو قيل إنما قال ﴿ تجهلون ﴾ بالتاء لأن قوم هو أنتم في المعنى فلذلك قال تجهلون

BURHAN:v3p303/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p303/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p303/r5.claim: In يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون, the address in لعلكم attaches to خلقكم, encompassing both generations rather than only those commanded to worship.
BURHAN:v3p303/r5.anchor: فإن الخطاب في ﴿ لعلكم ﴾ متعلق بقوله ﴿ خلقكم ﴾ لا بقوله ﴿ اعبدوا ﴾ حتى يختص بالناس المخاطبين

BURHAN:v3p98/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p98/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p98/r3.claim: The causal لعل in the command to worship may explain either the command itself or the creation mentioned in the relative clause.
BURHAN:v3p98/r3.anchor: التاسع التعليل بلعل كقوله تعالى ﴿ اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون ﴾ 1 قيل هو تعليل لقوله ﴿ اعبدوا ﴾ وقيل لقوله ﴿ خلقكم ﴾

BURHAN:v3p98/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p98/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p98/r5.claim: A ruling may follow a fitting attribute with أن, with فاء, or with no connective; the examples include rulings for pious people and commands linked to their quality.
BURHAN:v3p98/r5.anchor: العاشر ذكر الحكم الكوني أو الشرعي عقب الوصف المناسب له فتارة يذكر بأن وتارة بالفاء وتارة يجرد

SULAMI:v1p52#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p52#5/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p52#5/r1.claim: Some gloss the command to worship your Lord as a command to affirm His oneness.

SULAMI:v1p52#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p52#5/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p52#5/r2.claim: Others call for worship purified of partners, teaching that divine oneness and sincerity lead to God-consciousness.
SULAMI:v1p52#5/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أخلصوا عبادة ربكم من غير اتخاذ الشريك فيه

ITQAN:v1p55/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r1.speaker: عبد الله
ITQAN:v1p55/r1.claim: A report through al-A‘mash, Ibrahim, and ‘Alqama from Ibn Mas‘ud says ‘believers’ addresses are Medinan and ‘people’ addresses Meccan.
ITQAN:v1p55/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله قال ما كان ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا ﴾ أنزل بالمدينة وما كان ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ فبمكة

ITQAN:v1p55/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r2.speaker: علقمة
ITQAN:v1p55/r2.claim: Abu ‘Ubayd also transmits the same Meccan/Medinan rule from ‘Alqama as a mursal report.
ITQAN:v1p55/r2.anchor: وأخرجه أبو عبيد في الفضائل عن علقمة مرسلا

ITQAN:v1p55/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
ITQAN:v1p55/r3.claim: Maymun ibn Mihran extends the rule to ‘Children of Adam’: both ‘people’ and ‘children of Adam’ addresses are Meccan, while ‘believers’ is Medinan.
ITQAN:v1p55/r3.anchor: وأخرج عن ميمون بن مهران قال ما كان في القرآن

ITQAN:v1p55/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r4.speaker: ابن عطية وابن الغرس
ITQAN:v1p55/r4.claim: Ibn ‘Atiyya and Ibn al-Ghars accept the rule for ‘believers’ but say ‘people’ can also address a Medinan audience.
ITQAN:v1p55/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية وابن الغرس وغيرهما هو في

ITQAN:v1p55/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r5.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v1p55/r5.claim: Ibn al-Hisar says scholars of abrogation relied on this report despite its weakness; the Medinan sura al-Nisa’ opens with ‘people,’ and Meccan al-Hajj includes ‘believers.’
ITQAN:v1p55/r5.anchor: قال ابن الحصار قد اعتنى المتشاغلون بالنسخ بهذا الحديث واعتمدوه على ضعفه وقد اتفق الناس على أن النساء مدنية

ITQAN:v1p55/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r6.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v1p55/r6.claim: Another critic rejects a universal reading: al-Baqara and al-Nisa’ are Medinan yet begin with ‘people.’
ITQAN:v1p55/r6.anchor: وقال غيره هذا القول إن أخذ على إطلاقه فيه نظر

ITQAN:v1p55/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r7.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v1p55/r7.claim: Makki says the rule holds only in most cases, not universally; many Meccan suras contain ‘believers’ addresses.
ITQAN:v1p55/r7.anchor: وقال مكي هذا إنما هو في الأكثر وليس بعام

ITQAN:v1p55/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r8.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v1p55/r8.claim: Another proposed reading is that the addressee phrase usually targets the people, or most of the people, of Mecca or Medina.
ITQAN:v1p55/r8.anchor: وقال غيره الأقرب حمله على أنه خطاب المقصود به أو جل المقصود به أهل مكة أو المدينة

ITQAN:v1p55/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r9.speaker: القاضي
ITQAN:v1p55/r9.claim: The Qadi accepts the rule if transmitted, but rejects the rationale that Medina simply had more believers: believers may be addressed by their quality, and worship is enjoined on all.
ITQAN:v1p55/r9.anchor: وقال القاضي إن كان الرجوع في هذا إلى النقل فمسلم وإن كان السبب فيه حصول المؤمنين بالمدينة على الكثرة دون مكة فضعيف

ITQAN:v1p55/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p55/r10.speaker: هشام بن عروة عن أبيه
ITQAN:v1p55/r10.claim: A report from ‘Urwa classifies Qur’anic passages about past peoples and generations as Meccan, and passages on obligations and sunnas as Medinan.
ITQAN:v1p55/r10.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال كل شيء نزل من القرآن فيه ذكر الأمم والقرون فإنما نزل بمكة

ITQAN:v3p222#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r1.claim: A vocative summons the addressee with a particle standing for ‘I call’; it most often precedes and accompanies a command or prohibition.
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r1.anchor: وهو طلب إقبال المدعو على الداعي بحرف نائب مناب ( أدعو ) ويصحب في الأكثر الأمر والنهي والغالب تقدمه

ITQAN:v3p223/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p223/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p223/r1.claim: Ya normally calls someone far away, literally or figuratively, but may address someone near to show eagerness for attention, stress an important address, magnify the addressee, or belittle him.
ITQAN:v3p223/r1.anchor: أصل النداء ب ( يا ) أن تكون للبعيد حقيقة أو حكما

ITQAN:v3p47/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p47/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p47/r6.claim: Most scholars hold that a general address to people includes the Prophet because the wording is general; al-Zuhri reports that he is among the believers addressed by commands to believe.
ITQAN:v3p47/r6.anchor: على مذاهب أصحها وعليه الأكثرون نعم لعموم الصيغة له

ITQAN:v3p47/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p47/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p47/r7.claim: Other views exclude the Prophet because the message is spoken through him for others, or exclude him only when the address is preceded by “say,” while including him otherwise.
ITQAN:v3p47/r7.anchor: والثاني لا لأنه ورد على لسانه لتبليغ غيره ولما له من الخصائص

ITQAN:v3p47/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p47/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p47/r8.claim: The preferred legal-theory view is that “O people” includes unbelievers and enslaved people because its wording is general.
ITQAN:v3p47/r8.anchor: الرابع الأصح في الأصول أن الخطاب ( يأيها الناس ) يشمل الكافر والعبد لعموم اللفظ

ITQAN:v1p252/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p252/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p252/r5.claim: Nūn assimilates into rā or lām after a vowel and is otherwise clear, except nūn in naḥnu, which assimilates because it recurs often, repeats nūn, stays vocalized, and is heavy.
ITQAN:v1p252/r5.anchor: لكثرة دورها وتكرار النون فيها ولزوم حركتها وثقلها

ITQAN:v2p460#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r8.claim: Ayy also serves as a linking form before a vocative noun that has the definite article, as in O people and O Prophet.
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r8.anchor: الرابع أن تكون وصلة إلى نداء ما فيه أل نحو ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ ﴿ يا أيها النبي ﴾

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p22/r1.speaker: علقمة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p22/r1.claim: Alqama says the address ‘O people’ marks a Meccan verse, while ‘O you who believe’ marks a Medinan one, identifying the former as directed to Meccans and the latter to Medinans.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p22/r1.anchor: عن الأعمش عن إبراهيم عن علقمة قال: كل شيء نزل فيه: {يا أيها الناس} فهو مكي

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p22/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p22/r2.claim: The address is to the polytheists of Mecca and continues through the announcement to believers.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p22/r2.anchor: قوله: {يا أيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم} خطاب لمشركي مكة إلى قوله: {وبشر الذين آمنوا}

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r1.claim: Al-nas denotes human beings; its singular is insan and its plurals include nas and anasi.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r1.anchor: الناس : [ اسم ] للحيوان الآدمي . وواحد الناس إنسان .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r2.claim: Ibn Faris links the name al-ins to humans being visible or manifest.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن فارس : سمي الإنس إنسا لظهورهم .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r3.claim: The related verb آنست can mean seeing a thing, hearing a sound, or knowing; anis is whatever provides company or solace.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r3.anchor: ويقال : آنست الشيء : رأيته . وآنست الصوت : سمعته .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r4.speaker: الراجز
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r4.claim: With a doubled s, nas means thirsty; an anonymous rajaz line using نسا is cited as evidence.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r4.anchor: والناس بتشديد السين : العطشان . قال الراجز

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r5.claim: Mecca is called al-nasiya because water is scarce there.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r5.anchor: ويقال لمكة : الناسية ، لقلة الماء بها .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r6.claim: One Qur'anic referent of al-nas is Muhammad, in the verse about people envying what God gave him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الناس في القرآن على اثني عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r7.claim: Another referent is the other messengers, in the statement that believers are witnesses over the people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الناس في القرآن على اثني عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r9.claim: Al-nas can mean believers, as in the curse against those who disbelieve after having believed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r9.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الناس في القرآن على اثني عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r10.claim: It can mean believing people of the Torah, identified here as Ibn Salam and his companions.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r10.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الناس في القرآن على اثني عشر وجها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r11.claim: In the scope verses, al-nas refers to the people of Mecca; the wording remains general although the address is directed to Meccans.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r11.anchor: وهو اللفظ عام وإن خوطب به أهل مكة .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r13.claim: Al-nas can also refer to the Children of Israel, as in the Torah and Gospel being sent as guidance for people and Jesus's address about taking him and his mother as gods.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r13.anchor: والسابع : بنو إسرائيل . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r1.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says la'alla can mean 'so that'; Arabs use it to express purpose, and an anonymous couplet's la'alla-na illustrates that use.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : وللعل ( 113 / أ ) أربعة معاني : أحدها : بمعنى ' كي ' .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r2.claim: An anonymous couplet says 'hold back from war so that we may hold back'; its poet is not named, and لعلنا witnesses the purpose sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r2.anchor: وقلتم لنا كفوا الحروب لعلنا … نكف ووثقتم لنا كل موثق …

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r3.claim: A second Arabic sense is conjecture, as in 'I think I will make pilgrimage this year.'
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : وللعل ( 113 / أ ) أربعة معاني

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r4.claim: A third Arabic sense is 'perhaps' or 'it may be,' as in the example that Abd Allah may rise.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : وللعل ( 113 / أ ) أربعة معاني

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r5.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r5.claim: A fourth Arabic sense is interrogation, as in asking whether someone intends to insult the speaker and be punished.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : وللعل ( 113 / أ ) أربعة معاني

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r6.claim: In Qur'anic use, la'alla can express purpose: people worship their Lord so that they may become mindful of Him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن لعل في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r7.claim: A Qur'anic sense is hope or expectation, expressed in Moses and Aaron's hope that Pharaoh may remember or fear and in the hope God may bring about a matter.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن لعل في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r8.claim: A third Qur'anic sense is 'as if': the people build structures as though they expected to live forever.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p529/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن لعل في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

NAHHAS:v1p197/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r1.claim: Yā is the vocative particle; ayy is a singular vocative in the place of a pronoun, kept moving because it was formerly declinable, with ḍamma chosen over vocative fatḥa and possessive kasra.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r1.anchor: يا حرف النداء و أي نداء مفرد ضم لأنه في موضع المكني وكان يجب أن لا يعرب

NAHHAS:v1p197/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان المازني
NAHHAS:v1p197/r2.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī permits al-nāsu to follow the syntactic position, as in “yā Zayd al-ẓarīf.”
NAHHAS:v1p197/r2.anchor: أجاز أبو عثمان المازني يا أيها الناس على الموضع كما يقال يا زيد الظريف

NAHHAS:v1p197/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r3.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p197/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash treats al-nās as attached to ayy and the hāʾ as an attention particle that stays with ayy in place of annexation.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r3.anchor: لا تفارق أيا لأنها عوض من الإضافة

NAHHAS:v1p197/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r4.speaker: بعض بني مالك من بني أسد
NAHHAS:v1p197/r4.claim: Some Banū Mālik of Banū Asad say yā ayyuhar-rajulu, giving the obligatory hāʾ the vowel of ayy.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r4.anchor: ولغة بعض بني مالك من بني أسد يا أيه الرجل بضم الهاء لما كانت الهاء لازمة حركتها

NAHHAS:v1p197/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r5.speaker: أبو العباس
NAHHAS:v1p197/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās says al-nās follows ayy as an adjective and cannot be accusative because it is indispensable, unlike a direct “yā nās.”
NAHHAS:v1p197/r5.anchor: لا يجوز نصبه عند أبي العباس لأنه لا يستغنى عنه فصار كما تقول يا ناس

NAHHAS:v1p197/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r6.claim: The imperative ʿbudū begins with a connecting hamza; its ḍamma replaces the root kasra to avoid a kasra followed by ḍamma.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r6.anchor: ألف وصل لأنه من يعبد وضممتها والأصل الكسر لئلا تجمع بين كسرة وضمة

NAHHAS:v1p197/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r7.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p197/r7.claim: Sībawayh says Arabic has no verb on the pattern fiʿil.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r7.anchor: قال سيبويه ليس في الكلام فعل وحذف النون للجزم عند الكوفيين

NAHHAS:v1p197/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v1p197/r8.claim: The Kūfans explain the missing nūn in the imperative by jussive mood; the Basrans say the verb does not resemble the indicative form.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r8.anchor: وحذف النون للجزم عند الكوفيين ولأنه لم يضارع عند البصريين

NAHHAS:v1p197/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r9.claim: Rabbakum is the direct object of ʿbudū.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r9.anchor: ربكم ) نصب باعبدوا ( الذي ) نعت له

NAHHAS:v1p197/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r10.claim: Alladhī modifies rabbakum, while khalaqakum is its relative clause and kum is the verb’s object.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r10.anchor: نعت له ( خلقكم ) في الصلة والكاف والميم نصب بالفعل

NAHHAS:v1p197/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r11.claim: Alladhīna is coordinated with the object pronoun kum, and min qablikum is its relative clause.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r11.anchor: عطف على الكاف والميم ( من قبلكم ) في الصلة

NAHHAS:v1p197/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p197/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p197/r12.claim: Kum is the subject of laʿalla; tattaqūn is a present indicative verb whose nūn marks the indicative and whose clause is laʿalla’s predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p197/r12.anchor: الكاف والميم اسم لعل ( تتقون ) فعل مستقبل علامة رفعه النون

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r1.claim: Ya is the basic vocative particle, can be omitted, and marks lament and calls for help; a report says all Quranic vocatives use it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r1.anchor: حرف نداء وهي أم الباب، وزعم بعضهم أنها اسم فعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r2.claim: Some unusually interpret the light-mīm reading of the phrase in 39:9 as hamza plus ya of address.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r2.anchor: أن قراءة { أمن هو قانت } [الزمر: 9] بتخفيف الميم

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r3.claim: Ya may serve as a mere attention marker before nominal or verbal clauses, as in the Quranic and poetic examples.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r3.anchor: وقد يراد بها مجرد التنبيه فيليها الجمل الاسمية والفعلية

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r4.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash analyzes ay as a relative pronoun, with an omitted subject and a relative clause meaning “those who are the people”; the author prefers direct address.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r4.anchor: وزعم الأخفش أنها هنا موصولة، وأن المرفوع بعدها خبر مبتدأ مضمر

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r5.claim: Ay is a nominative-built vocative in the accusative; its following adjective must be nominative, not accusative by attraction, contrary to al-Mazini.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r5.anchor: والمرفوع بعدها صفة لها يلزم رفعه

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r6.claim: The hāʾ is an obligatory added attention particle, usually fatḥa but sometimes ḍamma by assimilation to yāʾ; ʿAmir reads that way in some instances, supported by the written form.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r6.anchor: ويجوز ضمها إتباعا للياء، وقد قرأ عامر بذلك

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r7.claim: This ay may be modified only by a definite phrase, a relative pronoun containing the article, or a demonstrative; ay also has interrogative, conditional, relative, and other uses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r7.anchor: هذه إلا بما فيه الألف واللام، أو بموصول هما فيه

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r8.claim: Al-nas is either an adjective of ay or the predicate of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r8.anchor: صفة لأي، أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف حسبما تقدم من الخلاف

SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r9.claim: Uʿbudu rabbakum is an initial imperative clause with no syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21/r9.anchor: جملة أمرية لا محل لها لأنها ابتدائية

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r1.claim: Alladhi has three parses: accusative as an adjective to rabbakum, accusative by qatʿ, or nominative by qatʿ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r1.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه، أظهرها: نصبه على النعت لربكم. الثاني: نصبه على القطع.

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r2.claim: Alladhina is accusative by coordination with the object of khalaqakum; min qablikum is its relative clause and min marks the starting point.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r2.anchor: محله النصب لعطفه على المنصوب في

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r3.claim: Some object that min qablikum is incomplete as a relative clause; one answer supplies “who were from a time before your time.”
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r3.anchor: واستشكل بعضهم وقوع " من قبلكم " صلة من حيث

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies the sense “those whom He created before your creation,” deleting creation and leaving its pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " التقدير: والذين خلقهم من قبل خلقكم

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads the mīm of min with fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: " والذين من قبلكم " بفتح الميم

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the reading by inserting a second relative pronoun as emphasis between the first pronoun and its relative clause, analogously to repeated wording in poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ووجهها على إشكالها أن يقال: أقحم الموصول الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r7.claim: A critic rejects insertion because an emphasized particle must repeat what it attaches to; an alternative makes the second relative clause predicate an omitted subject, though the author calls this strained.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#2/r7.anchor: إلا أن بعضهم يرد هذا القول ويجعله فاسدا، من جهة

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r1.claim: Khalq can mean origination and creation, unique to God, or measuring and shaping, which is not exclusive to God.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r1.anchor: والخلق يقال باعتبارين، وأحدهما: الإبداع والاختراع، وهذه الصفة ينفرد بها الباري تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r2.speaker: زهير
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r2.claim: Zuhayr uses khalq in the sense of measuring or shaping, which a person may do without successfully carrying it through.

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r3.speaker: الحجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r3.claim: Al-Hajjaj likewise uses khalq for planning or promising followed by carrying out the plan.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r3.anchor: وقال الحجاج: " ما خلقت إلا فريت ولا وعدت إلا وفيت "

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r4.claim: The author rejects Abu Abd Allah al-Basri's denial that God may be called Creator on the ground that measuring and shaping would imply thought; Quranic usage names God Creator and creation also means origination.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r4.anchor: وقد غلط أبو عبد الله البصري في أنه لا يطلق اسم الخالق على الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r5.claim: The author cites God as “the Creator, the Originator” and “Creator of everything” to refute the denial of the divine name al-Khaliq.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r5.anchor: وكأنه لم يعلم أن الخلق يكون عبارة عن الإنشاء والاختراع

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r6.claim: Laʿalla has a noun and predicate here; its use in divine speech has three reported analyses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r6.anchor: لعل واسمها وخبرها، وإذا ورد ذلك في كلام الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r7.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r7.claim: On its ordinary meaning of hope and inducement, laʿalla is relative to the addressees: they worship in hope of becoming God-fearing; Sibawayh applies this to Moses and Aaron.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r7.anchor: وكذا قال سيبويه في قوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r8.speaker: قطرب
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r8.claim: Qutrub, al-Tabari, and others take laʿalla causally, meaning “so that you may become God-fearing”; a poem uses it to mean “so that we may cease fighting.”
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r8.anchor: وبه قال قطرب والطبري وغيرهما وأنشدوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r9.speaker: المهدوي
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r9.claim: A third analysis takes laʿalla to mean acting in openness to attaining taqwa; al-Mahdawi and Abu al-Baqa favor attaching the clause semantically to the command to worship.

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya sees laʿalla as attached to khalqakum: every child is born on the natural disposition and may therefore be expected to become God-fearing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " يتجه تعلقها ب "

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r11.speaker: المهدوي
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r11.claim: Al-Mahdawi objects that this cannot attach to creation, since those created for Hell were not created in order to become God-fearing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r11.anchor: إلا أن المهدوي منع من ذلك، قال:

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches laʿalla to khalqakum, says the plural includes earlier peoples by rhetorical dominance, and argues that taqwa is worship's ultimate aim rather than a repetition of worship.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r12.anchor: ولم يذكر الزمخشري غير تعلقها ب

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r13.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r13.claim: The Shaykh rejects al-Zamakhshari's appeal to matching the ends of the wording: “worship so you may worship” or “fear so you may fear” would be awkward and semantically defective.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r13.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وأما قوله: ليتجاوب طرفا النظم

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r14.claim: The author attaches laʿalla to uʿbudu: worship is the commanded purpose, while the relative clause describes or praises the one worshipped rather than supplying a competing attachment.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#3/r14.anchor: والذي يظهر به صحته أن يكون

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r1.claim: Laʿalla has many dialect forms and can govern a genitive; on the correct view it does not put both nouns in the accusative, and an can enter its predicate by analogy with ʿasa.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r1.anchor: ولا تنصب الاسمين على الصحيح، وقد تدخل

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r2.claim: Its basic meaning is expectation of desired things and apprehension regarding feared things, like ʿasa, though it can also convey question or cause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r2.anchor: ولكن أصلها أن تكون للترجي والطمع في المحبوبات والإشفاق في المكروهات كعسى

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r3.claim: Tattaqun derives from tawtaqiyun: wāw becomes tāʾ before the infix tāʾ and assimilates, then vowel and hiatus changes yield the current pattern taftaʿūn.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r3.anchor: وأصل تتقون: توتقيون لأنه من الوقاية، فأبدلت الواو تاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r4.claim: Laʿallakum tattaqun cannot be a circumstantial clause because it is a request; tattaqun has an omitted object, such as shirk or the Fire.
SAMIN-DURR:2:21#4/r4.anchor: وهذه الجملة أعني " لعلكم تتقون " لا يجوز أن تكون حالا لأنها طلبية

ZAJJAJ:v1p97/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p97/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p97/r4.claim: God argues with the Arabs from what they already acknowledge: He created them and those before them, so they should worship Him rather than idols.
ZAJJAJ:v1p97/r4.anchor: إن الله احتج على العرب بأنه خالقهم وخالق من قبلهم لأنهم كانوا مقرين بذلك

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r1.claim: Tattaqūn means guarding yourselves from forbidden things and refraining from what God prohibited.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r1.anchor: معناه تتقون الحرمات بينكم وتكفون عما تأتون مما حرمه الله

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r2.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r2.claim: Some linguists interpret laʿalla causally here as meaning so that you may become God-fearing.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r2.anchor: عن بعض أهل اللغة: أحدهما: معناها كي تتقوا، والذي يذهب إليه

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r3.speaker: سيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r3.claim: Sībawayh takes laʿalla in such contexts as expressing hope; Zajjāj follows this analysis, illustrated by Moses and Aaron hoping Pharaoh might remember while God knows the outcome.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r3.anchor: والذي يذهب إليه سيبويه في مثل هذا أنه ترج لهم كما قال في قصة فرعون

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r4.claim: Ayyu is an indeclinable singular vocative, and al-nās is its required adjective; yāʾ cannot directly precede a definite noun, so ayyu provides access to the article.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r4.anchor: وأما إعراب (يا أيها) فأي اسم مبهم مبني على الضم لأنه منادى مفرد

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r5.claim: The attention particle hāʾ is required with ayyu and substitutes for its usual annexation, since ayyu is normally annexed in interrogative or declarative use.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r5.anchor: وها لازمه لأي، للتنبيه، وهي عوض من الإضافة في أي

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r6.speaker: سيبويه عن الخليل
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r6.claim: Sībawayh reports al-Khalīl's analysis: a singular vocative is built on the nominative form, so its adjective has regular nominative case.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r6.anchor: زعم سيبويه عن الخليل أن المنادى المفرد مبني وصفته مرفوعة رفعا صحيحا

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r7.speaker: المازني
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r7.claim: Al-Māzinī permits an accusative adjective by analogy with the vocative's underlying accusative position; Zajjāj notes other grammarians do not accept this for yā ayyuhā al-rajul.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r7.anchor: والمازني يجيز في يا أيها الرجل النصب في الرجل، ولم يقل بهذا القول

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r8.claim: Although the vocative's true target is al-rajul and ayyu is only a link to it, Arab usage in yā ayyuhā consistently raises the adjective.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r8.anchor: والنحويون لا يقولون إلا يا أيها الرجل، يا أيها الناس، والعرب لغتها في هذا الرفع

ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r9.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r9.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash says it is more analogical for al-rajul to serve as a complement to ayyu, but no Basran grammarian follows him.
ZAJJAJ:v1p98/r9.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن الأخفش إن الرجل أن يكون صلة لأي أقيس، وليس أحد من البصريين يتابعه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p586/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p586/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p586/r1.claim: Allah is used in contexts of severe warning, obligation, and threat; Rabb highlights lordship, nurture, guidance, and blessings bestowed on all people, so guidance often appears with Rabb.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p586/r1.anchor: لفظ الجلالة الله هو اللفظ العام لله تعالى ويذكر هذا اللفظ دائماً في مقام التخويف الشديد

NASHR:v1p226/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p226/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p226/r2.claim: Complete pauses may also precede the end of a verse, occur inside a verse or after its last word; he gives the transition into the address to humankind as an example.
NASHR:v1p226/r2.anchor: نحو إن الله على كل شيء قدير والابتداء ياأيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم

NASHR:v1p235/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p235/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p235/r4.claim: Sajawandi bars a stop at laʿallakum tattaqūn because alladhī is an adjective of the Lord, but it can instead be the predicate of an implied huwa or a commendatory phrase, so stopping is good; Maki's accusative analyses are judged remote.

IBNHISHAM:v1p533/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p533/r1.speaker: author
IBNHISHAM:v1p533/r1.claim: The command addresses both unbelievers and hypocrites: worship means affirming the oneness of the Lord who created them and earlier peoples, so they may become God-fearing.
IBNHISHAM:v1p533/r1.anchor: للفريقين جميعا، من الكفار والمنافقين، أي وحدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.claim: Yā is the Qurʾān’s only vocative particle despite frequent address and is the broadest, addressing near, far, implored, and lamented listeners; it can also mark attention.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r1.anchor: وهي أعم حروف النداء، إذ ينادى بها القريب والبعيد والمستغاث والمندوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.claim: The stronger analysis supplies no omitted vocative noun after ayy; ayy has interrogative, conditional, adjectival, relative, and definite-vocative uses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r2.anchor: والأصح أن لا ينوى بعدها منادي. أي: استفهام وشرط وصفة ووصلة لنداء ما فيه الألف واللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā denies the relative use of ayy; al-Akhfash denies its adjectival use.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r3.anchor: وموصولة، خلافا لأحمد بن يحيى، إذ أنكر مجيئها موصولة، ولا تكون موصوفة خلافا للأخفش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.claim: Hā is an attention particle commonly used with a separate nominative pronoun or demonstrative; in a vocative it separates ayy from the following noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r4.anchor: ها: حرف تنبيه، أكثر استعمالها مع ضمير رفع منفصل مبتدأ مخبر عنه باسم إشارة غالبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.speaker: بنو مالك من بني أسد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.claim: Banū Mālik of Banū Asad use a ḍamma in hā when addressing a man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r5.anchor: وضمها فيه لغة بني مالك من بني أسد، يقولون: يا أيه الرجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r6.claim: Creation means originating without a model and originally meant measuring; Zuhayr’s line witnesses the root sense. Quṭrub defines it as measured, ordered origination.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r6.anchor: الخلق: الاختراع بلا مثال، وأصله التقدير، خلقت الأديم قدرته، قال زهير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r7.claim: Qabla is a temporal adverb that ordinarily remains adverbial only when governed by min; it originated as an adjective standing for an omitted noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r7.anchor: قبل: ظرف زمان، ولا يعمل فيها عامل فيخرجها عن الظرفية إلا من، وأصلها وصف ناب عن موصوفه لزوما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r8.claim: Laʿalla expresses hope for desired things and expectation for feared things, and applies only to possibilities; it is not kay contrary to Quṭrub and Ibn Kaysān, nor interrogative contrary to the Kufans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r8.anchor: لعل: حرف ترج في المحبوبات، وتوقع في المحدورات، ولا تستعمل إلا في الممكن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r9.speaker: الأخفش وأبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash reports that some Arabs use genitive after laʿalla; Abū Zayd attributes that dialect to Banū ʿUqayl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p151#2/r9.anchor: وحكى الأخفش أن من العرب من يجر بلعل، وزعم أبو زيد أن ذلك لغة بني عقيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas takes الناس to address all rational beings; Abū Ḥayyān prefers this since restricting the address requires evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r10.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، أو اليهود خاصة، قاله الحسن ومجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r11.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r11.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say the address is specifically to the Jews.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r11.anchor: أو اليهود خاصة، قاله الحسن ومجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r12.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r12.claim: Muqatil says the address is to the Jews and hypocrites.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r13.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r13.claim: Al-Suddi says the address is to Arab polytheists and other disbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r13.anchor: أو لكفار مشركي العرب وغيرهم، قاله السدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r14.claim: After describing believers, disbelievers, and hypocrites, the verse shifts to direct address, engaging the listener; it resembles the shift from praise to direct address in 1:5.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r14.anchor: انتقل من الإخبار عنهم إلى خطاب النداء، وهو التفات شبيه بقوله: إياك نعبد، بعد قوله: الحمد لله رب العالمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r15.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r15.claim: An unnamed exegete calls this a shift from specific to general address; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because no specific address preceded it, unless كلام is loose for discourse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r15.anchor: وليس هذا انتقالا من الخطاب الخاص إلى الخطاب العام، كما زعم بعض المفسرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r16.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r16.claim: As an example of addressing close kin and broadening the call, the Prophet warns al-Abbas, Fatima, and Banu Abd al-Muttalib that he cannot avail them against God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152/r16.anchor: فقال: «يا عباس عم محمد لا أغني عنك من الله شيئا، ويا فاطمة بنت محمد لا أغني عنك من الله شيئا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r1.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r1.claim: The poet's call to his sons, household, and clan illustrates addressing a specific group and then broadening the call.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r1.anchor: وقال الشاعر: يا بني اندبوا ويا أهل بيتي ... وقبيلي علي عاما فعاما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعلقمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r2.claim: They say every يا أيها الناس passage is Meccan and every يا أيها الذين آمنوا passage Medinan; Abū Ḥayyān accepts the latter but treats the former as a tendency since this Medinan sura contains يا أيها الناس.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وعلقمة أنهم قالوا: كل شيء نزل فيه: يا أيها الناس فهو مكي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r3.speaker: author
