ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r3.claim: أي is a singular vocative built on ḍamm, not inflection, contrary to al-Kisa'i and al-Riyashi; it mediates calling a definite noun that cannot be directly called.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r3.anchor: وأي في أيها منادى مفرد مبني على الضم، وليست الضمة فيه حركة إعراب خلافا للكسائي والرياشي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r4.claim: أي is accusative by position and الناس nominative as its adjective by surface form; it cannot be accusative by position, contrary to Abu Uthman.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r4.anchor: وارتفع الناس على الصفة على اللفظ، لأن بناء أي شبيه بالإعراب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r5.speaker: أبو عثمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r5.claim: Abu Uthman permits الناس to be accusative by syntactic position rather than nominative by surface agreement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r5.anchor: ولا يجوز نصبه على الموضع، خلافا لأبي عثمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r6.claim: In one account, Abu al-Hasan treats أي as a relative expression and the following nominative as predicate of an omitted subject: يا من هو الرجل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r6.anchor: وزعم أبو الحسن في أحد قوليه أن أيا في النداء موصولة وأن المرفوع بعدها خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r7.claim: The worship command includes believers and unbelievers; for believers already worshiping, it commands an increase in worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r7.anchor: الأمر بالعبادة شمل المؤمنين والكافرين. لا يقال: المؤمنون عابدون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r8.claim: Calling God رب is apt because He is master and rectifier; one who owns or rectifies the servant's affairs deserves exclusive worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r8.anchor: فإنه السيد والمصلح، وجدير بمن كان مالكا أو مصلحا أحوال العبد أن يخص بالعبادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r9.claim: For a universal audience, who created you is praise; for Arab polytheists it clarifies which lord is meant, since they also called idols lords.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r9.anchor: وإن كان لمشركي العرب كانت للتوضيح، إذ لفظ الرب بالنسبة إليهم مشترك بين الله تعالى وبين آلهتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r10.claim: The question whether one who creates is like one who does not create is evidence that creation distinguishes God from idols.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r11.claim: The description recalls God's favor in creating humans in complete form, distinguishing them by reason and granting outward and inward blessings; lordship and creation entail worship and love-driven obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r11.anchor: امتنانه عليهم بالخلق على الصورة الكاملة، والتمييز عن غيرهم بالعقل، والإحسان إليهم بالنعم الظاهرة والباطنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r12.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the final consonant of خلقكم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p152#2/r12.anchor: وأدغم أبو عمرو خلقكم، وتقدم تفسير الخلق في اللغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r1.claim: Muslims unanimously affirm no creator but God; when خلق means determining, Arabic can apply it to others, as Zuhayr's verse and Qur'anic uses show.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r1.anchor: وقد أجمع المسلمون على أن لا خالق إلا الله تعالى، وإذا كان بمعنى التقدير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله البصري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: Abu Abd Allah al-Basri, teacher of Qadi Abd al-Jabbar, says calling God خالق is impossible because measuring and shaping imply thought, conjecture, and calculation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله البصري، أستاذ القاضي عبد الجبار: إطلاق اسم الخالق على الله تعالى محال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Basri: he overlooked the Arabic sense of origination, and his claim conflicts with Qur'an, Arabic usage, and consensus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r3.anchor: وكلام البصري مصادم لقوله تعالى: هو الله الخالق البارئ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r4.claim: والذين من قبلكم coordinates with the object pronoun in خلقكم; predecessors are mentioned first despite their earlier time because people know themselves best and are immediate addressees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r4.anchor: وعطف قوله: والذين من قبلكم على الضمير المنصوب في خلقكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r5.claim: Creation is mentioned first because Arabs, the immediate audience in whose language the Qur'an came, already acknowledged God as their creator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r5.anchor: وبدأ أولا بصفة الخلق، إذ كانت العرب مقرة بأن الله خالقها، وهم المخاطبون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r6.speaker: ابن السميفع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfa reads وخلق من قبلكم, making this coordination of clauses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع: وخلق من قبلكم، جعله من عطف الجمل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r7.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads من with fatḥa; al-Zamakhshari explains it as an inserted emphatic second relative, by analogy with Jarir's line.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r7.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: والذين من قبلكم بفتح ميم من، قال الزمخشري: وهي قراءة مشكلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses the second relative as an inserted emphatic repetition without its own clause, comparing Jarir's repeated تيم and the lam in لا أبا لك.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154/r8.anchor: وجهها على إشكالها أن يقال: أقحم الموصول الثاني بين الأول وصلته تأكيدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r1.speaker: أصحابنا
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān's grammarian school rejects al-Zamakhshari's parse: an emphatic relative should repeat with its clause, just as an emphasized preposition repeats with what it governs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r1.anchor: قال أصحابنا: وهذا الذي ذهب إليه باطل، لأن القياس إذا أكد الموصول أن تكرره مع صلته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r2.claim: They parse the poetry with the clause attached to the second relative as predicate of an omitted subject; this forms the first relative's clause, yielding والذين هم من قبلكم for Zayd's reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r2.anchor: وخرج أصحابنا البيت على أن الصلة للموصول الثاني وهو خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r3.claim: On the standard reading, من قبلكم seems an incomplete prepositional phrase attached to a relative denoting individuals; it is understood as a temporal predicate, meaning those from a time before yours.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r3.anchor: وفي ذلك إشكال، لأن الذين أعيان، ومن قبلكم جار ومجرور ناقص ليس في الإخبار به عن الأعيان فائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r4.claim: Earlier generations are included though their creation does not itself require our worship, because they are our ancestors and their creation benefits their descendants too.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r4.anchor: وإنما ذكر والذين من قبلكم، وإن كان خلقهم لا يقتضي العبادة علينا لأنهم كالأصول لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r5.claim: لعل does not mean purpose; hope belongs to the human addressees, since God knows the unseen and does not hope.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r5.anchor: وليست لعل هنا بمعنى كي لأنه قول مرغوب عنه ولكنها للترجي والإطماع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows لعل to attach to خلقكم, since every child born upon the primordial nature may be hoped to become pious.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويتجه تعلقها بخلقكم لأن كل مولود يوجد على الفطرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches لعل to creation and calls hope figurative: God equips people for duty and gives them choice, like a person whose action remains undecided.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r7.anchor: قال: لعل واقعة في الآية موقع المجاز لا الحقيقة، لأن الله تعالى خلق عباده ليتعبدهم بالتكليف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān identifies al-Zamakhshari's account as resting on Mu'tazili doctrines that humans choose their acts and God wills only good for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p154#2/r8.anchor: وهو مبني على مذهبه الاعتزالي من أن العبد مختار، وأنه لا يريد الله منه إلا فعل الخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r1.claim: He prefers attaching لعل to اعبدوا: worship is the reason for the address, while the creation phrase praises or explains the object of worship rather than making the main assertion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r1.anchor: والذي يظهر ترجيحه أن يكون: لعلكم تتقون متعلقا بقوله: اعبدوا ربكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r2.claim: If لعل attaches to creation, al-Zamakhshari says its restriction to the addressees is grammatical dominance: the meaning includes them and their predecessors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r2.anchor: لم يقصره عليهم ولكن غلب المخاطبين على الغائبين في اللفظ والمعنى على إرادتهم جميعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r3.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r3.claim: Al-Mahdawi connects لعل to worship, not creation, because God did not create for piety those whom He destined for Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r3.anchor: وقال المهدوي: لعل متصلة باعبدوا لا بخلقكم، لأن من درأه الله عز وجل لجهنم لم يخلقه ليتقي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r4.claim: Sibawayh glosses the construction as doing the commanded act in hope and expectation of becoming pious.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r4.anchor: والمعنى عند سيبويه: افعلوا ذلك على الرجاء والطمع أن تتقوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says piety is the culmination and highest goal of worship, strongly motivating obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r5.anchor: فإذا قال: اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم للاستيلاء على أقصى غايات العبادة كان أبعث على العبادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the reply about matching the syntax: it would say worship so that you may worship, a poor meaning and expression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في هذا من غثاثة اللفظ وفساد المعنى، والقرآن متنزه عن ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r7.claim: The command clause is the main requested action, and its hope clause addresses those same addressees; this supports connecting لعل to worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156/r7.anchor: بخلاف قوله: اعبدوا، فإنها الجملة المفتتح بها أولا والمطلوبة من المخاطبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r1.claim: The omitted object of يتقون is explained by reports; piety guards against harm, while worship produces that guarding, so using piety for the act itself is metaphorical.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r1.anchor: فعل المأمور به ليس نفس الاحتراز بل يوجب الاحتراز، فكأنه قال: اعبدوه فتحترزوا عن عقابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the omitted object of piety as associating partners with God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الشرك، وقال الضحاك: النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the omitted object of piety as the Fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الشرك، وقال الضحاك: النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r4.claim: Mujahid explains يتقون here as “you obey.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r5.claim: Some exegetes object that if God created people hoping they would be pious, they would be innately obedient, contrary to the many sins people commit; Abū Ḥayyān says this objection fails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r5.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: فيه بعد من حيث إنه لو خلقهم راجين للتقوى كانوا مطيعين مجبولين عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r6.claim: A person can hope for something that does not occur; humans do not control whether they act or refrain, and a cited poet says awareness of sin while committing it shows compulsion by decree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r6.anchor: ولقد صدق الشاعر في قوله: علمي بقبح المعاصي حين أركبها ... يقضي بأني محمول على القدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r7.claim: The proposed circumstantial reading is impossible: لعل expresses hope by one who does not know, so neither it nor its clause can function as حال.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r7.anchor: فهي وما دخلت عليه ليست جملة خبرية فيصح وقوعها حالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r8.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r8.claim: Al-Tabari says the command is evidence against denying the permissibility of imposing an unperformable duty: God commanded believers and unbelievers although some would not believe or leave error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p156#2/r8.anchor: قال الطبري: هذه الآية، يريد: يا أيها الناس اعبدوا من أدل دليل على فساد قول من زعم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r6.claim: The passage gives five signs: creating the addressees and their forebears, then earth as a bed, heaven as a building, and rain and fruit; humans come first as familiar, earth before sky, and effects after causes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r6.anchor: وانتهى عند قوله: رزقا لكم ذكر خمسة أنواع من الدلائل: اثنين من الأنفس خلقهم وخلق من قبلهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r7.claim: Another explanation puts accountable humans first because life, ability, desire, and reason are prerequisites for benefiting from the heavens, earth, water, and fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p160/r7.anchor: وقيل: قدم المكلفين لأن خلقهم أحياء قادرين أصل لجميع النعم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches the prohibition to لعل, parses تجعلوا as subjunctive after a hope, and understands creation as aimed at fear of God's punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري: متعلق بلعل، على أن ينتصب تجعلوا انتصاب فأطلع في قوله: لعلي أبلغ الأسباب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Zamakhshari's parsing because Basran grammarians do not allow a subjunctive as the answer to hope; only Kufans analogize it to an interrogative answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r9.anchor: فهذا التخريج الذي أخرجه الزمخشري لا يجوز على مذهب البصريين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r10.claim: He also objects that this parsing makes human creation serve the purpose of fearing punishment, which follows al-Zamakhshari's previously discussed Muʿtazilite doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p161/r10.anchor: وفي كلامه تعليق لعلكم تتقون بخلقكم، ألا ترى إلى تقديره أي خلقكم لكي تتقوا وتخافوا عقابه؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r1.claim: Some exegetes say these creations are singled out because they invite reflection, display benefits in both lives, and prove the Creator's existence, power, wisdom, life, will and exclusive creation and governance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r1.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: اختص تعالى بهذه المخلوقات وهي: الخلقة البشرية، والبنيتان الأرضية والسماوية، لأنها محل الاعتبار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r2.claim: They explain the human creation's precedence by its intricate workmanship, clearer in delicate bodies, and by self-reflection being mentally nearer; the passage cites the call to observe oneself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r2.anchor: وقدم الخلقة البشرية، وإن كانت للعالم الأصغر، لما فيها من بدائع الصنعة ما لا يعبر عنه وصف لسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r3.claim: Another reason for mentioning humans first is Arab custom of placing what matters most first; God gives special care to humanity as his noblest creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r3.anchor: أو لأن العرب عادتها تقديم الأهم عندها والمعتنى به، قال: وهو تعالى بإصلاح حال البنية البشرية أكثر اهتماما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r4.claim: The sequence can also put the beneficiary before the gifts, since God made these things as benefits for Adam's children and prepared them as blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p163/r4.anchor: ولأنه تعالى خلق هذه الأشياء منافع لبني آدم وأعدها نعما يمتن بها عليهم، وذكر المنعم عليه يتقدم على ذكر النعمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r2.claim: The two verses' craft, wisdom and clear proofs show that God alone creates and provides; rivals neither create nor provide, and can neither benefit nor harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r2.anchor: وقد تضمنت هاتان الآيتان من بدائع الصنعة، ودقائق الحكمة، وظهور البراهين، ما اقتضى تعالى أنه المنفرد بالإيجاد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r3.speaker: بعض أصحاب الإشارات
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r3.claim: An allusive reading compares earth to a mother and sky to a father, rain to semen descending from the father, and fruit to a child born from the mother; the analogy teaches that God truly creates both offspring and fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r3.anchor: قال بعض أصحاب الإشارات: لما امتن تعالى عليهم بأنه خلقهم والذين من قبلهم، ضرب لهم مثلا يرشدهم إلى معرفة كيفية خلقهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r4.speaker: بعض أصحاب الإشارات
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r4.claim: The allusion concludes that recognition of God as the real creator should lead people to single him out in divinity and worship, bringing them to guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p164/r4.anchor: فإذا أوضح ذلك لهم أفردوه بالإلهية، وخصوه بالعبادة، وحصلت لهم الهداية.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r1.claim: After classifying believers, disbelievers, and hypocrites and describing their outcomes, the discourse turns to address all people directly.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r1.anchor: لما بين سبحانه فرق المكلفين وقسمهم إلى مؤمنين وكفار ومذبذبين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r2.claim: The preceding descriptions include the believers’ guidance and success, the disbelievers’ sealed hearts and great punishment, and the hypocrites’ diseased hearts and painful punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r2.anchor: وفي الثانية ( سواء عليهم ) وفي الثالثة ( يخادعون الله ) وشرح ما ترجع إليه أحوالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r3.claim: The shift to direct address is an iltifāt that rouses people to listen and directs their hearts toward receiving the message.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r3.anchor: أقبل عز شأنه عليهم بالخطاب على نهج الالتفات هزا لهم إلى الإصغاء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r4.claim: The sweet intimacy of direct address eases the burden involved in worship; the rhetorical effect need only occur for some of the audience.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r4.anchor: وجبرا لما في العبادة من الكلفة بلذيذ المخاطبة ويكفي للنكتة الوجود في البعض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r5.claim: The correct view is that yā is a vocative particle, not a noun or a verb, and it was originally used to call someone distant.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r5.anchor: حرف لا اسم فعل على الصحيح وضع لنداء البعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r6.claim: Other grammarians take yā for any vocative or say it is shared by the classes of vocative.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r6.anchor: لمطلق النداء أو مشتركة بين أقسامه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r7.claim: A near addressee may be called “distant” because of the caller’s or addressee’s rank, the listener’s inattention, or to stress urgency and encourage compliance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r7.anchor: وعلى الأول ينادي بها القريب لتنزيله منزلة غيره إما لعلو مرتبة المنادي أو المنادي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r8.claim: The distance-based urgency may be analyzed as metonymy or as a dependent or implicit metaphor with its imagined image.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r8.anchor: فأستعمل في لازم معناه على أنه مجاز مرسل أو استعارة تبعية في الحرف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r9.claim: Yā with its vocative noun, overt or understood, forms a complete performative utterance, equivalent to an invocation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r9.anchor: وهو مع المنادي المنصوب لفظا أو تقديرا به لنيابته عن نحو ناديت الإنشائي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r10.claim: In a vocative, ayy is an indefinite meaning “some of all”; the vocative makes it definite and lets it introduce a noun with the article.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r10.anchor: والواقعة في النداء نكرة موضوعة لبعض من كل ثم تعرفت بالنداء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r11.claim: Yā normally cannot directly precede an al-defined noun other than God, since two definiteness markers like two identical letters do not combine except rarely.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r11.anchor: لا يدخل عليها في غير الله إلا شذوذا لتعذر الجمع بين حرفي التعريف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r12.speaker: المازني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r12.claim: Al-Māzinī permits accusative ayy, but al-Ālūsī rejects this as unsupported by transmitted usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r12.anchor: خلافا للمازني فإنه أجاز نصبه وليس له في ذلك سلف ولا خلف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r13.claim: Ayy takes the vocative’s ḍamma even though its following description is normally subordinate, because the description becomes the intended object of address.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r13.anchor: وأعطيت حكم المنادي وجعل المقصود بالنداء وصفا لها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r14.claim: Unlike ordinary adjectives, this vocative description need not be morphologically derived; it clarifies an ambiguous referent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r14.anchor: ومن هنا لم يشترطوا في هذا الوصف الاشتقاق مع أن النحويين إلا النذر كابن الحاجب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r15.claim: The required hāʾ of attention adds emphasis and compensates for an expected genitive complement or tanwīn, as in the expression ayyāman tadʿū.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r15.anchor: التنبيهية زائدة لازمة للتأكيد والتعويض عما تستحق من المضاف إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r16.claim: The Qur’an often uses this vocative pattern for repeated emphasis, clarification after ambiguity, the attention particle, and two markers of definiteness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r16.anchor: وكثر النداء في الكتاب المجيد على هذه الطريقة لما فيها من التأكيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r17.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r17.claim: Al-Akhfash instead analyzes ayy as a relative pronoun whose clause opening is obligatorily omitted; he cites its frequent relative and rare adjectival uses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r17.anchor: وقطع الأخفش لضعف نظره بأن ( أيا ) الواقعة في النداء موصولة حذف صدر صلتها وجوبا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r18.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r18.claim: On al-Akhfash’s analysis, yā attaches to a form already built on ḍamma and does not alter it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r18.anchor: فحرف النداء على هذا يكون داخلا على مبني على الضم ولم يغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r19.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the majority analysis because it needs no deletion, fits ayy as an adjective, and avoids restrictions on what may follow a relative pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r19.anchor: ويؤيد الأول عدم الاحتياج إلى الحذف وصدق تعريف النعت

ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r20.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that some earlier Arab grammarians found a difficult objection to the majority analysis, but this excerpt does not state the objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p181/r20.anchor: نعم أورد عليه إشكال أستصعبه بعض من سلف من علماء العربية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r1.speaker: أبو نزار
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r1.claim: Abu Nizar treats the final vowel of the vocative’s dependent as built, since no governing عامل can account for an inflectional nominative here.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r1.anchor: أبو نزار أنها ضمة بناء وليست ضمة إعراب لأن ضمة الإعراب لا بد لها من عامل يوجبها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r2.speaker: الشيخ منصور موهوب بن أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r2.claim: Mansur says الناس is genuinely nominative: it describes أي, the actual built vocative, and cannot itself be built as well.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r2.anchor: الشيخ منصور موهوب بن أحمد أنها ضمة إعراب ولا يجوز أن تكون ضمة بناء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r3.speaker: المازني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r3.claim: Al-Mazini allows الناس to take accusative by syntactic position, as in يا زيد الظريف.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r3.anchor: ولهذا أجاز فيه المازني النصب على الموضع كما يجوز في ( يا ) زيد الظزيف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r4.speaker: ابن الشجري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r4.claim: Ibn al-Shajari also regards the vowel as inflectional; the regular vocative damma lies between built forms and ordinary governed inflection, making it analogous to the subject’s semantic عامل.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r4.anchor: ابن الشجري بما أجاب به الشيخ وكتب أنها ضمة إعراب لأن ضمة المنادي المفرد لها بإطرادها منزلة بين منزلتين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r5.speaker: ابن الشجري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r5.claim: Ibn al-Shajari explains that the regular damma of definite vocatives made Arabs analogize it to a nominative subject and raise its descriptive dependent accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r5.anchor: فلما أستمرت ضمة المنادي في معظم الأسماء كما أستمرت في الأسماء المعربة الضمة الحادثة عن الإبتداء شبهتها العرب بضمة المبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r6.speaker: ابن الشجري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r6.claim: He adduces reciprocal vowel-following: a case ending follows a built vowel in one reading of الحمد لله, and a built vowel follows inflection in يا زيد بن عمرو.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r6.anchor: حتى أنهم قد حملوا أشياء على نقائضها ألا ترى أنهم أتبعوا حركة الإعراب حركة البناء في قراءة من قرأ الحمد لله بضم اللام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r7.claim: Al-Alusi considers the preceding grammatical arguments weak; the following discussion gives a different account of the vowel.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p182/r7.anchor: وأنت تعلم ما في ذلك كله من الوهن ولهذا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r1.claim: The majority hold that the article on the vocative’s dependent is the ordinary definite article.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r1.anchor: والذي عليه الجمهور وهو المشهور أنها للتعريف كما تقدمت الإشارة إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r2.speaker: أبو نزار
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r2.claim: Abu Nizar denies that the article marks definiteness; he treats it as compensation for repeated vocative particles, using ها and أل instead.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r2.anchor: أبو نزار قال : إنها هناك ليست للتعريف لأن التعريف لا يكون إلا بين إثنين في ثالث

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r3.speaker: ابن الشجري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r3.claim: Ibn al-Shajari rejects Abu Nizar’s account: the article marks presence, while the vocative itself identifies the addressee, so no third person is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r3.anchor: تعقبه ابن الشجري قائلا : إن هذا قول فاسد بل اللام هناك لتعريف الحضور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r4.speaker: ابن الشجري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r4.claim: Ibn al-Shajari argues that definiteness does not always require a third party; first-person pronouns and direct vocatives are definite without one.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r4.anchor: ليس كل وجوه التعريف يقتضي أن يكون بين إثنين في ثالث فإن ضمير المتكلم في أنا خرجت معرفة إجماعا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r5.speaker: ابن الشجري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r5.claim: He says the compensation theory entails an implausible original form, يا أي يا يا رجل, which ordinary hearing and taste reject.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r5.anchor: وتعقبه ابن الشجري قائلا : إن هذا قول فاسد بل اللام هناك لتعريف الحضور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r6.claim: Al-Alusi identifies الناس as a collective noun and takes its definite form without an external antecedent as general, supported by connected exceptions and emphatic general expressions.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r6.anchor: والناس ( أسم جمع على ما حققه جمع والجموع وأسماؤها المحلاة بالعموم حيث لا عهد خارجي كما يدل عليه وقوع الإستثناء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r7.claim: Most non-Hanbali usul scholars say direct address reaches those present at revelation by its form alone; later people require another proof, such as text, analogy, or consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r7.anchor: هذا الخطاب في نحو ( ياأيها الناس ) يسمى بالخطاب الشفاهي عند الأصوليين قالوا : وليس عاما لمن بعد الموجودين في زمن الوحي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r8.claim: They argue that absent people cannot literally be addressed; children and the insane are also not addressed, and al-Adud calls denial of this self-evident.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r8.anchor: قال العضد : وإنكاره مكابرة وبأنه أمتنع خطاب الصبي والمجنون بنحوه وإذا لم نوجهه نحوهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r9.speaker: الحنابلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r9.claim: The Hanbalis hold that the address is general through the Day of Resurrection, citing the Prophet’s mission to later people and scholars’ continuing use of it as proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r9.anchor: وقالت الحنابلة : بل هو عام لمن بعدهم إلى يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r10.claim: The reply is that conveying a message does not require face-to-face address, and later scholars may rely on separate proof that the same rule applies to later generations.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183/r10.anchor: وأجيب : أما عن الأول فبأن الرسالة إنما تستدعي التبليغ في الجملة وهو لا يتوقف على المشافهة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r1.claim: خلق means origination without a model, exclusive to God, or can mean estimation, a sense applicable to others as in the cited examples.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r1.anchor: والخلق الإختراع بلا مثال ويكون بمعنى التقدير وعلى الأول لا يتصف به سواه سبحانه وعلى الثاني قد يتصف به غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r2.speaker: العلامة الثاني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r2.claim: Al-Allama al-Thani says the view that direct address is general, though attributed to the Hanbalis, is not far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r2.anchor: في شرح العلامة الثاني للشرح العضدي أن القول بعموم الشفاهي وإن نسب إلى الحنابلة ليس ببعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r3.speaker: بعض أجلة المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r3.claim: Some eminent investigators call generality the well-known view, even a necessary part of Muhammadan religion; Al-Alusi calls it the nearer position.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أجلة المحققين : إنه المشهور حتى قالوا إن الحق أن العموم معلوم بالضرورة من الدين المحمدي وهو الأقرب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r4.speaker: بعض أجلة المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r4.claim: They answer al-Adud that denying address to absent people is obstinacy only if they alone are addressed; present and absent may be included by common, eloquent predominance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r4.anchor: وقول العضد : إن إنكاره مكابرة حق لو كان الخطاب للمعدومين خاصة أما إذا كان للموجودين والمعدومين على طريق التغليب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r5.speaker: كثير من الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r5.claim: Many Shafiites say the address is general to later people in its literal wording and explicit meaning, without needing separate evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r5.anchor: وإلى العموم ذهب كثير من الشافعية على أنه عندهم عام بحاق لفظه ومنطوقه من غير احتياج إلى دليل آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r6.claim: A general address used beyond its apparent scope is compared with the cited verse-like poetic maxim about honoring the noble and the base.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r6.anchor: وقد قيل : إنه من قبيل الخطاب العام الذي أجرى على غير ظاهره كما في قوله : إذا أنت أكرمت الكريم ملكته وإن أنت أكرمت اللئيم تمردا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود وعلقمة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Masud and Alqama says passages beginning يا أيها الناس are Meccan and those beginning يا أيها الذين آمنوا are Medinan; even if sound, it does not exclude unbelievers from this address.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r7.anchor: ما روى عن ابن مسعود وعلقمة من أن كل شيء نزل فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r8.speaker: العراقيون والشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r8.claim: The Iraqis and Shafiites hold that unbelievers are also commanded to perform religious duties, including worship and belief, since commanding an act includes what is necessary to perform it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r8.anchor: وهذا ماذهب إليه العراقيون والشافعية ويؤيده ظواهر الآيات كقوله تعالى :

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r9.speaker: العراقيون والشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r9.claim: They cite the rebuke of polytheists for withholding zakat and the sinners’ admission that they did not pray or feed the poor.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r9.anchor: قوله تعالى : ( وويل للمشركين الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة ) وقوله سبحانه : ( ما سلككم في سقر قالوا لم نك من المصلين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r10.speaker: البخاريون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r10.claim: The scholars of Bukhara hold that unbelievers are obligated only concerning belief.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r10.anchor: وذهب البخاريون إلى أنهم مكلفون في حق الإعتقاد فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r11.claim: Abu Hanifa made no explicit statement on whether unbelievers owe ritual duties, though his second companion’s words suggest a position; the dispute affects afterlife punishment, not worldly practice or make-up duties after conversion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r11.anchor: وأبو حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه لم ينص ظاهرا على شيء في المسألة لكن في كلام صاحبه الثاني ما يدل عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r12.claim: Both sides agree that unbelievers are addressed by rules on punishments and transactions; while they remain unbelievers they cannot perform rituals, and after conversion need not make them up.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r12.anchor: وهذا في غير العقوبات والمعاملات أما هي فمتفق على خطابهم بها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r13.claim: The command can address unbelievers as beginning worship, some believers as increasing it, and others as continuing it; those nuances are not part of the word’s lexical meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r13.anchor: فأعبدوا يدل على طلب في الحال لعبادة مستقلة وهي من الكفار ابتداء عبادة ومن بعض المؤمنين زيادة ومن آخرين مواظبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r14.claim: Calling God their Lord points to the immediate motive for worship: His nurturing grace, although perfected worship is offered for God’s own essence without an intermediary motive.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r14.anchor: وذكر سبحانه الرب ليشير إلى أن الموجب القريب للعبادة هي نعمة التربية وإن كانت عبادة الكاملين لذاته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r15.claim: The relative clause describing the Lord is laudatory and can also explain the grounds of worship or lordship; its force depends on whether ربكم addresses all groups or only polytheists.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p183#2/r15.anchor: الموصول صفة مادحة للرب وفيها أيضا تعليل العبادة أو الربوبية على ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r1.claim: Zuhayr’s line contrasts one who creates what he measures with people who may measure but fail to carry it through, illustrating the second sense of خلق.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r1.anchor: بعض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفرى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r2.speaker: أبو عبدالله البصري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r2.claim: Abu Abdullah al-Basri says calling God Creator is impossible because estimation requires thought and conjecture.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r2.anchor: ومن العجب أن أبا عبدالله البصري أستاذ القاضي عبدالجبار قال : إطلاق الخالق عليه تعالى محال لأن التقدير يستدعي الفكر والحسبان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r3.claim: Al-Alusi rejects al-Basri’s claim by appealing to God’s own description of Himself as Creator and Originator.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r3.anchor: القائل : ( هو الخالق الباريء ) وبقول الله تعالى أقول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r4.claim: The second relative pronoun is coordinated with the object of خلقكم; قبل is usually temporal, less often spatial, and can figuratively mean precedence in rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r4.anchor: والموصول الثاني عطف على المنصوب في ( خلقكم ) وقبل ظرف زمان بكثرة ومكان بقلة ويتجوز بها عن التقدم بالشرف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r5.claim: If the address includes believers and unbelievers, those before them are earlier beings and those still present who outrank them; this recalls God’s majesty and reinforces worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r5.anchor: فالمراد بالذين قبلهم من تقدمهم في الوجود ومن هو موجود وهو أعلى منزلة منهم وفي هذا تذكير لكمال جلال الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r6.claim: The audience’s own creation is mentioned first despite being later in time because people know themselves most directly and are the ones commanded to worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r6.anchor: وقدم سبحانه التنبيه على خلقهم وإن كان متأخرا بالزمان لأن علم الإنسان بأحوال نفسه أظهر ولأنهم المواجهون بالأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r7.claim: A relative clause must describe an attribution already known to its audience; the wording therefore assumes they know Allah created them, as the cited verses confirm.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r7.anchor: والصلات لابد من كونها معلومة الإنتساب عند المخاطب ولذا يعرف الموصول عنده بما فيها من العهد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r8.claim: If some hearers do not know Allah created them, the wording either uses general predominance or treats them as knowing because the proofs are clear, phrasing the sentence contrary to the apparent situation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r8.anchor: وإن كان هناك من لا يعلم أن الله تعالى خالقه وخالق من قبله احتيج إلى ادعاء التغليب أو تنزيل غير العالم منزلة العالم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r9.speaker: ابن السميقع
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r9.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa reads وَخَلَقَ مَن قَبْلَكُمْ, replacing the relative construction with a verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r9.anchor: وقرأ إبن السميقع وخلق من قبلكم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r10.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r10.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads the phrase with fatḥa on the mīm, as the source specifies.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r10.anchor: وزيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما والذين من قبلكم بفتح الميم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r11.claim: One analysis makes من an emphatic appositive to الذين, but critics object that a relative pronoun, like a particle, is not normally reinforced without repeating its connector.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r11.anchor: وأعترض بأن الحرف لا يؤكد بدون إعادة ما أتصل به فالموصول أولى بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r12.claim: Another analysis makes من relative or descriptive, with an omitted subject and following clause completing the first relative; a cited poetic construction is offered as a parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r12.anchor: فمن حينئذ موصولة أو موصوفة وهي خبر مبتدأ مقدر وما بعدها صلة أو صفة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r13.claim: Some object that the familiar reading leaves الذين and من قبلكم without a useful predicate; the next discussion supplies an analysis of the temporal phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p184/r13.anchor: وبعضهم أستشكل القراءة المشهورة أيضا بأن الذين أعيان و ( من قبلكم ) ناقص ليس في الأخبار به عنها فائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r1.claim: A temporal phrase can serve as predicate or relative clause when described explicitly or implicitly with contextual support; here the estimate is people from a time before yours.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r1.anchor: في يوم طيب وماهنا في تقدير والذين كانوا من زمان قبل زمانكم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa estimates الذين خلقهم من قبل خلقكم, omitting the relative verb and placing its temporal complement in its stead.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r2.anchor: وقدر أبو البقاء والذين خلقهم من قبل خلقكم فحذف الفعل الذي هو صلة وأقيم متعلقه مقامه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r3.claim: The common account gives لعل hope for a possible desired event or apprehension of a possible feared event; because these seem opposed, لعل is treated as having two senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r3.anchor: لعلفي المشهور موضوعة للترجي وهو الطمع في حصول أمر محبوب ممكن الوقوع والإشفاق وهو توقع مخوف ممكن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r4.speaker: الرضى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r4.claim: Al-Radi defines لعل as expectation without certainty, broad enough to include both hope and apprehension.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r4.anchor: وذكر الرضى إنها للترجي وهو ارتقاب شيء لا وثوق بحصوله فيدخل فيه الطمع والإشفاق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r5.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r5.claim: Al-Alusi leans toward investigators who define لعل as expressing expectation between occurrence and nonoccurrence, with occurrence more likely; a good event is hope, a bad one apprehension.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r5.anchor: والذي يميل إليه القلب ما ذكره بعض المحققين إنها لا نشاء توقع أمر متردد بين الوقوع وعدمه مع رجحان الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r6.claim: Expectation may be actual in the speaker, commonly, or in the addressee treated as fully engaged in the exchange; it may also be potential by figurative extension without any actual expectant.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r6.anchor: وذلك قد يعتبر تحققه بالفعل إما من جهة المتكلم وهو الشائع لأن معاني الإنشاآت قائمة به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r7.claim: If the clause is circumstantial of those created, لعل cannot be literal: God cannot be uncertain, and humans could not hope while being created; the prospective state then was taqwa, not hope for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r7.anchor: امتنع حمل لعل على حقيقتها لا بالنظر إلى المتكلم لاستحالة الترجي على عالم الغيب والشهادة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r8.claim: On that parsing, figurative readings include a dependent metaphor, a representational metaphor comparing the Creator’s relation to capable people with a hoper’s relation to someone able to act, or a metaphor treating people as hoped-for pious.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r8.anchor: فلا بد أن يحمل على المعنى المجازي بأن يشبه طلب التقوى منهم بعد اجتماع أسبابه ودواعيه بالترجي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r9.claim: Making God’s will the object of the metaphor is a Muʿtazilite tendency built on the premise that His will may fail to occur.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p185/r9.anchor: وجعل المشبه إرادته تعالى في الاستعارة والتمثيل نزغة إعتزالية مؤسسة على القاعدة القائلة بجواز تخلف المراد عن إرادته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r1.claim: If لعل is a circumstantial phrase of the subject of خلقكم, it is still not literal; some place expectation in an outside observer, since every child is born on the natural disposition and may become pious.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r1.anchor: قال بالترجي هنا إلا أنه ليس من المتكلم ولا من المخاطب بل من غيرهما كما في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r2.claim: If لعل modifies the command to worship, it can retain literal expectation addressed to people: they worship hoping for taqwa, the highest spiritual station of abandoning desire and all but God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r2.anchor: وإن جعلت حالا من ضمير ( أعبدوا ) جاز إبقاء الترجي على حقيقته مصروفا إلى المخاطبين أي راجين التقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r3.claim: This reading makes taqwa a compelling goal and answers the objection that Qur’anic eloquence should foreground reward rather than the hardship of piety, since taqwa leads to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r3.anchor: وبذلك يصح الترغيب ويندفع ما قيل إن اللائق بالبلاغة القرآنية أن يعتبر من أول الأمر غاية عبادتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r4.speaker: التفتازاني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r4.claim: Al-Taftazani objects that qualifying worship with hope for taqwa adds little meaning; al-Alusi replies that hope teaches worshippers not to slacken and to keep fear and hope.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r4.anchor: وما قاله المولى التفتازاني من أن تقييد العبادة بترجي التقوى ليس له كثير معنى إنما المناسب تقييدها بالتقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r5.claim: If the circumstantial phrase qualifies an imperative understood as obligatory, it may seem to make hope obligatory too; whether obligation of the qualified act entails obligation of its qualifier is an usul dispute.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r5.anchor: قالوا : الحال قيد لعاملها وهو هنا الأمر فإن قلنا : إنه أعم من الوجوب فلا إشكال وإن قلنا : إنه حقيقة في الوجوب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r6.claim: The long interruption objection can be eased by treating the following phrase as parenthetical, or by making الذي the subject with فلا تجعلوا as predicate; this parsing remains less likely despite al-Baydawi’s apparent preference.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r6.anchor: ومع هذا لا شك في مرجوحية هذا الوجه وإن أشعر كلام مولانا البيضاوي بأرجحيته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari and others allow لعل to mean كي, ‘so that,’ citing a line in which a speaker says they were trusted to stop fighting.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r7.anchor: كما ذهب إليه إبن الأنباري وغيره وأستشهدوا بقوله : فقلتم لنا كفوا الحروب لعلنا نكف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r8.claim: Alternatively, hope can imply that what follows is certain by the convention that a great person’s expressed hope signals fulfillment, then extend to any certain outcome.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r8.anchor: لأنها للأطماع فيكنى به بقرينة المقام عن تحقق ما بعدها على عادة الكبراء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r9.claim: Al-Alusi says God’s acts are truly guided by the interests of His servants, though God is not obliged to do what is best; denying purposes even in legal rulings nearly denies prophecy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r9.anchor: الحق الذي لا محيص عنه أن أفعاله تعالى معللة بمصالح العباد مع أنه سبحانه لا يجب عليه الأصلح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r10.speaker: صدر الشريعة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r10.claim: Sadr al-Sharia is cited as saying that denying purpose in some divine acts, especially legal rulings such as penalties, comes close to denying prophecy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r10.anchor: ومن أنكر تعليل بعض الأفعال لا سيما الأحكام الشرعية كالحدود فقد كاد أن ينكر النبوة كما قاله مولانا صدر الشريعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r11.claim: The dispute over causal purposes may be verbal: purpose as something God depends on for perfection is impossible, while wisdom that outwardly guides action despite divine self-sufficiency is plainly real.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r11.anchor: لأن العلة إن فسرت بما يتوقف عليه ويستكمل به الفاعل امتنع ذلك في حقه سبحانه وإن فسرت بالحكمة المقتضية للفعل ظاهرا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r12.claim: Some say the matching forms at the beginning and end create rhetorical return, and taqwa as worship’s ultimate end makes the command more compelling; al-Alusi expresses some reservation about this explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r12.anchor: لأن التقوى قصارى أمر العابد فيكون الكلام أبعث على العبادة وأشد إلزاما كذا قيل وفي القلب منه شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas supplies shirk as the omitted object of تتقون.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r13.anchor: وابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه يقدره الشرك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r14.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak supplies the Fire as the omitted object of تتقون.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r15.claim: Because the Lord is distinguished by creating and nurturing, the verse points to reflection on God’s works as the route to knowing His oneness and right to worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r15.anchor: أشعرت الآية أن طريق معرفته تعالى والعلم بوحدانيته واستحقاقه العبادة النظر في صنعه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r16.claim: Since creation and nurture precede the command to worship, the servant cannot claim to deserve reward: prior blessings are countless and human worship cannot repay even a fraction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r16.anchor: فهم أن العبد لا يستحق ثوابا حيث أنعم عليه قبل العبادة بما لا يحصى مما لا تفي الطاقة البشرية بشكره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r17.claim: Some use the command to worship despite prior statements that people will not believe as evidence that moral responsibility can include the impossible; al-Alusi refers back to his earlier discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p186/r17.anchor: واستدل بالآية من زعم أن التكليف بالمحال واقع حيث أمر سبحانه بعبادته من آمن به ومن كفر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says “O people” addresses Meccans, while “O you who believe” addresses Medinans; here the address is general except for children and the insane.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يا أيها الناس خطاب أهل مكة، ويا أيها الذين آمنوا خطاب أهل المدينة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r2.claim: The address here is general, excluding only children and the insane.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r2.anchor: وهو هاهنا عام إلا من حيث إنه لا يدخله الصغار والمجانين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says that every occurrence of worship in the Quran means affirming God's oneness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: كل ما ورد في القرآن من العبادة فمعناها التوحيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r4.claim: Creation is bringing something into being without a prior example.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r4.anchor: والخلق: اختراع الشيء على غير مثال سبق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r5.claim: The phrase means that God also created those who came before you.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r6.claim: One explanation is that worship lets you escape punishment; another takes laʿalla as hope that you become protected from God's punishment, while God's decree remains sovereign.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r6.anchor: لكي تنجوا من العذاب وقيل معناه كونوا على رجاء التقوى بأن تصيروا في ستر ووقاية من عذاب الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r7.claim: The hopeful sense of laʿalla parallels Moses and Aaron being told to speak gently to Pharaoh at 20:44; Sibawayh says laʿalla and ʿasā express hope, but when used of God the promised outcome is certain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p71#2/r7.anchor: قال سيبويه: لعل وعسى حرفا ترج وهما من الله واجب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r1.claim: After listing the accountable groups and their traits, the discourse turns to direct address to startle and enliven the listener, stress worship's importance, magnify it, and ease its burden through the pleasure of being addressed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r1.anchor: لما عدد فرق المكلفين وذكر خواصهم ومصارف أمورهم، أقبل عليهم بالخطاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r2.claim: Yā normally calls someone distant but may address someone near as distant because of majesty, inattention or poor understanding, or to give the call greater emphasis and urgency.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r2.anchor: و (يا) حرف وضع لنداء البعيد، وقد ينادي به القريب تنزيلا له منزلة البعيد.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r3.claim: The vocative and its particle form a meaningful clause because they stand in place of a verb. Ay bridges yā and a noun with al-, takes vocative status, and is clarified by the raised hādhā-like address; the inserted hā alerts and reinforces.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r3.anchor: وأي: جعل وصلة إلى نداء المعرف باللام، فإن إدخال «يا» عليه متعذر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r4.claim: Definite plurals without a prior referent are general, as shown by the validity of exception and emphatic generalizers; the address covers people present at revelation and those yet to come under the Prophet's enduring law, except where evidence specifies otherwise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r4.anchor: والجموع وأسماؤها المحلاة باللام للعموم حيث لا عهد، ويدل عليه صحة الاستثناء منها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r5.speaker: علقمة والحسن
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r5.claim: A report attributed to ʿAlqama and al-Ḥasan says every address beginning yā ayyuhā al-nās is Meccan and yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū is Medinan; Bayḍāwī says even if soundly raised to the Prophet, it does not restrict this command to unbelievers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r5.anchor: وما روي عن علقمة والحسن أن كل شيء نزل فيه { يا أيها الناس } فمكي

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r6.claim: The command addresses both unbelievers and believers: unbelievers must begin worship after the prerequisite knowledge and acknowledgment of the Creator, while believers must increase and persevere in worship; disbelief does not remove its obligation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r6.anchor: فإن المأمور به هو القدر المشترك بين بدء العبادة، والزيادة فيها، والمواظبة عليها،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r7.claim: Calling God their Lord points to lordship as the reason worship is obligatory.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21/r7.anchor: وإنما قال: { ربكم } تنبيها على أن الموجب للعبادة هي الربوبية.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r1.claim: Alladhī is an attributive clause adding grandeur and explaining the reason for worship; if the addressees are specifically polytheists and rabb is taken broadly, it can instead distinguish the true Lord from their supposed lords.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r1.anchor: صفة جرت عليه تعالى للتعظيم والتعليل، ويحتمل التقييد والتوضيح إن خص الخطاب بالمشركين،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r2.claim: Khalq means bringing something into existence proportioned and well-formed; its original sense is measuring, as in measuring and shaping a sandal to its dimensions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r2.anchor: والخلق إيجاد الشيء على تقدير واستواء، وأصله التقدير يقال: خلق النعل إذا قدرها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r3.claim: Those before you includes everyone who precedes human beings essentially or in time; grammatically the phrase is accusative, coordinated with the object pronoun in khalaqakum.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r3.anchor: متناول كل ما يتقدم الإنسان بالذات أو بالزمان.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r4.claim: Their creation is stated as something the audience acknowledges, as in 43:87, or can know by minimal reflection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r4.anchor: والجملة أخرجت مخرج المقرر عندهم، إما لاعترافهم به كما قال الله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r5.claim: A reading repeats the relative pronoun in min qablikum, inserting it between the first relative pronoun and its clause for emphasis; Jarīr's repeated Taym in his line illustrates the construction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء { من قبلكم } على إقحام الموصول الثاني بين الأول وصلته تأكيدا، كما أقحم جرير في قوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r1.claim: Laʿallakum tattaqūn may be circumstantial to the subject of worship: worship hoping to join the Godfearing, attain guidance and success, and merit God's presence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r1.anchor: حال من الضمير في { اعبدوا } كأنه قال: اعبدوا ربكم راجين أن تنخرطوا في سلك المتقين

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r2.claim: Taqwā is the wayfarer's highest degree: turning from everything besides God toward Him. A worshipper should not be self-satisfied but should combine fear and hope.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r2.anchor: نبه به على أن التقوى منتهى درجات السالكين وهو التبري من كل شيء سوى الله تعالى إلى الله، وأن العابد ينبغي

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial to the objects of creation: God created the addressees and their predecessors in a state where taqwā is hoped for because its causes and incentives are abundant; the spoken addressees stand for all.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r3.anchor: أو من مفعول { خلقكم } والمعطوف عليه على معنى أنه خلقكم ومن قبلكم في صورة من يرجى منه التقوى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r4.claim: One interpretation makes taqwa the purpose of creation, connecting the verse to 51:56, but Bayḍāwī calls it weak because this use lacks a linguistic parallel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r4.anchor: وقيل تعليل للخلق أي خلقكم لكي تتقوا كما قال: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r5.claim: The verse teaches that knowledge of God, His oneness, and His exclusive right to worship is reached by examining His works and reasoning from His acts.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r5.anchor: والآية تدل على أن الطريق إلى معرفة الله تعالى والعلم بوحدانيته واستحقاقه للعبادة، النظر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r6.claim: A servant earns no entitlement to reward through worship: worship is already owed in gratitude for prior blessings, like a worker paid before doing the work.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:21#3/r6.anchor: فإنها لما وجبت عليه شكرا لما عدده عليه من النعم السابقة فهو كأجير أخذ الأجر قبل العمل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.claim: The two verses command worship and forbid associating partners, then give their rationale: lordship grounds worship; God created people, their ancestors, and necessities of life, and these uniquely divine provisions witness His oneness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:22#4/r3.anchor: واعلم إن مضمون الآيتين هو الأمر بعبادة الله سبحانه وتعالى، والنهي عن الإشراك به تعالى،

BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r3.claim: After describing the two disbelieving groups and their state, the argument for divine oneness entails exclusive worship; the call now directly addresses people because the preceding discourse has qualified them for direct address.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r3.anchor: للواحدانية أنتج قطعا إفراده بالعباده الموجبه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r4.claim: Harali explains yā as alerting a hearer to attend; ayy is an indefinite whose referent is specified, and hā further signals the matter to be learned.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي في تفسيره { يا } تنبيه من يكون بمسمع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r5.claim: The layered call uses ambiguity, alert, and explicit identification to stress that the ensuing matters are important and demand earnest effort.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r5.anchor: وأكد سبحانه الكلام بالإبهام والتنبيه والتوضيح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r6.claim: Harali says each sura has a comprehensive title that gathers its repeated verses and a conclusion integrated with that title; a sura can summarize several suras.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r6.anchor: جعل لكل سورة ترجمة جامعة تحتوي على جميع مثاني آيها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r7.claim: Harali distinguishes the hamzated prophet as one informed by news from the unhamzated form, derived from elevation and high rank.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r8.claim: Unlike other prophets, Muhammad was given advance knowledge of his people’s divinely decreed outcomes: some are naturally receptive, some sealed in disbelief, and some outwardly believe while inwardly disbelieving; each is enabled for its created end.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r9.claim: The sequence moves from explaining alif-lām-mīm, through the Book’s three classes of addressees, to the general call to all people in this verse.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r9.anchor: فكان أول ما افتتح له كتابه أن عرفه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r10.claim: God Himself delivers this universal call: its warning and royal severity would not suit Muhammad’s merciful mission, whereas God cannot be resisted, so the form promises victory and the religion’s manifestation; the speech returns to the Prophet at the mercy of glad tidings.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p53/r10.anchor: وتولى الله سبحانه دعوة الخلق في هذه الدعوة العامة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r1.claim: Earlier messengers call people to worship Allah, a name difficult for many minds to grasp; this divine call uses Lord, nearer through observable acts of nurture, making the signs accessible to sense and reason and easing response.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r1.anchor: ومع إجراء دعوة المرسلين على ألسنتهم علقت باسم الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r2.claim: The command addresses both those whose worship was corrupted by shirk or otherwise and those continuing sound worship, since increasing and persisting in true worship is itself a fresh act of worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r2.anchor: العبادة المختلة بشرك أو غيره ساقطة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r3.claim: The Lord is the only Lord of the people; describing Him as their creator shows His beneficence and their duty to worship Him in gratitude.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r3.anchor: أي الذي لا رب لكم غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r4.claim: Harali defines the relative pronoun as an initially unspecified entity identified by its following description, creation as the shaping of mixed elements into form, and those before you by their relation to the point of origin.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r4.anchor: قا لالحرالي : { الذي } اسم مبهم مدلوله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r5.claim: The intended result of worship is a hoped-for state of taqwa: avoiding what is blameworthy out of fear of God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r5.anchor: ولا حسن في غيرها حال من ترجى له التقوى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r6.claim: Harali treats laʿalla as hope grounded in what precedes; beginning with human creation and extending to earlier generations makes people attribute both their origin and their resulting traits and actions to God, so they cease self-sufficiency and develop taqwa.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p54/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : لعل كلمة ترج لما تقدم سببه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r1.claim: The servant's fulfillment of the station taught by this passage is associated with the address to the tranquil soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r1.anchor: ويتأكد تحلي العبد بمستحق أوصافه لقراءة هذا الحرف والعمل به

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r2.claim: Reading and practicing the decisive teaching requires avoiding ambiguous matters, whose pursuit reflects the limits of reason; believers affirm them without comparing divine address with human inference.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r2.anchor: لأن اتباع المتشابه زيغ لقصور العقل والفهم عن نيله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r3.claim: God has made the recognition of Him possible only through acknowledging that He cannot be fully known.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r3.anchor: سبحانه من لم يجعل سبيلا إلى معرفته إلا بالعجز عن معرفته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r4.claim: The decisive teaching is joined to the opening revelation, “Read in your Lord's name,” and to the first command in the Qur'an's arrangement to worship the Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r4.anchor: وجامع منزل المحكم ما افتتح به التنزيل في قوله تعالى :

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r5.claim: Worship of the heart is knowledge of God; the call first directs people to worship, then to know Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r5.anchor: إلى ما ينتظم بذلك من ذكر عبادة القلب التي هي المعرفة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r6.claim: Worship of the soul consists in patient steadfastness and good recompense; a humbled heart would make the limbs humble as well.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r6.anchor: ومن ذكر عبادة النفس التي هي الإجمال في الصبر وحسن الجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r7.claim: The commands, prohibitions, lawful, and unlawful regulate outward conduct and worldly or future affairs; the deeper teaching is exclusive loyalty to God and servitude to Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r7.anchor: وما تقدم من حرفي الحلال والحرام لإصلاح الدنيا , وحرفي الأمر والنهي لإصلاح العقبى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r8.claim: Unlike outward observances that a hypocrite can imitate, knowledge, humility, longing for God, acceptance of decree, and love belong to sincere servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59/r8.anchor: وليس يمكنه مع نفاقه التحلي بالمعرفة , ولا بالخشوع ولا بالخضوع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r1.claim: The description of the Merciful's servants and the assurance that Satan has no authority over God's servants exemplify those who embody the decisive teaching.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.claim: Because the decisive teaching accords with the servant's created nature and relation to God, it remains constant across religions and revealed laws.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r2.anchor: ولما كان حرف المحكم مستحق العبد في حق الرب في فطرته التي فطر عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.claim: The decisive verses are the Mother of the Book, containing the four other modes that vary, abrogate one another, and differ among legal communities.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r3.anchor: فكانت آياته لذلك هن أم الكتاب المشتمل على الأحرف الأربعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.claim: Those who act on the decisive teaching are guided people of the Sunna and community; following ambiguous verses produces sectarian division, innovations, and misguidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r4.anchor: وقرأته العملة به هم المهتدون أهل السنة والجماعة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r5.claim: The decisive teaching brings unity and guidance, while the ambiguous teaching brings division and error.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r5.anchor: فحرف المحكم للاجتماع والهدى , وحرف المتشابه للافتراق والضلال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.claim: Ordinary believers receive the four earlier modes of worship, while those fully realized in servitude know themselves as property of the Master, without a claim against Him even in assigning bliss or misery.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r6.anchor: قراءة الأحرف الماضية الأربعة هو حظ العامة من الأمة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.claim: From the heart, this teaching means recognizing creation's dependence in existence, provision, and divine direction: creatures possess no independent power, and surrender all inward and outward affairs to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p59#2/r7.anchor: لا يملك لنفسه ضرا ولا نفعا ولا موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r1.claim: The servant's truthful religion is Islam; rational reflection and a purified inner core lead to Abraham's upright faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r1.anchor: وما يتحقق للعبد من ذلك عن اعتبار العقل وخلوص اللب هي الملة الحنيفية ملة النبي الخليل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r2.claim: The soul's proper state is servile humility, gentleness, and freedom from pride over other creatures; this produces good conduct with people and truthful worship of God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r2.anchor: جماع ذلك وأصله الذل وانكسارا والذل عطفا والبراءة من الترفع والفخر على سائر الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r3.claim: The limbs complete Islam by submitting to God in speech, action, and giving, while keeping other people safe from tongue and hand.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r3.anchor: وإما من جهة العمل فتصرف الجوارح وإسلامها لله قولا وفعلا وبذلا , ومسالمة الخلق لسانا ويدا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r4.claim: The text states that a person is not counted among Muslims until people are safe from his tongue and hand; it gives no transmitter or grading.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r4.anchor: لا يكتب أحدكم في المسلمين حتى يسلم الناس من لسانه ويده

BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r5.claim: Prayer's lowered gaze and the right hand placed over the left at the chest express a servant waiting respectfully for an unknown command from the master.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r5.anchor: كالذي بنيت عليه هيئة الصلاة من الإطراق في القيام ووضع اليمنى على اليسرى بحذاء الصدر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r6.claim: The Prophet sat for food in the humble posture of a servant and said, “I am a servant; I eat as a servant eats.”
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r6.anchor: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يجلس لطعامه ليستوي حال تعبده في أمر دنياه وأخراه ويقول : ( إنما أنا عبد آكل كما يأكل العبد )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r7.claim: Following the Prophet, as commanded in 3:31, joins realization of servitude in the heart, humility of the soul, and submission of the limbs.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p60/r7.anchor: فبهذه الأمور من تحقق العبودية للقلب وذل النفس وانكسار الجوارح تحصل قراءة حرف المحكم

DURR-FULL:v1p83/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p83/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p83/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says Quranic addresses to humankind are Meccan, while addresses to believers are Medinan.
DURR-FULL:v1p83/r12.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: ما كان (يا أيها الذين آمنوا) أنزل بالمدينة وما كان {يا أيها الناس} فبمكة

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Mufaṣṣal was recited in Mecca without any address beginning O you who believe.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قرأنا المفصل ونحن بمكة حجيجا ليس فيها (يا أيها الذين آمنوا)

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r2.speaker: علقمة
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r2.claim: ʿAlqama says every Quranic address to humankind is Meccan and every address to believers is Medinan.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r2.anchor: عن علقمة قال: كل شيء في القرآن {يا أيها الناس} فهو مكي وكل شيء في القرآن (يا أيها الذين آمنوا) فإنه مدني

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk is reported giving the same Meccan and Medinan distinction for the two forms of address.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن مردويه وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن الضحاكمثله

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r4.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r4.claim: Maymūn ibn Mihrān says addresses to humankind and to the children of Adam are Meccan, while addresses to believers are Medinan.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r4.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران قال: ماكان في القرآن {يا أيها الناس} ويابني آدم فإنه مكي

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r5.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r5.claim: ʿUrwa likewise assigns O humankind to Mecca and O believers to Medina.

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r6.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r6.claim: ʿUrwa says pilgrimage, obligatory duties, legal punishments, and jihad were revealed in Medina; accounts of peoples and generations and parables were revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r6.anchor: عن عروة قال: ما كان من حج أو فريضة فإنه نزل بالمدينة أو حد أو جهاد

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r7.claim: ʿIkrima says every sura containing O you who believe is Medinan.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: كل سورة فيها (يا أيها الذين آمنوا) فهي مدنيه

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the address O humankind includes both disbelievers and believers.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس فيقوله {يا أيها الناس} فهي للفريقين جميعا من الكفار والمؤمنين

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses worship as affirming God's oneness.
