DURR-FULL:v1p84/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس فيقوله {يا أيها الناس} فهي للفريقين جميعا من الكفار والمؤمنين {اعبدوا} قال: وحدوا

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r10.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r10.claim: Al-Suddī explains the creator of you and those before you to mean that He created you and those who preceded you.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r10.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم} يقول: خلقكم وخلق الذين من قبلكم

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r11.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r11.claim: Abū Mālik glosses laʿalla as so that, except at 26:129 where it means as though you would live forever.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r11.anchor: عن أبي مالك قوله {لعلكم} يعني كي غير آية في الشعراء (لعلكم تخلدون) (الشعراء 129) يعني كأنكم تخلدون

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r12.speaker: عون بن عبد الله بن غنية
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r12.claim: ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghunya says that when laʿalla is used by God, its result is certain.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r12.anchor: عن عون بن عبد الله بن غنية قال {لعل} من الله واجب

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r13.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r13.claim: Mujāhid glosses the purpose clause as so that you obey.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {لعلكم تتقون} قال: تطعيون

DURR-FULL:v1p84/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r14.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r14.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains the purpose as so that you may fear the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v1p84/r14.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {لعلكم تتقون} قال: تتقون النار

IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says “O people” addresses both groups, unbelievers and hypocrites.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : يا ايها الناس اي الفريقين جميعا من الكفار والمنافقين

IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains worshiping the Lord as affirming His oneness.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r2.anchor: وبه عن ابن عباس : قوله يا ايها الناس اعبدوا ربكم اي وحدوا ربكم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r3.speaker: السدي ومجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi, with a similar report from Mujahid, says God created you and those before you.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r3.anchor: عن السدى : يا ايها الناس اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم يقول : خلقكم وخلق الذين من قبلكم . وروى عن مجاهد نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r4.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r4.claim: Abu Malik explains laʿallakum in the cited phrase as “as though you will remain forever.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي مالك . قوله : لعلكم يعني غير آية في الشعراء لعلكم تخلدون يعني كانكم تخلدون .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the purpose is that people may guard themselves from the Fire through the five prayers.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : لعلكم تتقون قال : يقول : لعلكم تتقون النار بالصلوات الخمس .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as “so that you may obey Him.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p59#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد : لعلكم تتقون لعلكم تطيعونه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r1.claim: After describing believers and their opponents, the passage begins an address suited to every group, extending guidance and mercy despite their misconduct.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r1.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي ثني به العنان إلى موعظة كل فريق من الفرق الأربع المتقدم ذكرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r2.claim: The general address reassures people after threats and blame: divine severity aims at reform, like a mentor who rebukes then gently restores the pupil's spirits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r2.anchor: ففيه تأنيس لأنفسهم بعد أن هددهم ولامهم وذم صنعهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r3.claim: The consolation increases the good in the righteous and turns wrongdoers from misconduct, so each previously described group receives its share of the address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r3.anchor: الإقبال على موعظة نبذ الشرك وذلك هو غالب اصطلاح القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r4.claim: In Quranic usage, O people chiefly introduces an exhortation to abandon polytheism; the prohibition of rivals in 2:22 confirms the aim, and the vocative dignifies the address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r4.anchor: قوله : { فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r5.claim: يا is the most frequent vocative particle and the default form; when a vocative particle is omitted, no other one is implicitly supplied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p323#2/r5.anchor: حرف للنداء وهو أكثر حروف النداء استعمالا فهو أصل حروف النداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r1.claim: Legislative addresses are not limited like ordinary speech to whoever is physically present; hearers are directly obligated, while later generations receive the address as information, analogously to legal theory on commands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن خطابات التشريع ونحوها غير جارية على المعروف في توجه الخطاب في أصل اللغات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r2.claim: Worship originally means abasement and submission; Ibn Ashur had discussed the term under 1:5.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r2.anchor: عند قوله تعالى : { إياك نعبد } ( الفاتحة : 5 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r3.claim: True submission requires certainty, so belief in God and exclusive divine unity are the beginning of worship; associating an unworthy partner undermines submission to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r3.anchor: ولما كان التذلل والخضوع إنما يحصل عن صدق اليقين كان الإيمان بالله وتوحيده بالإلاهية مبدأ العبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r4.claim: The address includes Arab polytheists, materialists, People of the Book, and believers, each according to their duty: affirm the Creator, God's unity, the Messenger, Islam, and continued obedience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r4.anchor: فالمخاطب بالأمر بالعبادة المشركون من العرب والدهريون منهم وأهل الكتاب والمؤمنون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r5.claim: The shared command is the common meaning of worship across audiences, avoiding polysemy for those who reject it; Ibn Ashur allows polysemy when context supports it, and 2:22 branches from the command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r5.anchor: فالمأمورية هو القدر المشترك حتى لا يلزم استعمال المشترك في معانيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r6.claim: This verse does not prove that unbelievers are addressed by subsidiary legal duties: for them worship means faith, monotheism, and affirming the Messenger, which is agreed upon.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r6.anchor: فليس في هذه الآية حجة للقول بخطاب الكفار بفروع الشريعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r7.claim: The meaning of Lord was explained under al-Fatiha 1:2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r7.anchor: عند قوله تعالى : { الحمد لله رب العالمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r8.claim: Using your Lord instead of another identifying form signals that the one who manages creation's affairs especially deserves worship, which expresses gratitude and dependence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p326/r8.anchor: ووجه العدول عن غير طريق الإضافة من طرق التعريف نحو العلمية إذ لم يقل اعبدوا الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.claim: The reasons for worship in 2:21–22 are paired with reasons against disbelief here: creation and provision are followed by life, death, resurrection, return, and creation of what is on earth, preparing for the account of human origins and stages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.anchor: ومن بديع المناسبة وفائق التفنن في ضروب الانتقالات في المخاطبات أن كانت العلل التي قرن بها الأمر بعبادة الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r1.claim: يا is the vocative particle and an attention-getter; أي is the noun being called.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r1.anchor: «يا» حرف نداء، وفيه تنبيه، و «أي» هو المنادى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains that أي follows the vocative particle before a noun with the definite article to avoid two markers of definiteness; ها draws attention, and الناس is the necessary adjective of أي.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r2.anchor: اجتلبت أي بعد حرف النداء فيما فيه الألف واللام لأن في حرف النداء تعريفا فكان يجتمع تعريفان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says يا أيها الناس occurs in Meccan revelations, whereas يا أيها الذين آمنوا occurs in Medinan ones.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يا أيها الناس حيث وقع في القرآن مكي، ويا أيها الذين آمنوا مدني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes that this sūra was already established as entirely Medinan, so يا أيها الناس can occur in a Medinan revelation; he accepts Mujāhid’s claim for يا أيها الذين آمنوا.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.anchor: قد تقدم في أول السورة أنها كلها مدنية، وقد يجيء في المدني يا أيها الناس، وأما قوله في يا أيها الذين آمنوا فصحيح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r5.claim: Worship your Lord means affirm His oneness and devote worship exclusively to Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r5.anchor: اعبدوا ربكم معناه وحدوه وخصوه بالعبادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r6.claim: Creation is singled out from God’s attributes because the Arabs acknowledged that God created them, making it an argument against them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r6.anchor: وذكر تعالى خلقه لهم من بين سائر صفاته إذ كانت العرب مقرة بأن الله خلقها، فذكر ذلك حجة عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r7.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r7.claim: Many exegetes take لعل here as an assurance or enjoining of God-fearing conduct, not as hope or expectation in God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r7.anchor: قال فيها كثير من المفسرين هي بمعنى إيجاب التقوى وليست من الله تعالى بمعنى ترج وتوقع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r8.speaker: سيبويه ورؤساء اللسان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r8.claim: Sībawayh and leading linguists keep لعل to its ordinary sense: hope and expectation belong to humans, who may expect to attain piety when they consider their worship; لعلكم attaches to اعبدوا ربكم.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r8.anchor: وقال سيبويه ورؤساء اللسان: هي على بابها، والترجي والتوقع إنما هو في حيز البشر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r9.claim: لعل may instead attach to خلقكم: since every child is born upon the fitra, an observer may expect that person to become God-fearing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r9.anchor: ويتجه تعلقها بخلقكم أي لما ولد كل مولود على الفطرة فهو إن تأمله متأمل توقع له ورجا أن يكون متقيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r10.claim: Tattaqūn derives from wiqāya; its underlying form توتقيون undergoes vowel transfer, deletion at the meeting of wāw and sukūn, and assimilation of the first wāw into tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p104#2/r10.anchor: وتتقون مأخوذ من الوقاية، وأصله «توتقيون» نقلت حركة الياء إلى القاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r13.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r13.claim: One group says the address is to all polytheists; their knowledge is specifically that God created, sent water, and brought forth provision, without denying their general ignorance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p105/r13.anchor: فقالت جماعة من المفسرين: المخاطب جميع المشركين. فقوله على هذا: وأنتم تعلمون يريد العلم الخاص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the address to include all people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه عام في جميع الناس وهو قول ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid take the address to be directed specifically to the Jews.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه خطاب لليهود دون غيرهم قاله الحسن ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the addressees are the unbelievers among the Arab polytheists and others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r3.anchor: والثالث أنه خطاب للكفار من مشركي العرب وغيرهم قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r4.claim: Muqatil identifies the addressees as hypocrites and Jews.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r4.anchor: والرابع أنه خطاب للمنافقين وإليهود قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r5.claim: Al-nas names the human species; the author links the name to movement toward people's aims and to the root naws, movement.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r5.anchor: والناس اسم للحيوان الآدمي وسموا بذلك لتحركهم في مراداتهم والنوس الحركة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r6.claim: Another proposed etymology derives anas from the forgetfulness that befalls people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r6.anchor: وقيل سموا أناسا لما يعتريهم من النسيان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r7.claim: One interpretation transmitted from Ibn Abbas takes worship here to mean affirming God's oneness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r7.anchor: وفي المراد بالعبادة هاهنا قولان أحدهما التوحيد والثاني الطاعة رويا عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r8.claim: A second interpretation transmitted from Ibn Abbas takes worship here to mean obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r8.anchor: وفي المراد بالعبادة هاهنا قولان أحدهما التوحيد والثاني الطاعة رويا عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r9.claim: Mentioning earlier generations strengthens the reminder, blocks denial, and makes the proof more conclusive.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r9.anchor: وإنما ذكر من قبلهم لأنه أبلغ في التذكير وأقطع للجحد وأحوط في الحجة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r10.claim: Another explanation is that earlier generations are mentioned to prompt reflection on the reward of the obedient and punishment of the disobedient.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r10.anchor: وقيل إمنا ذكر من قبلهم لينبههم على الاعتبار بأحوالهم من إثابة مطيع ومعاقبة عاص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r11.speaker: مقاتل وقطرب وابن كيسان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r11.claim: They take laʿalla causally, meaning “so that”: worship God so that you may attain mindfulness; a poem is cited to show this usage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r11.anchor: يريد لكي نكف و إلى هذا المعنى ذهب مقاتل وقطرب وابن كيسان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r12.speaker: سيبويه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r12.claim: Sibawayh takes laʿalla as expressing hope or expectation: worship while hoping for mindfulness and protection from God's punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r12.anchor: والثاني أنها بمعنى الترجي ومعناها اعبدوا الله راجين للتقوى ولأن تقوا أنفسكم بالعبادة عذاب ربكم وهذا قول سيبويه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the intended mindfulness as avoiding associating partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس لعلكم تتقون الشرك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r14.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the intended mindfulness as protecting yourselves from Hell.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r15.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p47#2/r15.claim: Mujahid explains the intended mindfulness as obedience.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r1.claim: God establishes His exclusive divinity by creating people from nothing and bestowing outward and inward blessings upon them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p194/r1.anchor: شرع تبارك وتعالى في بيان وحدانية ألوهيته، بأنه تعالى هو المنعم على عبيده، بإخراجهم من العدم إلى الوجود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r3.claim: The verses establish worship of God alone and, a fortiori, prove the Creator exists: reflecting on the ordered, varied, useful upper and lower worlds reveals His power, wisdom, knowledge, and sovereignty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية دالة على توحيده تعالى بالعبادة وحده لا شريك له، وقد استدل به كثير من المفسرين كالرازي وغيره على وجود الصانع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r4.speaker: أعرابي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r4.claim: A Bedouin argues that dung points to a camel and footprints to a traveler, so a constellated sky, furrowed earth, and wavy seas point to the Subtle, All-Aware Creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r4.anchor: كما قال بعض الأعراب، وقد سئل: ما الدليل على وجود الرب تعالى؟ فقال: يا سبحان الله، إن البعرة لتدل على البعير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r5.claim: Al-Razi transmits that Imam Malik answered Harun al-Rashid’s question about the Creator by pointing to the diversity of languages, voices, and tones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r5.anchor: وحكى فخر الدين عن الإمام مالك أن الرشيد سأله عن ذلك فاستدل باختلاف اللغات والأصوات والنغمات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa compares belief in an unguided universe to believing that a laden ship sails itself; the skeptics concede the absurdity, then accept the same reasoning about creation and convert.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197/r6.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة أن بعض الزنادقة سألوه عن وجود الباري تعالى، فقال لهم: دعوني فإني مفكر في أمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.claim: Al-Shafiʿi points to one mulberry leaf producing silk, honey, dung, and musk through different animals as evidence for the Creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.anchor: وعن الشافعي: أنه سئل عن وجود الصانع، فقال: هذا ورق التوت طعمه واحد تأكله الدود فيخرج منه الإبريسم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.claim: Ahmad compares an egg to a sealed, shining fortress that splits and yields a hearing, seeing, beautifully formed, melodious creature, the chicken.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.anchor: وعن الإمام أحمد بن حنبل أنه سئل عن ذلك فقال: هاهنا حصن حصين أملس، ليس له باب ولا منفذ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.speaker: أبو نواس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.claim: Abu Nuwas’s poem reads plants and their crafted forms as signs that the Maker has no partner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.anchor:
وسئل أبو نواس عن ذلك فأنشد:
تأمل في نبات الأرض وانظر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.speaker: ابن المعتز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s verses ask how God can be disobeyed or denied when every thing bears a sign that He is One.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.anchor:
وقال ابن المعتز:
فيا عجبا كيف يعصى الإله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.claim: Contemplating the high heavens and stars, surrounding seas, diverse mountains, rivers, animals, and varied plants despite shared soil and water demonstrates the Creator’s power, wisdom, mercy, and kindness; the mountain colors are cited at 35:27–28.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p197#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك هذه الأنهار السارحة من قطر إلى قطر لمنافع العباد وما زرأ في الأرض من الحيوانات المتنوعة والنبات المختلف الطعوم

JISHUMI:v1p278/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p278/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p278/r7.claim: Yā is the vocative particle; ay is indefinite, and hāʾ is the required attention particle because a vocative alerts and ay is ambiguous.
JISHUMI:v1p278/r7.anchor: و(أي): اسم مبهم، و(ها) تنبيه لازم ل (أي) في النداء؛ لأن النداء موضع تنبيه

JISHUMI:v1p278/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p278/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p278/r8.claim: Creation, action, and origination are related but distinct: creation brings into being by design, origination brings something about recently, and action covers all of these.
JISHUMI:v1p278/r8.anchor: والخلق والفعل والإحداث نظائر، وبينها فرق، فالخلق: الإيجاد على تقدير، والإحداث: الإيجاد عن قرب عهد

JISHUMI:v1p278/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p278/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p278/r9.claim: The poet's line illustrates creation as shaping: the addressee cuts what he fashioned, while some fashion without finishing the work.
JISHUMI:v1p278/r9.anchor: قال الشاعر: فلأنت تفري ما خلقت وبع ... ض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

JISHUMI:v1p278/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p278/r10.speaker: الأخفش
JISHUMI:v1p278/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash says al-nās qualifies the vague noun ay, as generic nouns can qualify an indefinite.
JISHUMI:v1p278/r10.anchor: وقال الأخفش: الأقيس أن يكون الناس صفة ل (أي)

JISHUMI:v1p278/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p278/r11.speaker: أكثر النحويين
JISHUMI:v1p278/r11.claim: Most grammarians reject treating al-nās as an adjective of ay.

JISHUMI:v1p278/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p278/r12.speaker: المازني
JISHUMI:v1p278/r12.claim: Al-Māzinī permits the accusative adjective after ay by analogy with an adjective after a demonstrative, though Arabs were not heard using it and no one followed him.
JISHUMI:v1p278/r12.anchor: وأجاز المازني وجه النصب في صفة أي قياسا على جوازه في صفة هذا

JISHUMI:v1p278/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p278/r13.speaker: قطرب وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p278/r13.claim: One explanation takes laʿalla as a purpose particle, meaning so that you may become God-fearing; this is attributed to Quṭrub and Abū ʿAlī.
JISHUMI:v1p278/r13.anchor: الأول قيل: بمعنى لام (كي)، أي لتتقوا، عن قطرب وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p849#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p849#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p849#2/r8.claim: The sūra first establishes the Book and faith in resurrection and divine unity, then prophethood, recounts Israel’s story and its scriptural foretelling of Islam and the Prophet, and proceeds to Islamic laws beginning with the qibla change.
JISHUMI:v1p849#2/r8.anchor: ذكر تعالى في أول السورة الكتاب وما يلزم الإيمان به من البعث والتوحيد، وغيره في قوله: (ياأيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r1.claim: After describing believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites in the third person, God turns to direct address; this rhetorical shift jolts the listener and makes the admonition more arresting.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r1.anchor: فن من الكلام جزل فيه هز وتحريك من السامع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r2.speaker: علقمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r2.claim: A report with a sound chain from Ibrahim via ʿAlqama says verses addressed with يا أيها الناس are Meccan, while يا أيها الذين آمنوا are Medinan.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r2.anchor: عن علقمة أن كل شيء نزل فيه ( يا أيها الناس ) فهو مكي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r3.claim: Yā was originally a call to someone distant; it is also used for a nearby person who is inattentive, treating him as distant, while addressing an attentive nearby person adds emphasis.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r3.anchor: يا ) حرف وضع في أصله لنداء البعيد صوت يهتف به الرجل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r4.claim: A supplicant who says yā rabb or yā Allāh despite God's nearness humbles himself as distant from divine favor while fervently seeking response.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r4.anchor: هو استقصار منه لنفسه واستبعاد لها من مظان الزلفى وما يقربه إلى رضوان الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r5.claim: Ayy is the linking form for calling a noun with the definite article, just as dhū and alladhī link descriptions to common nouns or definite nouns through clauses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p120/r5.anchor: وصلة إلى نداء ما فيه الألف واللام كما ان ذو والذي وصلتان إلى الوصف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r1.claim: Ayy is an ambiguous noun needing a clarifying following noun, which functions as its adjective; the vocative governs ayy, which cannot stand independently like Zayd.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r1.anchor: وهو اسم مبهم مفتقر إلى ما يوضحه ويزيل إبهامه فلا بد أن يردفه اسم جنس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r2.claim: The progression from ambiguity to clarification intensifies the address; inserted hāʾ reinforces the vocative and supplies the annexation ayy would otherwise require.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r2.anchor: وفي هذا التدرج من الإبهام إلى التوضيح ضرب من التأكيد والتشديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r3.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly uses this emphatic call because its commands, prohibitions, admonitions, warnings, promises, threats, and historical accounts are weighty matters requiring alert attention.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p121/r3.anchor: لاستقلاله بأوجه من التأكيد وأسباب من المبالغة لأن كل ما نادى الله له عباده من أوامره ونواهيه وعظاته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r1.claim: The author answers that increasing worship is itself worship, so an instruction to increase it is not a second, separate act.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r1.anchor: قلت الازدياد من العبادة عبادة وليس شيئا آخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r2.claim: If only polytheists are addressed, rabb is a shared name for God and the deities they call lords; “who created you” clarifies the intended referent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r2.anchor: فإن خصوا بالخطاب فالمراد به اسم يشترك فيه رب السموات والأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r3.claim: The Qur'an says the Meccan polytheists answer that Allah created them, showing that they know and acknowledge Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r3.anchor: ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r4.claim: For a universal address, rabb means the true Lord and “who created you” is praise; this reading can also apply to unbelievers, but the specific polytheist reading is clearer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r4.anchor: وإن كان الخطاب للفرق جميعا فالمراد به ربكم على الحقيقة والذي خلقكم صفة جرت عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r5.claim: Khalq means bringing something into existence with measure and proper proportion, as when a shoemaker measures and fits a shoe.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r5.anchor: والخلق إيجاد الشيء على تقدير واستواء يقال خلق النعل اذا قدره وسواها بالمقياس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r6.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads خلقكم with assimilation (idghām).
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122/r6.anchor: اذا قدره وسواها بالمقياس وقرأ أبو عمرو

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r1.speaker: ابن السميفع
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfa reads وخلق من قبلكم.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع وخلق من قبلكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r2.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads والذين من قبلكم, a difficult construction explained as emphatic insertion of a second relative pronoun, like Jarīr's repeated تيم.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r2.anchor: وفي قراءة زيد بن علي ( والذين من قبلكم ) وهي قراءة مشكلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r3.speaker: جرير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r3.claim: Jarīr's verse inserts a repeated name between the first name and its complement, an analogy for the difficult reading attributed to Zayd ibn ʿAlī.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r3.anchor: كما أقحم جرير في قوله ( يا تيم تيم عدي لا أبالكم ) تيما الثاني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r4.claim: Laʿalla can express expectation of good or apprehension of harm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r4.anchor: ولعل للترجي أو الإشفاق تقول لعل زيدا يكرمني ولعله يهينني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r5.claim: When God holds out hope, His generosity and mercy make it effectively certain, like kings whose indirect promises are understood as assured fulfillment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r5.anchor: ولكن لأنه إطماع من كريم رحيم اذا أطمع فعل ما يطمع فيه لا محالة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r6.speaker: من قال
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r6.claim: Some say laʿalla means “so that”; the author rejects this since laʿalla does not mean kay.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r6.anchor: قال من قال ان ( لعل ) بمعنى كي ولعل لا تكون بمعنى كي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, laʿalla may offer hope without guaranteeing the outcome, keeping people from complacently relying on certainty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p122#2/r7.anchor: أو يجيء على طريق الإطماع دون التحقيق لئلا يتكل العباد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r1.claim: Laʿalla cannot express God's literal hope or creation of people as hopeful for piety; it is metaphorical because humans choose between obedience and disobedience after being equipped and guided.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r1.anchor: لا يجوز أن يحمل على رجاء الله تقواهم لان الرجاء لا يجوز على عالم الغيب والشهادة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r2.claim: God created people for accountable worship, gave them reason and desire, removed impediments, showed the two paths, enabled choice, and wills good and piety for them; their outcome is left to their choice.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r2.anchor: خلق عباده ليتعبدهم بالتكليف وركب فيهم العقول والشهوات وأزاح العلة في أقدارهم وتمكينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r3.claim: The human-directed promise of forgiveness in the cited verse illustrates expectation language used in addressing people, not God's literal uncertainty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p123/r3.anchor: عسى ربكم أن يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124/r1.claim: The purpose of taqwa also applies to earlier peoples; the present addressees dominate the wording, while the meaning includes both present and absent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124/r1.anchor: لم يقصره عليهم ولكن غلب المخاطبين على الغائبين في اللفظ والمعنى على إرادتهم جميعا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124/r2.claim: Taqwa is worship's ultimate end; commanding worship toward that highest goal makes the command more forceful and firmly rooted than simply saying “worship” or “be pious.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p124/r2.anchor: وإنما التقوى قصارى أمر العابد ومنتهى جهده

BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r1.speaker: التيسير
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r1.claim: Al-Taysir takes the address as both rebuke for answering favors with ingratitude and disobedience, and as instruction that God excuses forgetful, unintentional opposition on account of faith.
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r1.anchor: قال في "التيسير" : وإذا كان الإنسان من النسيان ففيه عتاب وتلقين أما العتاب فكأنه يقول : أيها الناس قابلتم نعمنا بالكفران

BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r2.claim: Bursevi reads the command for different audiences: polytheists should affirm God's oneness, sinners obey, hypocrites sincerely know Him through tawhid, and the obedient persist; the wording encompasses all, as Abu al-Layth says.
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r2.anchor: يقول للكفار وحدوا ربكم ويقول للعاصين أطيعوا ربكم ويقول للمنافقين أخلصوا بالتوحيد معرفة ربكم ويقول للمطيعين أثبتوا على طاعة ربكم

BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r3.claim: Worship is exhausting obedience toward its completion while cultivating awe that keeps one distant from disobedience.
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r3.anchor: والعبادة استفراغ الطاعة في استكمال الطاعة واستشعار الخشية في استبعاد المعصية

BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r4.claim: The clause describing the Lord is an adjective serving exaltation and causal justification: obey Him because He created you when you were nothing.
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r4.anchor: {الذي خلقكم} صفة جرت عنه للتعظيم والتعليل معناه أطيعوا ربكم الذي خلقكم لخلقكم ولم تكونوا شيئا

BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r5.claim: Creation means bringing a thing into existence without a prior model.
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r5.anchor: والخلق اختراع الشيء على غير مثال سبق

BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r6.claim: Those before you are earlier nations; min is partitive in origin and attaches to an omitted element.
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r6.anchor: خلق {الذين من قبلكم} أي : من زمن قبل زمانكم من الأمم فمن ابتدائية متعلقة بمحذوف

BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r7.claim: Mentioning the ancestors' creation reinforces worship's obligation, demonstrates God's power, and warns that earlier peoples passed away, so listeners should remember their own end and not excuse neglect.
BURSEVI:v1p57#2/r7.anchor: وفي الوصف به إيماء إلى سبب وجوب عبادته تعالى فإن خلق

BURSEVI:v1p58/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58/r1.claim: The clause is circumstantial to the implied subject of worship: people worship hoping to join the Godfearing, who attain guidance, success, and divine nearness.
BURSEVI:v1p58/r1.anchor: {لعلكم تتقون} حال من ضمير اعبدوا أي : راجين أن تدخلوا في سلك المتقين الفائزين بالهدى والفلاح

BURSEVI:v1p58/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58/r2.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v1p58/r2.claim: Laʿalla expresses hope, but from God its promise is certain because the Generous only hopes for what He will do; all generations are addressed to become pious, with the present audience singled out by predominance.
BURSEVI:v1p58/r2.anchor: ولعل للترجي والأطماع وهي من الله تعالى واجب لأن الكريم لا يطمع إلا فيما يفعل والأولون والآخرون مخاطبون بالأمر بالتقوى

BURSEVI:v1p58/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58/r3.claim: Taqwa is the wayfarer's ultimate station: disavowing everything besides God.
BURSEVI:v1p58/r3.anchor: وفيه تنبيه على أن التقوى منتهى درجة السالكين وهو التبري من كل شيء سوى الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p58/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p58/r4.claim: The worshipper must not become conceited over worship but remain between fear and hope, as the verses about praying in fear and hoping for mercy teach.
BURSEVI:v1p58/r4.anchor: وأن العابد ينبغي أن لا يغتر بعبادته ويكون ذا خوف ورجاء كما قال تعالى :

BURSEVI:v1p58/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p58/r5.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p58/r5.claim: Saʿdi's couplet warns that a worshipper does not necessarily attain sincere faith through worship alone.
BURSEVI:v1p58/r5.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : اكر مردى از مردىء خود مكوى نه هر شهسواري بدر برد كوى

BURSEVI:v1p60/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60/r1.claim: The address recalls the primordial covenant: humanity affirmed God's lordship and vowed to worship only Him, then forgot, broke the covenant, and worshipped idols, worldly life, ego, desire, and Satan.
BURSEVI:v1p60/r1.anchor: الإشارة في تحقيق الآيتين إنه تعالى خاطب ناسى عهود يوم الميثاق والإقرار بربوبيته ومعاهدته أن لا تعبدوا إلا إياه فخالفوه ونقضوا عهده

BURSEVI:v1p60/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60/r2.claim: The Messenger and scripture recall that covenant; worship means fulfill it through verbal tawhid, a heart freed for God, a singular secret, avoidance of prohibitions, and performance of commanded acts.
BURSEVI:v1p60/r2.anchor: فبعث إليهم الرسول وكتب إليه الكتاب وأخبرهم عن النسيان والشرك ودعاهم إلى التوحيد والعبودية وقال : {اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم

BURSEVI:v1p60/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p60/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p60/r3.claim: Taqwa here is release from worshipping anything besides God; God fulfills His lordship covenant by saving servants from low states, raising their ranks in Paradise, and granting nearness and honors.
BURSEVI:v1p60/r3.anchor: {لعلكم تتقون} عن شرك عبادة غير الله فيوفى الله بعهد الربوبية بالنجاة من الدركات ورفع الدرجات

MUQATIL:2:21-22/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r1.claim: The address to people means the hypocrites and Jews, whom Muqatil calls to worship and affirm the oneness of their Lord.

MUQATIL:2:21-22/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r2.claim: God created the addressees when they were nothing, as He created the nations before them.
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r2.anchor: ولم تكونوا شيئا، { والذين من قبلكم } من الأمم الخالية

MUQATIL:2:21-22/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r3.claim: Laʿalla here means “so that”; reflecting on creation should lead people to avoid shirk and affirm God’s oneness.
MUQATIL:2:21-22/r3.anchor: الشرك وتوحدوا الله عز وجل إذا تفكرتم فى خلقكم وخلق الذين من قبلكم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r1.claim: After describing believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites and their outcomes, God turns to direct address, an instance of iltifāt.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r1.anchor: لما عدد الله فرق المكلفين من المؤمنين والكفار والمنافقين وذكر صفاتهم وأحوالهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r2.speaker: علقمة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r2.claim: ʿAlqama says Qur’anic ‘O people’ addresses Meccans, while ‘O you who believe’ addresses Medinans; al-Nasafī identifies this call as directed to Meccan polytheists.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r2.anchor: قال علقمة ما فى القرآن يا أيها الناس فهو خطاب لأهل مكة وما فيه يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو خطاب لأهل المدينة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r3.claim: Here ‘O people’ addresses the polytheists of Mecca.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r4.claim: Yāʾ is conventionally for a distant addressee and ayyuha with hamza for a near one; it is also used for the heedless as if distant, making a call to someone nearby emphatic.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r4.anchor: فذاك للتوكيد المؤذن بأن الخطاب الذى يتلوه معتنى به جدا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r5.claim: Calling the nearby ‘O Lord’ expresses the caller’s self-abasement and distance from divine nearness despite longing for a response.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r5.anchor: واستبعاد لها عن مظان الزلفى هظما لنفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r6.claim: Ayyu connects a vocative to a definite noun or description, as dhū and alladhī connect generic nouns or clauses; ayyu is ambiguous and needs a following clarifying descriptor.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r6.anchor: فلا بد أن يردفه اسم جنس أو ما يجرى مجراه يتصف به حتى يتضح المقصود بالنداء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r7.claim: Unlike Zayd, ayyu cannot stand independently; the following noun or clause describes it, and interposed hāʾ of alerting emphasizes the call and compensates for absent annexation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r7.anchor: إلا أن أيا لا يستقل بنفسه استقلال زيد فمم ينفك عن الصفة وكلمة التنبيه المقحمة بين الصفة وموصوفها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r8.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly uses this emphatic form because its commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats are weighty while people are heedless.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r8.anchor: وكثر النداء فى القرآن على هذه الطريقة لأن ما نادى الله به عباده من اوامره ونواهيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r9.claim: ‘Worship your Lord’ means affirm His oneness.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r9.anchor: وحدوه قال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما كل عبادة فى القرآن فهى توحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says every act of worship mentioned in the Qur’an is tawḥīd.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما كل عبادة فى القرآن فهى توحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r11.claim: The Creator is the one who brings the nonexistent into being according to measure and proportion.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r11.anchor: والخلق إيجاد المعدوم على تقدير واستواء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r12.speaker: المعتزلة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r12.claim: The Muʿtazila define creation as bringing a thing into being according to measure and proportion, since they regard the nonexistent as a thing that can be known and described.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r12.anchor: وعند المعتزلة إيجاد الشىء على تقدير واستواء وهذا بناء على أن المعدوم شيء عندهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r13.claim: Al-Nasafī’s position is that ‘thing’ names what exists.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r14.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r14.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads khalaqakum with assimilation.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r15.claim: Because the audience already acknowledged God as creator of them and their predecessors, they are urged to worship Him rather than idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r15.anchor: احتج عليهم بانه خالقهم وخالق من قبلهم لأنهم كانوا مقرين بذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r16.claim: Worship is enjoined in hope that they will thereby become God-fearing and escape punishment; from a generous giver, inducement by laʿalla functions like a firm promise.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r16.anchor: أى اعبدوا على رجاء أن تتقوا فتنجوا بسببه من العذاب ولعل للترجى والاطماع

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r17.speaker: سيبويه
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r17.claim: Sībawayh treats laʿalla here as hope or inducement, which from a generous speaker functions like a binding promise.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r17.anchor: ولكنه إطماع من كريم فيجرى مجرى وعده المحتوم وفاؤه وبه قال سيبويه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r18.speaker: قطرب
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r18.claim: Quṭrub reads laʿalla as ‘so that,’ expressing purpose.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p25#3/r18.anchor: وقال قطرب هو بمعنى كى أى لكى تتقوا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r1.speaker: الحجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r1.claim: The cited usage contrasts bringing something into being with carrying it through: al-Hajjaj says that whatever he creates he completes, as he fulfills every promise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r1.anchor: وقال الحجاج: ما خلقت إلا فريت، ولا وعدت إلا وفيت.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r2.claim: A second sense of khalq is creating, originating, and innovating; the cited verse uses it for fabricating falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r2.anchor: الثاني: الإنشاء والاختراع والإبداع قال الله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r3.claim: Mentioning earlier generations reminds people that the one who created them also caused their deaths; their fate and trials warn later people of their own.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r3.anchor: فالجواب: أنه إنما يجري الكلام على التنبيه والتذكير ليكون أبلغ في العظة فذكرهم من قبلهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r4.claim: Laʿalla attaches to the command to worship, not to “created you,” since those created for Hell were not created in order to attain taqwa.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r4.anchor: «لعل» متصلة باعبدوا لا بخلقكم لأن من ذرأه الله لجهنم لم يخلقه ليتقي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r5.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r5.claim: On the literal reading, laʿalla expresses human hope: people are told to act in expectation that they may become mindful; Sibawayh explains it this way.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r5.anchor: الأول: أن «لعل» على بابها من الترجي والتوقع، والترجي والتوقع إنما هو في حيز البشر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r6.speaker: أبو المعالي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r6.claim: Abu al-Maʿali prefers the literal hope reading of laʿalla.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r7.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r7.claim: Sibawayh applies the hope sense to Moses and Aaron’s mission: they should speak gently in hope Pharaoh may remember or fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r7.anchor:
قال سيبويه في قوله عز وجل:
اذهبا إلى فرعون إنه طغى فقولا له قولا لينا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r8.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r8.claim: Qutrub and al-Tabari say Arabic laʿalla can lose its sense of doubt and mean “so that,” making the clause an expression of purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r8.anchor: الثاني: أن العرب استعملت «لعل» مجردة من الشك بمعنى لام كي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r9.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r9.claim: A poet’s treaty example supports laʿalla as purpose: the parties stopped fighting so that the other side would stop too.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r10.claim: A third interpretation makes laʿalla mean exposing oneself to a possibility; here obedience offers protection from Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r10.anchor: الثالث: أن تكون «لعل» بمعنى التعرض للشيء كأنه قيل: افعلوا ذلك متعرضين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r11.claim: The intended protection is achieved by accepting God’s command; Arabic also says one protects oneself from a claim by paying the due.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r11.anchor: والمعنى في قوله { لعلكم تتقون }: أي لعلكم أن تجعلوا بقبول ما أمركم الله به وقاية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r12.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r12.claim: Ali says that in the heat of battle they used the Prophet as a shield against the enemy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r12.anchor: ومنه قول علي رضي الله عنه: كنا إذا احمر البأس اتقينا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r13.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r13.claim: A cited poet contrasts completing what one creates with people who create something but fail to carry it through.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21/r13.anchor:
ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبع
ض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

QURTUBI-FULL:2:21#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21#2/r1.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21#2/r1.claim: Antarah’s verse uses ittaqa for the cavalry sheltering behind him, illustrating the sense of taking cover or protection.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:21#2/r1.anchor: ولقد كررت المهر يدمى نحره حتى اتقتني الخيل بابني حذيم

RAZI-FULL:v2p74#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p74#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p74#2/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī introduces the following verses as an argument establishing divine unity, prophethood, and resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v2p74#2/r3.anchor: القول في إقامة الدلالة على التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r1.claim: After describing believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites, God shifts from speaking about them to addressing them directly, an iltifāt also seen in 1:5.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r1.anchor: أقبل عليهم بالخطاب ، وهو من باب الالتفات المذكور في قوله تعالى : { إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين }

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r2.claim: Direct address stirs and moves the hearer more than continuing to speak about that person in the third person.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r2.anchor: أن فيه مزيد هز وتحريك من السامع

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r3.claim: The shift honors and draws the addressee near: after initially making the Messenger an intermediary, God now addresses the person without an intermediary.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r3.anchor: كأنه سبحانه وتعالى يقول . جعلت الرسول واسطة بيني وبينك أولا ثم الآن أزيد في إكرامك وتقريبك

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r4.claim: The move from third to direct address suggests that a servant engaged in worship is continually ascending.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r4.anchor: أنه مشعر بأن العبد إذا كان مشتغلا بالعبودية فإنه يكون أبدا في الترقي

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r5.claim: Because the earlier verses narrated their condition and these verses impose difficult commands, God’s direct personal address gives relief and makes the burden pleasant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r5.anchor: الآيات المتقدمة كانت في حكاية أحوالهم ، وأما هذه الآيات فإنها أمر وتكليف ، ففيه كلفة ومشقة فلا بد من راحة

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r6.speaker: علقمة والحسن
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r6.claim: ʿAlqama and al-Ḥasan say that Qur’anic addresses “O people” are Meccan, while “O you who believe” is Medinan.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r6.anchor: حكي عن علقمة والحسن أنه قال : كل شيء في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī accepts that distinction if it rests on transmitted reports, but rejects deriving it merely from the larger number of believers in Medina: believers may be addressed as people, and unbelievers may be commanded to worship just as believers are told to persist and increase in worship.
RAZI-FULL:v2p75/r7.anchor: هذا الذي ذكروه إن كان الرجوع فيه إلى النقل فمسلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r1.claim: Words normally denote linguistic or nonlinguistic things; the vocative particle is different, functioning as an act that draws attention rather than denoting another thing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r1.anchor: لفظ النداء لم يجعل دليلا على شيء آخر ، بل هو لفظ يجري مجرى عمل يعمله عامل لأجل التنبيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r2.claim: “O Zayd” cannot mean “I call Zayd”: the latter is a truth-apt report, does not itself make Zayd the addressee, may be spoken to a third party, and reports rather than performs the call.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r2.anchor: أن قولنا . أنادي زيدا ، خبر يحتمل التصديق والتكذيب

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r3.claim: Though names are strongest and particles weakest, a name can join a particle in calling; by analogy, a human can serve the transcendent Lord through invocation and humble supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r3.anchor: قد يأتلف الاسم مع الحرف في حال النداء ، فكذا البشر يصلح لخدمة الرب حال النداء والتضرع

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r4.claim: Yā originally calls someone distant; hamza (a-) calls someone near. Using yā for someone nearby treats an inattentive or heedless person as distant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r4.anchor: ( ياء ) حرف وضع في أصله لنداء البعيد وإن كان لنداء القريب لكن لسبب أمر مهم جدا

RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r5.claim: Although God is nearer than the jugular vein, a supplicant says “O Lord” either from humility and self-reproach, distancing himself from the stations of intimacy, or because answering prayer is supremely important.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76/r5.anchor: هو استبعاد لنفسه من مظان الزلفى وما يقربه إلى منازل المقربين هضما لنفسه وإقرارا عليها بالتنقيص

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r1.claim: Ay connects the vocative to a noun bearing the definite article, just as dhū and alladhī connect generic nouns to descriptions and definite nouns to clauses; ay is ambiguous and needs a noun or equivalent adjective to specify it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r1.anchor: ( أي ) وصلة إلى نداء ما فيه الألف اللام كما أن ( ذو ) و ( الذي ) وصلتان إلى الوصف بأسماء الأجناس

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r2.claim: The vocative particle governs ay, while the following noun is its adjective, as in “O Zayd, the courteous”; unlike Zayd, ay cannot stand independently and therefore remains joined to its adjective and described noun.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r2.anchor: فالذي يعمل فيه حرف النداء هو أي والاسم التابع له صفة كقولك يا زيد الظريف

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r3.claim: The inserted attention particle reinforces the call and compensates for the genitive construction expected with ay.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r3.anchor: التنبيه المقحمة بين الصفة وموصوفها ففيها فائدتان

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r4.claim: The emphatic formula is frequent in the Qur’an because its commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, and momentous histories must awaken listeners who are heedless.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#2/r4.anchor: إن كل ما نادى الله تعالى به عباده من الأوامر والنواهي ، والوعد والوعيد ، واقتصاص أخبار المتقدمين بأمور عظام

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r1.claim: Rāzī holds that a definite plural denotes the whole class; al-Ashʿarī, al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr, and Abū Hāshim dispute this, while emphasis and unrestricted exception support generality.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r1.anchor: أن لفظ الجمع المعرف بلام التعريف يفيد العموم ، والخلاف فيه مع الأشعري والقاضي أبي بكر

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r2.claim: The direct address covers all people present at the time, but face-to-face speech does not directly address people who do not yet exist.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r2.anchor: يا أيهاالناس } خطاب مشافهة وخطاب المشافهة مع المعدوم لا يجوز

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r3.claim: Later generations are included by separate, mass-transmitted evidence in Muhammad’s religion, which extends these commands to everyone until the Day of Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r3.anchor: عرفنا بالتواتر من دين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تلك الخطابات ثابتة في حق من سيوجد

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r4.claim: Taken by genus semantics alone, the command to worship is discharged by performing one instance, since that instance brings the worship genus into existence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r4.anchor: قوله اعبدوا معناه ادخلوا هذه الماهية في الوجود ، فإذا أتوا بفرد من أفراد الماهية

RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r5.claim: Rāzī nevertheless takes every worship act to be commanded: worship as worship is the fitting cause of the command, since it expresses glorification and submission to God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p76#3/r5.anchor: ترتيب الحكم على الوصف مشعر بعلية الوصف ، لا سيما إذا كان الوصف مناسبا للحكم

RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r1.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r1.claim: An objector says unbelievers cannot be commanded to know God: if commanded while ignorant they cannot recognize the divine command, and if commanded after knowing Him the knowledge would already exist.
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r1.anchor: لقائل أن يقول : قوله : { قدير ياأيها الناس اعبدوا } لا يتناول الكفار البتة لأن الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r2.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r2.claim: The objector infers that unbelievers cannot be commanded to worship, because worship before knowing God is impossible and worship afterward depends on an impossible command to acquire knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r2.anchor: عبادة من لا يعرف ممتنعة أو يؤمر بالعبادة بعد المعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r3.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r3.claim: The objection also excludes believers as addressees: they already worship God, so commanding them to worship would command an accomplished act.
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r3.anchor: وأيضا يستحيل أن يكون هذا الخطاب مع المؤمنين ، لأنهم يعبدون الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r4.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r4.claim: One reply says worship is conditional on prior knowledge, just as zakāt is conditional on owning the minimum threshold; these proponents regard knowledge as necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r4.anchor: من الناس من قال : الأمر بالعبادة مشروط بحصول المعرفة ، كما أن الأمر بالزكاة مشروط

RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r5.speaker: من لم يقل بذلك
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r5.claim: Those who reject that reply infer that knowledge is not self-evident: commanding worship also commands its prerequisite, knowledge, as purification, obtaining water, and seeking a deposit must precede their acts.
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r5.anchor: وأما من لم يقل بذلك استدل بهذه الآية على أن المعارف ليست ضرورية

RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r6.claim: On this reasoning, an unbeliever can be addressed with worship, provided that he first believes and then performs worship.
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r6.anchor: يصح أن يكون الكافر مخاطبا بالعبادة وشرط الإتيان بها الإتيان بالإيمان أولا

RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r7.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r7.claim: A remaining objection says commanding the acquisition of knowledge is impossible; Rāzī refers the full issue to works on legal theory and argues the objection need not apply to other attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v2p77/r7.anchor: بقي لهم : الأمر بتحصيل المعرفة محال ، قلنا هذه المسألة مستقصاة في الأصول

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r1.claim: To avoid treating believers as commanded to do what is already done, Rāzī reads the command as requiring continued or increased worship; added worship is still worship.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r1.anchor: لما تعذر ذلك فنحمله إما على الأمر بالاستمرار على العبادة أو على الأمر بالازدياد منها

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r2.speaker: منكرو التكليف
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r2.claim: Opponents of divine obligation argue that equal motives make choosing an act impossible, while unequal motives make one option inevitable and the other impossible; either way, the command exceeds capacity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r2.anchor: قال منكرو التكليف : لا يجوز ورود الأمر من الله تعالى بالتكليف لوجوه : أحدها

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r3.speaker: منكرو التكليف
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r3.claim: They argue that divine foreknowledge makes the commanded act either inevitable, impossible, or unknown to God; the first two defeat the command and the last attributes ignorance to God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r3.anchor: إن كان الأول كان واجب الوقوع ممتنع العدم فلا فائدة في ورود الأمر به

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r4.speaker: منكرو التكليف
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r4.claim: They deny a benefit in obligations: God cannot benefit from worship, while any benefit to people could be granted directly without hardship, making the hardship purposeless.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r4.anchor: فإن كان لفائدة فهي إما عائدة إلى المعبود أو إلى العابد أما إلى المعبود فمحال

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r5.speaker: منكرو التكليف
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r5.claim: They say people do not create their own actions; if God has already created an act in a person, ordering it is redundant, and if not, the order asks for the impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r5.anchor: أن العبد غير موجد لأفعاله لأنه غير عالم بتفاصيلها ومن لا يعلم تفاصيل الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r6.speaker: منكرو التكليف
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r6.claim: They argue that obligations aim to purify the heart, so outward duties should lapse when they obstruct constant absorption in knowing God; jurists and analogists should follow rationalized rulings over appearances.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r6.anchor: المقصود من التكليف إنما هو تطهير القلب على ما دلت عليه ظواهر القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r7.claim: Rāzī answers the first three objections that their proponents must adopt the contradictory duty to believe that no duties exist.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r7.anchor: أوجبوا بما ذكروه اعتقاد عدم التكاليف فهذا تكليف ينفي التكليف وأنه متناقض

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r8.claim: Rāzī’s theological reply is that everything God does is permissible, including imposing what people call an impossible burden, because God is creator and owner.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r8.anchor: عندنا يحسن من الله تعالى كل شيء سواء كان ذلك تكليف ما لا يطاق أو غيره

RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r9.claim: The general command is qualified for those without understanding or capacity, including children, the insane, the unaware, the forgetful, and those unable to act.
RAZI-FULL:v2p78/r9.anchor: الأمر بالعبادة وإن كان عاما لكل الناس لكنه مخصوص في حق من لا يفهم كالصبي

RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r1.speaker: قائلون
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r1.claim: Some also exempt slaves: the specific duty to obey their masters takes precedence over the general command to worship.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r1.anchor: ومنهم من قال إنه مخصوص في حق العبيد ، لأن الله تعالى أوجب عليهم طاعة مواليهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r2.claim: Al-Qāḍī says the verse identifies God’s creation and beneficence as the reason worship exists.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r2.anchor: قال القاضي : الآية تدل على أن سبب وجود العبادة ما بينه من خلقه لنا والإنعام علينا

RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r3.claim: Rāzī’s school argues that servants do not earn reward from their acts: worship fulfills an obligation caused by God’s creation and favor, and fulfilling a duty earns no payment owed by God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79/r3.anchor: أصحابنا يحتجون بهذه الآية على أن العبد لا يستحق بفعله الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r1.claim: After commanding worship, the verse adduces the creation of the accountable people and their predecessors as evidence for the Creator’s existence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r1.anchor: لما أمر بعبادة الرب أردفه بما يدل على وجود الصانع وهو خلق المكلفين وخلق من قبلهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r2.claim: Rāzī says the verse establishes that God is known through rational inquiry and inference; he rejects the Ḥashwiyya claim that pursuing this science is an innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r2.anchor: وطعن قوم من الحشوية في هذه الطريقة وقالوا الاشتغال بهذا العلم بدعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r3.claim: First reason for theology’s superiority: a science is nobler when its subject is nobler, and God’s essence and attributes are the noblest objects of knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r3.anchor: شرف العلم بشرف المعلوم فمهما كان المعلوم أشرف كان العلم الحاصل به أشرف

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r4.claim: Second reason: religious sciences outrank nonreligious ones, and exegesis, hadith, and jurisprudence all depend on theology’s establishment of the Creator, prophecy, and divine unity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r4.anchor: وثانيها : أن العلم إما أن يكون دينيا أو غير ديني ، ولا شك أن العلم الديني أشرف

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r5.claim: Third reason: theology is nobler because its opposites, unbelief and innovation, are among the vilest things.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r5.anchor: وثالثها : أن شرف الشيء قد يظهر بواسطة خساسة ضده ، فكلما كان ضده أخس كان هو أشرف وضد علم الأصول هو الكفر والبدعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r6.claim: Fourth reason: knowledge can be honored by its subject, need, or proof; astronomy illustrates noble subject, medicine greater need, and arithmetic stronger proofs, while theology combines all three.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r6.anchor: ورابعها : أن شرف الشيء قد يكون بشرف موضوعه وقد يكون لأجل شدة الحاجة إليه ، وقد يكون لقوة براهينه ، وعلم الأصول مشتمل على الكل

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r7.claim: Theology’s subject is exceptionally noble: it investigates God’s essence, attributes, acts, and the categories of what exists and does not exist.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r7.anchor: أما علم الأصول فالمطلوب منه معرفة ذات الله تعالى وصفاته وأفعاله ، ومعرفة أقسام المعلومات من المعدومات والموجودات

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r8.claim: Its religious need is great because knowing these matters earns immense reward and association with angels, while ignorance brings punishment and association with devils.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r8.anchor: من عرف هذه الأشياء استوجب الثواب العظيم والتحق بالملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r9.claim: Its worldly need is great because social order depends on belief in the Creator and resurrection; without that belief, disorder would spread.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r9.anchor: مصالح العالم إنما تنتظم عند الإيمان بالصانع والبعث والحشر

RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r10.claim: Its proofs reach the highest strength because they are arranged with certainty from certain premises.
RAZI-FULL:v2p79#2/r10.anchor: براهين هذا العلم يجب أن تكون مركبة من مقدمات يقينية تركيبا يقينيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r1.claim: Fifth reason theology is noblest: it is not subject to abrogation or change and does not vary among peoples or regions.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r1.anchor: وخامسها : أن هذا العلم لا يتطرق إليه النسخ ولا التغيير ، ولا يختلف باختلاف الأمم والنواحي

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r2.claim: Sixth reason: verses on theological claims are nobler than legal verses; Rāzī contrasts the reported virtues of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, the end of al-Baqara, and the Throne Verse with verses on menstruation and debt.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r2.anchor: الآيات المشتملة على مطالب هذا العلم وبراهينها أشرف من الآيات المشتملة على المطالب الفقهية

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r3.claim: Seventh reason: fewer than six hundred verses concern legal rulings; most others concern unity, prophecy, and rebuttal of idolaters, while stories teach God’s wisdom and power.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r3.anchor: وسابعها : أن الآيات الواردة في ا لأحكام الشرعية أقل من ستمائة آية

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r4.claim: Rāzī identifies five proofs of the Creator in these verses: creating accountable people, their predecessors, heaven, earth, and fruits from rain sent down from heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r4.anchor: أولها : ما ذكر ههنا من الدلائل الخمسة وهي خلق المكلفين وخلق من قبلهم ، وخلق السماء وخلق الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s other signs in the heavens and earth likewise aim to establish the Creator’s existence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r5.anchor: وكل ما ورد في القرآن من عجائب السماوات والأرض ، فالمقصود منه ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r6.claim: God’s knowledge is shown by forming people in the wombs as He wills; effects and their ordering disclose the maker’s knowledge, just as theologians argue.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r6.anchor: وهذا هو عين دليل المتكلمين فإنهم يستدلون بأحكام الأفعال واتقانها على علم الصانع

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r7.claim: The verse “Does He who created not know?” makes the same inference from creation to the Creator’s knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r7.anchor: وقال : { ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير } ( االملك : 14 ) وهو عين تلك الدلالة

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r8.claim: God’s keys to the unseen indicate knowledge of all things; fulfillment of reports about hidden events shows that He knew them beforehand.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r8.anchor: وقال : { وعنده مفاتح الغيب لا يعلمها إلا هو } ( الأنعام : 59 ) وذلك تنبيه على كونه تعالى عالما بكل المعلومات

RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r10.claim: Rāzī turns to Qur’anic proofs of divine transcendence, maintaining that God is neither a body nor located in space.
RAZI-FULL:v2p80/r10.anchor: وأما التنزيه فالذي يدل على أنه ليس بجسم ، ولا في مكان قوله :

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r1.claim: As evidence for transcendence, Rāzī cites God’s proof given to Abraham against his people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r1.anchor: وتلك حجتنا ءاتيناها إبراهيم على قومه } ( الأنعام : 82 ) وثانيها : حاله مع أبيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r2.claim: Abraham challenged his father’s worship of an idol that could neither hear, see, nor help him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r2.anchor: ياأبت لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغنى عنك شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r3.claim: Abraham verbally challenged his people about the statues to which they were devoted.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r3.anchor: أما بالقول فقوله : { ما هاذه التماثيل التى أنتم لها عاكفون }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r4.claim: Abraham demonstrated the idols’ impotence by smashing them all except the largest, so that the people might turn to it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r4.anchor: فجعلهم جذاذا إلا كبيرا لهم لعلهم إليه يرجعون

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r5.claim: Before the ruler, Abraham argued that his Lord gives life and death, exposing the ruler’s claim to do the same.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r5.anchor: { ربي الذى يحى ويميت قال أنا أحى وأميت } ( البقرة : 258 ) إلى آخره

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r6.claim: Rāzī says sound minds recognize that kalām merely presents these prophetic proofs and answers objections to them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r6.anchor: وكل من سلمت فطرته علم أن علم الكلام ليسي إلا تقرير هذه الدلائل ودفع الأسئلة والمعارضات عنها

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r7.claim: Abraham also asked God to show him how He revives the dead, addressing the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r7.anchor: { رب أرنى كيف تحى الموتى } ( البقرة : 26 ) إلى آخره

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r8.claim: Moses answered Pharaoh with the Lord who gave each thing its form and guidance, the same creation-and-guidance proof Abraham used of God creating and guiding him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r8.anchor: قال ربنا الذى أعطى كل شىء خلقه ثم هدى

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r9.claim: Moses’ appeal to the Lord of Pharaoh’s forefathers echoes Abraham’s argument that his Lord gives life and death.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r9.anchor: ربكم ورب ءابائكم الاولين } ( الشعراء : 26 ) وهذا هو الذي قاله إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r10.claim: When Pharaoh demanded another proof, Moses named the Lord of the East and West.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r10.anchor: فلما لم يكتف فرعون بذلك وطالبه بشيء آخر قال موسى : { رب المشرق والمغرب }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r11.claim: These proofs belong to the prophets’ practice: they reasoned them out and inherited them from their purified predecessors.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r11.anchor: التمسك بهذه الدلائل حرفة هؤلاء المعصومين وأنهم كما استفادوها من عقولهم فقد توارثوها

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r12.claim: Moses also argued for his prophethood by offering a clear miracle as evidence of his truthfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r12.anchor: ففي قوله : { أو * لو * جئتك بشىء مبين } وهذا هو الاستدلال بالمعجزة على الصدق

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r13.claim: Muhammad’s argument for monotheism, prophethood, and resurrection is unmistakable because the Qur’an is full of such proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r13.anchor: اشتغاله بالدلائل على التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد أظهر من أن يحتاج فيه إلى التطويل

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r14.claim: The Qur’an refutes materialists who say only time destroys by presenting various proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r14.anchor: الدهرية الذين كانوا يقولون : { وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر } ( الجاثية : 24 ) والله تعالى أبطل قولهم بأنواع الدلائل

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r15.claim: Varied plants and animals arising despite shared natural temperaments and celestial influences refute those who deny a freely choosing Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r15.anchor: حدوث أنواع النبات وأصناف الحيوانات مع اشتراك الكل في الطبائع وتأثيرات الأفلاك

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r16.claim: Abraham’s argument when night covered him refutes those who make celestial bodies partners by claiming they influence the world.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r16.anchor: والله تعالى أبطله بدليل الخليل في قوله : { فلما جن عليه اليل }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r17.claim: The Qur’an also refutes lower partners: Christians claim divinity for Christ and idolaters for their idols.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r17.anchor: وأما الشريك السفلي فالنصارى قالوا بإلاهية المسيح وعبدة الأوثان قالوا : بإلاهية الأوثان

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r18.claim: One group denied prophethood altogether, asking whether God would send a human messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r18.anchor: الذين طعنوا في أصل النبوة وهم الذين حكى الله عنهم أنهم قالوا : { أبعث الله بشرا رسولا }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r19.claim: Another group, including Jews and Christians, accepted prophethood in general but challenged Muhammad’s prophethood; the Qur’an answers their objections.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r19.anchor: والثاني : الذين سلموا أصل النبوة وطعنوا في نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وهم اليهود والنصارى

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r20.claim: When critics objected to Qur’anic parables, God replied that He is not ashamed to give even a mosquito as an example.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r20.anchor: فأجاب الله بقوله : { إن الله لا * يستحى أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة }

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r21.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r21.claim: When critics demanded further miracles, including a spring from the earth, the Qur’an answered their challenge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r21.anchor: وقالوا لن نؤمن لك حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا

RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r22.speaker: author
