RAZI-FULL:v2p81#2/r22.claim: When critics objected to gradual revelation as grounds for suspicion, God explained that it strengthened the Prophet’s heart.

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r1.claim: The Qur’an answers those who dispute resurrection with many proofs for the resurrection and against its deniers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r1.anchor: الخامس : الذين نازعوا في الحشر والنشر ، والله تعالى أورد على صحة ذلك وعلى إبطال قول المنكرين

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r2.claim: To those who say obligations bring no benefit, God replies that good or evil deeds return to the doer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r2.anchor: إن أحسنتم أحسنتم لأنفسكم وإن أسأتم فلها

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r3.claim: To the claim that determinism invalidates obligation, God replies that He is not questioned about what He does, while people are questioned.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r3.anchor: { لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسئلون } ( الأنبياء : 23 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r4.claim: Rāzī abbreviates these examples because their full treatment appears elsewhere in the book.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r4.anchor: اكتفينا في هذا المقام بهذه الإشارات المختصرة لأن الاستقصاء فيها مذكور

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r5.claim: Since every prophet practiced this discipline, Rāzī concludes that its critic is either an unbeliever or ignorant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r5.anchor: ثبت أن هذه الحرفة هي حرفة كل الأنبياء والرسل علمنا أن الطاعن فيها إما أن يكون كافرا أو جاهلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r6.claim: Rationally, taqlīd cannot justify choosing one authority: following everyone entails following unbelievers, choosing only some has no basis, and rejecting all imitation leaves rational inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r6.anchor: فهو أنه ليس تقليد البعض أولى من تقليد الباقي ، فأما أن يجوز تقليد الكل فيلزمنا تقليد الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r7.claim: Scripture commands calling to God with wisdom and good admonition and debating in the best manner; Rāzī interprets wisdom as proof and demonstration.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r7.anchor: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r8.claim: The commanded debate concerns monotheism and prophethood, not legal branches: such branches are pointless to those rejecting prophecy, while those accepting it would not dispute the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r8.anchor: لا فائدة في الخوض معه في تفاريع الشرع ، ومن أثبت نبوته فإنه لا يخالفه

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r9.claim: Because Muslims are commanded to follow Muhammad and take him as their example, they too must engage in the debate he was commanded to conduct.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r9.anchor: ثم إنا مأمورون باتباعه عليه السلام لقوله : { فاتبعوني يحببكم الله }

RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r10.claim: The Qur’an condemns arguing about God without knowledge, which implies that argument grounded in knowledge is not blameworthy and is praiseworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83/r10.anchor: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم } ( الحج : 3 ، 8 لقمان : 20 ) ذم من يجادل في الله بغير علم

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r1.claim: Qurʾānic commands to examine revelation, creation, the self, and the cosmos establish rational inquiry as part of prophetic religion.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r1.anchor: وثالثها : أن الله تعالى أمر بالنظر فقال

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r2.claim: The Qurʾān praises reflection and insight while condemning heedlessness toward signs and failure to understand; this supports inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r2.anchor: ورابعها : أن الله تعالى ذكر التفكر في معرض المدح فقال

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r3.claim: The Qurʾān condemns imitation of forebears, so inquiry follows the Qurʾān and prophetic religion whereas blind imitation follows the unbelievers.

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r4.claim: A man of Banū Fazāra questioned the Prophet about his wife bearing a dark-skinned son; the Prophet compared it with a differently colored camel in his herd, and the man accepted inherited traits as the cause.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : ( جاء من بني فزارة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r5.claim: The camel exchange is an example of argument by compelling analogy (qiyās) and ilzām.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r5.anchor: واعلم أن هذا هو التمسك بالإلزام والقياس

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r6.claim: In a divine report, God says Adam’s son falsely denies resurrection by claiming he will not be recreated, and insults God by attributing a child to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( قال الله تعالى : كذبني ابن آدم

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r7.claim: The report argues from God’s power to originate creation to His power to resurrect, and from divine oneness to denying embodiment, parenthood, and offspring.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r7.anchor: فانظر كيف احتج الله تعالى في المقام الأول بالقدرة على الابتداء

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r8.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r8.claim: The Prophet said that whoever loves meeting God is loved by God, and whoever dislikes meeting God is disliked by God; ʿĀʾisha asked whether this meant believers’ dislike of death, and he distinguished that from meeting God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r8.anchor: روى عبادة بن الصامت أنه عليه السلام قال : ( من أحب لقاء الله أحب الله لقاءه

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r9.claim: The cited prophetic reports show that reflection and reasoning about proofs are commanded.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r9.anchor: وكل ذلك يدل على أن النظر والفكر في الدلائل مأمور به

RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r10.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r10.claim: Opponents frame five objections to rational inquiry: it yields no knowledge, is not under human control, is impermissible, was not commanded by the Messenger, or is an innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p83#2/r10.anchor: واعلم أن للخصم مقامات . أحدها : أن النظر لا يفيد العلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r1.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r1.claim: The opponent argues that one cannot know an inference-produced belief is knowledge: such meta-knowledge is weaker than immediate certainties, and checking it generates regress.
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r1.anchor: أما المقام الأول : فاحتج الخصم عليه بأمور : أحدها : أنا إذا تفكرنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r2.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r2.claim: People have been certain after reasoning yet later discovered their conclusions were ignorance; therefore an inferred belief cannot be certified as true rather than similarly mistaken.
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r2.anchor: وثانيها : إنا رأينا عالما من الناس قد تفكروا واجتهدوا وحصل لهم عقيب فكرهم اعتقاد

RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r3.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r3.claim: The opponent says a known object cannot be sought because that would acquire what is already acquired, while an unknown object cannot be the target of directed seeking.
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r3.anchor: وثالثها : أن المطلوب إن كان مشعورا به استحال طلبه

RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r4.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r4.claim: Knowing that inference yields knowledge must be either immediate, which rational people do not share, or inferred, which presupposes and attempts to prove itself and leads to regress.
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r4.anchor: ورابعها : أن العلم يكون النظر مفيدا للعلم إما أن يكون ضروريا أو نظريا

RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r5.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r5.claim: The opponent claims that only the two premises together produce a conclusion, but a person cannot attend to both at once, as introspection allegedly shows.
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r5.anchor: وخامسها : أن المقدمة الواحدة لا تنتج بل المنتج مجموع المقدمتين

RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r6.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r6.claim: The opponent says God’s essence cannot be conceived: negative attributes are not His essence and positive attributes describe relations, so neither permits rational affirmation of His essence or qualities.
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r6.anchor: الأول : أن حقيقة الإله غير متصورة وإذا لم تكن الحقيقة متصورة استحال التصديق

RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r7.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r7.claim: Defining God through necessary attributes does not solve the problem: if they are identical with the essence the claim is impossible, and if external, relating them to the unknown essence requires another conception and regress.
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r7.anchor: قلنا هذه الأمور المعلومة إما أن يقال إنها نفس الذات وهو محال

RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r8.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r8.claim: Even the self, the most evident reality, has a disputed essence—body, temperament, bodily parts, or something neither inside nor outside the body—so God should be still less knowable.
RAZI-FULL:v2p84/r8.anchor: الوجه الثاني : أن أظهر الأشياء عندنا ذاتنا وحقيقتنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p86/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p86/r1.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p86/r1.claim: The opponent argues that concepts cannot be acquired: what is already known need not be sought, what is wholly unknown cannot be sought, and basic judgments follow necessarily from their concepts; hence neither basic nor inferential judgments are voluntary.
RAZI-FULL:v2p86/r1.anchor: أما المقام الثاني : وهو أن النظر المفيد للعلم غير مقدور لنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p86/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p86/r2.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p86/r2.claim: An agent could produce knowledge only by distinguishing it from ignorance through its correspondence with what is known, but that requires already knowing the object; thus knowledge cannot be intentionally produced or sought.
RAZI-FULL:v2p86/r2.anchor: وثانيها : أن الإنسان إنما يكون قادرا على إدخال الشيء في الوجود لو كان يمكنه أن يميز ذلك المطلوب

RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r1.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r1.claim: The opponent argues that reason cannot make inquiry obligatory: immediate duties do not require reasoning, while a reasoned duty cannot be known before doing the inquiry and is useless afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r1.anchor: وثالثها : أن الموجب للنظر ، إما ضرورة العقل ، أو النظر أو السمع

RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r2.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r2.claim: Scripture cannot establish the duty to reason either: its authority would itself require prior knowledge of that duty, while inquiry after hearing it would be pointless.
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r2.anchor: والثالث : باطل ، لأنه قبل النظر لا يكون متمكنا من معرفة وجوب النظر

RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r3.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r3.claim: Even if inference yields attainable knowledge, the opponent says God should not command it because reasoning more often leads to ignorance and is therefore an improper risk.
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r3.anchor: المقام الثالث : وهو أن بتقدير كون النظر مفيدا للعلم ومقدورا للمكلف ، لكنه يقبح من الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r4.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r4.claim: Human weakness, distracting doubts, and mutually conflicting schools allegedly show that people cannot rely on reason to distinguish truth from falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r4.anchor: وثانيها : أن الواحد منا مع ما هو عليه من النقص وضعف الخاطر وما يعتريه

RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r5.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r5.claim: If religion rested on proof, each question about a premise would make a person doubt the conclusion and leave the faith, so believers would repeatedly exit religion.
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r5.anchor: وثالثها : أن مدار الدين لو كان على النظر في حقائق الدلائل لوجب أن لا يستقر

RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r6.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r6.claim: A popular saying compares seeking wealth through alchemy, which ends in bankruptcy, with seeking religion through kalām, which ends in heresy; the opponent uses it to oppose opening this field.
RAZI-FULL:v2p86#2/r6.anchor: اشتهر في الألسنة أن من طلب المال بالكيمياء أفلس

RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r1.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r1.claim: Because the Prophet reportedly accepted converts who had not considered detailed proofs, the opponent concludes that such proof is not a condition for valid religion.
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r1.anchor: علمنا أن ذلك غير معتبر في صحة الدين

RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r2.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r2.claim: If proof-based knowledge requires prolonged study and debate, the Prophet would have tested every convert in detail before accepting Islam; widespread reports instead say he accepted people who had never considered such questions.
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r2.anchor: وإن كان الثاني وجب أن لا يحصل ذلك العلم للإنسان ، إلا بعد الممارسة الشديدة

RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r3.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r3.claim: The opponent replies that most rational people know basic proofs, and only detailed objections and answers require advanced study; such detail is not a condition of basic faith.
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r3.anchor: فإن قيل : معرفة أصول الدلائل حاصلة لأكثر العقلاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r4.claim: Rāzī rejects the distinction between basic and advanced proof: a proof either includes all premises needed for certainty or it is incomplete; one uncertain premise makes its conclusion uncertain.
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r4.anchor: قلنا هذا ضعيف لأن الدليل لا يقبل الزيادة والنقصان البتة

RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r5.claim: Saying “Glory be to God” after sudden rain and thunder does not by itself establish demonstrated knowledge: one must prove an event has a cause and exclude planets, nature, and necessary causation as alternatives.
RAZI-FULL:v2p87/r5.anchor: إذا رأى الإنسان حدوث مطر ورعد وبرق بعد أن كان الهواء صافيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r1.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r1.claim: Opponents use Qurʾānic warnings against contentious dispute and engagement in God’s signs to argue that kalām is innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r1.anchor: أما القرآن فقوله تعالى : { ما ضربوه لك إلا جدلا بل هم قوم خصمون }

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r2.claim: Rāzī reads Qurʾān 43:58 as condemning false disputation, reconciling it with the command in 16:125 to argue in the best manner.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r2.anchor: فهو محمول على الجدل بالباطل ، توفيقا بينه وبين قوله : { وجادلهم بالتى هى أحسن }

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r3.claim: Rāzī says the “indulgence” prohibited in 6:68 is obstinate wrangling, not careful inquiry into the verses.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r3.anchor: فجوابه أن الخوض ليس هو النظر ، بل الخوض في الشيء هو اللجاح

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r4.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r4.claim: Opponents cite the prophetic saying, “Reflect on creation, not on the Creator,” against rational inquiry into God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r4.anchor: وأما الخبر فقوله عليه السلام : ( تفكروا في الخلق ولا تفكروا في الخالق )

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r5.claim: Rāzī answers that the instruction to reflect on the Creator is intended to yield knowledge of the Creator, which is precisely the inquiry sought.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r5.anchor: فذاك إنما أمر به ليستفاد منه معرفة الخالق وهو المطلوب

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r6.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r6.claim: Opponents cite the saying “Adhere to the religion of old women” as a warning against kalām.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r6.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام : ( عليكم بدين العجائز )

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r7.claim: Rāzī interprets “the religion of old women” as entrusting affairs to God and relying on Him, not as forbidding proof-based inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r7.anchor: فليس المراد ، إلا تفويض الأمور كلها إلى الله تعالى والاعتماد في كل الأمور على الله

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r8.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r8.claim: Opponents cite the prophetic instruction to stop when divine predestination is mentioned; Rāzī calls this report weak as a proof of a general ban.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r8.anchor: وأما قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إذا ذكر القدر فأمسكوا ) فضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r9.claim: Even if a specific topic is prohibited, Rāzī says a limited prohibition does not establish a universal prohibition of rational inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r9.anchor: لأن النهي الجزئي لا يفيد النهي الكلي

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r10.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r10.claim: The opponents argue that the Companions did not teach kalām, so it is an innovation and forbidden; they say the Companions refrained from such disputation and condemned it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r10.anchor: أما الإجماع فهو أن هذا علم لم تتكلم فيه الصحابة فيكون بدعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r11.claim: If the claim is only that Companions did not use theologians’ terminology, Rāzī accepts it but says that does not discredit kalām, just as their not using jurists’ terminology does not discredit jurisprudence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r11.anchor: إن عنيتم أن الصحابة لم يستعملوا ألفاظ المتكلمين فمسلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r12.claim: If the opponents mean the Companions did not know God and His Messenger through evidence, Rāzī rejects that claim outright.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r12.anchor: وإن عنيتم أنهم ما عرفوا الله تعالى ورسوله بالدليل ، فبئس ما قلتم

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r13.speaker: مالك بن أنس
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r13.claim: Mālik warns against innovations and defines innovators as people who discuss God’s names, attributes, and speech instead of remaining silent where the Companions and Successors were silent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r13.anchor: قال مالك بن أنس : إياكم والبدع قيل وما البدع يا أبا عبد الله ؟ قال أهل البدع الذين يتكلمون

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r14.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r14.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna answers a question about kalām by instructing people to follow the Sunnah and leave innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r14.anchor: وسئل سفيان بن عيينة عن الكلام فقال اتبع السنة ودع البدعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r15.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r15.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says suffering any sin short of associating partners with God is better than meeting God with kalām, and adds that kalām books are excluded from a bequest of scholarly books.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r15.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : لأن يبتلي الله العبد بكل ذنب سوى الشرك خير له

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r16.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r16.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī reportedly says that kalām books are not included when a person bequeaths his scholarly books.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r16.anchor: لو أوصى رجل بكتبه العلمية لآخر وكان فيها كتب الكلام لم تدخل تلك الكتب في الوصية

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r17.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r17.claim: Opponents cite the customary ruling that a bequest to scholars does not include a theologian.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r17.anchor: وأما الحكم فهو أنه لو أوصى للعلماء لا يدخل المتكلم فيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r18.claim: Rāzī answers that early Muslims’ condemnations of kalām concern innovators, not all rational theology.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r18.anchor: وأما تشديد السلف على الكلام فهو محمول على أهل البدعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r19.claim: Rāzī says bequests are interpreted by custom; excluding theologians from one customary class does not establish that they lack knowledge, just as a bequest for those who know God, His attributes and acts, and His messengers would exclude a jurist.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r19.anchor: ولأن مبنى الوصايا على العرف فهذا إتمام هذه المسألة

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r20.claim: The opponents’ proofs that reasoning cannot yield knowledge are themselves theoretical, so using some forms of reasoning to disprove all reasoning is contradictory.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r20.anchor: أما الشبه التي تمسكوا بها في أن النظر لا يفيد العلم فهي فاسدة

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r21.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r21.claim: The opponents’ claim that reasoning is not under human control is refuted by their voluntary construction of the very objections they offer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r21.anchor: وأما الشبه التي تمسكوا بها في أن النظر غير مقدور فهي فاسدة

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r22.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r22.claim: Calling reliance on reasoning improper is self-contradictory, since presenting their own objections would be improper by the same standard.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r22.anchor: وأما الشبه التي تمسكوا بها في أن التعاويل على النظر قبيح فهي متناقضة

RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r23.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r23.claim: Rāzī says all the prophets commanded inquiry and proof, so the claim that the Messenger did not command it is false.
RAZI-FULL:v2p88/r23.anchor: لأنا بينا أن الأنبياء بأسرهم ما جاءوا إلا بالأمر بالنظر والاستدلال

RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r1.claim: Rāzī says he explained the reality of worship when discussing “You alone we worship.”
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r1.anchor: أما حقيقة العبادة فذكرناها في قوله : { إياك نعبد }

RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī, as cited by al-Azharī, defines creation as measuring and proportioning; Qurʾānic usage and Arabic examples support this sense.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r2.anchor: حكى الأزهري صاحب ( التهذيب ) عن ابن الأنباري أنه التقدير والتسوية

RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r3.claim: The verbs for creating in 23:14, 29:17, and 5:110 can mean measuring or shaping; Zuhayr’s line about doing what one fashions likewise witnesses this sense.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r3.anchor: ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبعض القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r4.claim: Arabic expressions for making a shoe, implausible tales, a share of good, worthiness, smooth stone, and worn cloth all connect خلق with forming, proportion, or evenness.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r4.anchor: يقال خلق النعل إذا قدرها وسواها بالقياس

RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r5.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r5.claim: ʿAbd al-Jabbār says خلق means measuring and language allows humans to be called creators, as 23:14 and 5:110 show; God is distinguished because He acts with knowledge of outcomes and interests.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r5.anchor: قال القاضي عبد الجبار : الخلق فعل بمعنى التقدير واللغة لا تقتضي

RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله البصري
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r6.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Baṣrī says calling God a creator is impossible if creation means measuring, since measuring entails thought, reasoning, and calculation, which cannot apply to God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r6.anchor: وقال أستاذه أبو عبد الله البصري إطلاق اسم خالق على الله محال

RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r7.speaker: جمهور أهل السنة والجماعة
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r7.claim: The majority of Sunnis define creation as bringing into existence and initiating; Muslims’ statement that no creator exists except God supports this definition over mere measuring.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89/r7.anchor: وقال جمهور أهل السنة والجماعة : الخلق عبارة عن الإيجاد والإنشاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r1.claim: Since the command to worship presupposes knowing that God exists, and that knowledge is inferential rather than immediate, Rāzī reads the passage as supplying proofs of God’s existence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r1.anchor: الأمر بعبادته موقوف على معرفة وجوده ، ولما لم يكن العلم بوجوده ضروريا

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r2.claim: Rāzī classifies six routes to proving God: possibility, origination, or both, each argued from substances or from accidents.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r2.anchor: فيكون مجموع الطرق الدالة على وجوده سبحانه وتعالى ستة لا مزيد عليها

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r3.claim: The possibility of created essences points to God through human dependence, Abraham’s disavowal of enemies except the Lord of the worlds, and the final return to the Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r3.anchor: أحدها : الاستدلال بإمكان الذوات ، وإليه الإشارة بقوله تعالى : { والله الغنى وأنتم الفقراء }

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r5.claim: Abraham’s rejection of setting bodies as gods illustrates inference from the origination of bodies.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r5.anchor: وثالثها : الاستدلال بحدوث الأجسام . وإليه الإشارة بقول إبراهيم عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r6.claim: The nearest proof for ordinary understanding is the origination of accidents, approached through evidence from human selves and the external world; scripture chiefly uses these two kinds of sign.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r6.anchor: ورابعها : الاستدلال بحدوث الأعراض ، وهذه الطريقة أقرب الطرق إلى أفهام الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r7.claim: Each person knows they once did not exist and now exist; whatever begins after nonexistence needs an originator, and neither oneself, one’s parents, nor other humans can construct such a body.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r7.anchor: أما دلائل الأنفس ، فهي أن كل أحد يعلم بالضرورة

RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r8.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r8.claim: A possible objection is that seasonal natures, the celestial spheres, or stars could be the effective cause of human origination.
RAZI-FULL:v2p89#2/r8.anchor: إلا أن لقائل أن يقول ههنا : لم لا يجوز أن يكون المؤثر طبائع الفصول

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r1.claim: Bodies cannot account for their own differing attributes: the cause must be distinct; if bodily the question recurs, while a nonbodily cause must be a capable agent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r1.anchor: فلا بد وأن يكون قادرا ، فثبت بهذه الدلالة افتقار جميع الأجسام إلى مؤثر قادر ليس بجسم

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r2.claim: An argument from the origination of accidents proves a maker only when supplemented by the possibility of accidents and attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r2.anchor: الاستدلال بحدوث الأعراض على وجود الصانع لا يكفي إلا بعد الاستعانة بإمكان الأعراض والصفات

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r5.speaker: جعفر الصادق رضي الله عنه
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r5.claim: Jaʿfar asks an atheist rescued from a shipwreck whom he hoped in after ship, sailors, and plank failed; the man recognizes the Creator and converts.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r5.anchor: يروى أن بعض الزنادقة أنكر الصانع عند جعفر الصادق رضي الله عنه . فقال جعفر : هل ركبت البحر ؟

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r6.claim: A report in Kitāb Diyānāt al-ʿArab says the Prophet asks ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn which of his ten gods relieves distress; he answers Allah, and the Prophet declares there is no god but Allah.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r6.anchor: جاء في ( كتاب ديانات العرب ) أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لعمران بن حصين ( كم لك من إله )

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة رحمه الله
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa silences attackers from the materialists with the analogy of a loaded ship navigating rough seas without a sailor or guide, comparing it to the ordered world.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r7.anchor: وثالثها : كان أبو حنيفة رحمه الله سيفا على الدهرية

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r8.speaker: الشافعي رضي الله عنه
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r8.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī points to one mulberry leaf yielding silk, honey, dung, or musk in different creatures; the report says seventeen listeners converted.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r8.anchor: ورابعها : سألوا الشافعي رضي الله عنه ما الدليل على وجود الصانع ؟

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r9.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues for a Creator from parents' wishes being reversed: a father wanting a son may have a daughter, and vice versa.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r9.anchor: سئل أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه مرة أخرى فتمسك بأن الوالد يريد الذكر فيكون أنثى

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r10.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله عنه
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r10.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal compares the egg to a sealed smooth fortress; a hearing, seeing chick emerges, which requires an agent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r10.anchor: تمسك أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله عنه بقلعة حصينة ملساء لا فرجة فيها

RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r11.speaker: مالك
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r11.claim: When Hārūn al-Rashīd asks Mālik for proof of the Creator, Mālik cites the variety of voices, recurring melodies, and differing languages.
RAZI-FULL:v2p90/r11.anchor: سأل هرون الرشيد مالكا عن ذلك فاستدل باختلاف الأصوات وتردد النغمات وتفاوت اللغات

RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r5.claim: People's innate recognition of God appears when asked who created them and when they see divine punishment; the cited verses say they acknowledge God alone.
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r5.anchor: حادي عشرها : حكم البديهية في قوله : { ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله } ( الزخرف : 87 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī says creation is the reason worship is due: after commanding worship, God states the ground on which it is incumbent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r6.anchor: المسألة الرابعة : قال القاضي : الفائدة في قوله : { الذى خلقكم } أن العبادة لا تستحق إلا بذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r7.claim: Knowledge that God created earlier generations is reached by the same means as knowledge that He created the present audience.
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r7.anchor: ولكن علمهم بأن الله تعالى خلقهم كعلمهم بأنه تعالى خلق من قبلهم لأن طريقة العلم بذلك واحدة .

RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r8.claim: Ancestors are the audience's roots, so their creation was a prior blessing to descendants even thousands of years before the descendants existed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p91/r8.anchor: أن من قبلهم كالأصول لهم ، وخلق الأصول يجري مجرى الأنعام على الفروع

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r1.claim: Laʿalla ordinarily conveys hope or apprehension, as in the cited Qurʾanic examples, but these senses seem to imply uncertainty about the outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r1.anchor: أن كلمة لعل للترجي والإشفاق ، تقول لعل زيدا يكرمني وقال تعالى : { لعله يتذكر أو يخشى } ( طه : 44 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r2.claim: Since God cannot be ignorant of outcomes, expressions of hope or apprehension in divine speech require interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r2.anchor: والترجي والإشفاق لا يحصلان إلا عند الجهل بالعاقبة وذلك على الله تعالى محال

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r3.claim: One reading makes the hope belong to the human addressees, as in the command to Moses and Aaron to go hoping Pharaoh may remember or fear.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r3.anchor: أن معنى ( لعل ) راجع إلى العباد لا إلى الله تعالى فقوله : { لعله يتذكر أو يخشى } أي اذهبا أنتما على رجائكما وطمعكما في إيمانه

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r4.claim: A second explanation compares God's use of laʿalla to rulers' conventionally modest wording for commitments that they intend to fulfill with certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r4.anchor: من عادة الملوك والعظماء أن يقتصروا في مواعيدهم التي يوطنون أنفسهم على إنجازها

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r5.claim: Al-Kashshāf rejects laʿalla as simply meaning kay (so that); because God's promise is certain, His inducement of hope functions like an assured promise and can yield that paraphrase.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r5.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ولعل لا يكون بمعنى كي ، ولكن كلمة لعل للأطماع ، والكريم الرحيم إذا أطمع

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r6.claim: God gave people capacity for good and evil, guiding intellects, and removed excuses; another agent doing this would expect the intended result.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r6.anchor: لما أعطاهم القدرة على الخير والشر وخلق لهم العقول الهادية وأزاح أعذارهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl derives laʿalla from repetition and emphasis; on this account, urging an act with laʿalla means that doing it reinforces the demand and strengthens the person toward it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r7.anchor: قال القفال : لعل مأخوذ من تكرر الشيء كقولهم عللا بعد نهل ، واللام فيها هي لام التأكيد كاللام التي تدخل في لقد

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r8.claim: A questioner objects that if worship is itself taqwa, commanding worship so that people attain taqwa is tautological.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r8.anchor: إذا كانت العبادة تقوى فقوله : { اعبدوا ربكم لعلكم تتقون } جار مجرى قوله : اعبدوا ربكم لعلكم تعبدون

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r9.claim: Worship is the act that produces taqwa, while taqwa is avoiding harm; calling the act taqwa itself is figurative, transferring the name from result to means.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r9.anchor: بل العبادة فعل يحصل به التقوى ، لأن الاتقاء هو الاحتراز عن المضار ، والعبادة فعل المأمور به

RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r10.claim: A second answer connects the command with God's purpose in creating accountable beings: that they worship and obey, as stated in 51:56; al-Rāzī says this reading suits Muʿtazilī principles.
RAZI-FULL:v2p92/r10.anchor: أنه تعالى إنما خلق المكلفين لكي يتقوا ويطيعوا على ما قال : { وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون } ( الذاريات : 56 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads khalaqakum with assimilation (idghām).

RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r2.speaker: أبو السميفع
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r2.claim: Abū al-Sumayfa reads wa-khalaqa min qablikum.
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو السميفع : وخلق من قبلكم

RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r3.speaker: زيد بن علي
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r3.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī is reported to read wa-alladhīna min qablikum.
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r3.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي : والذين من قبلكم

RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains the second relative expression as emphatically inserted between the first relative and its clause, paralleling Jarīr's doubled Taym in his verse.
RAZI-FULL:v2p93/r4.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الوجه فيه أنه أفحم الموصول الثاني بين الأول وصلته تأكيدا كما أقحم جرير في قوله

BURHAN:v2p88/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p88/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
BURHAN:v2p88/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites interpret Qur’anic “perhaps you will” expressions as God’s willing the outcome, since they hold that God wills only good and evil occurs contrary to His will.
BURHAN:v2p88/r4.anchor: فالمعتزلة يفسرونه بالإرادة لأن عندهم أنه تعالى لا يريد إلا الخير ووقوع الشر على خلاف إرادته

BURHAN:v2p88/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p88/r5.speaker: أهل السنة
BURHAN:v2p88/r5.claim: Sunnis read “perhaps you will” as a demand, not a divine will: hope carries the sense of request, while nothing in existence can occur against God’s will.
BURHAN:v2p88/r5.anchor: وأهل السنة يفسرونه بالطلب لما في الترجي من معنى الطلب والطلب غير الإرادة على ما تقرر في الأصول
